Pick a census year from 1841 to 1911, a county by Chapman code and a surname and optional first name, and the results come back as a list that opens to the whole household, with relationship, marital status, age, occupation and birthplace for each member and the piece, enumeration district, folio, page and schedule. That makes it the free way to see a household and a lodger beside a head, which an index to one person cannot. COVERAGE IS PER COUNTY AND PER YEAR AND UNEVEN. For Hertfordshire the 1851 census was found (the Baldock district, Weston among its parishes); searches of Hertfordshire for 1841 and for 1861 returned nothing, which is not a finding that the records do not exist. A control surname at the same county and year should be run before a nil result is quoted. Birthplace is the parish as the enumerator heard it, and ages are often a year or two out against a baptism.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Luwinski archive. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Hertfordshire Names Online — Hertfordshire Archives and Local Studies
providers.what: A free, account-free name index to the Hertfordshire archive's holdings: marriages and marriage licences (1538 to 1925), wills (1413 to 1857, from the archdeaconries of Huntingdon (Hitchin Division) and St Albans), the poor (1623 to 1915), apprentices, crime and punishment, non-conformist registers, newspapers and tithe records. One search by exact surname, an optional keyword (a parish name works) and a year range returns a count per index, and each opens to a table. It gives what is INDEXED and not the document: a will or a licence bond is a reference number, and a copy is £11.45 an item, viewable free at Hertfordshire Archives. It is the second index to cross-check a FreeREG marriage, and it is where a yeoman's will before 1858 turns up, which a register will not show. Spell the surname both ways; the licence in the example was indexed under Phillips and the register entry under Philips.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Luwinski archive. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Macoupin County ILGenWeb — cemetery burial listings
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions of burials in Macoupin County, Illinois cemeteries, one page per letter-range (Calvary, Mt. Olive: calvarya.html, calvaryc.html … calvaryt.html), each row linking to a photograph of the stone. Free, no account. Read 17 October 2026 for the Calvary Catholic cemetery at Mount Olive: the R–S page lists thirteen Spudic/Spudick burials with birth and death years and photographs. It is a transcription by volunteers, not a register: the years come from the stones, not from a death record, and the page does not say how complete the cemetery coverage is.
providers.triageNote: Added from the Spudic/Polovich family page (External-Family-Work/spudic-polovich). Licence not stated on the pages read.

providers.name: UK Genealogy Archives
providers.what: A family-run British site, online since 1998 and free to view, that hosts its own searchable transcripts rather than pointing elsewhere. What its collections page lists as searchable: the England & Wales censuses of 1841, 1851, 1861, 1871, 1881, 1891, 1901 and 1911; marriage registers for Anglesey, Berkshire, Brecknock, Devon, Dorset, Durham, Gloucestershire, Hampshire, Leicestershire, Middlesex, Norfolk, Northumberland, Shropshire, Surrey and Wiltshire; baptism and burial registers for Devon, Dorset, Durham and Northumberland; the Phillimore marriage volumes (over 600 parishes and about 248,000 marriages, the site says) and a set of parish registers (over 40, with free images of the original pages where it has them); an England & Wales marriages 1538–1921 transcript; the First World War medals and awards; the 1873 Return of Owners of Land; the Samuel Lewis topographical dictionaries; trade directories and gazetteers; Who Was Who 1897–1916; school, college and university registers; and the peerage and pedigree books: Burke's Peerage and Landed Gentry, Debrett's, Dod's 1841 and the Heralds' Visitations. WHAT IT IS NOT: mostly transcripts, so the ordinary experience is an index with no image; only the parish-register collection says it carries page images. The county series cover parishes the site chose and carry the date ranges it states (some run 1538 to 1837, some to 1920 or 1950), so a name missing from one is not shown absent from the parish. The site also has sections for Scotland, Ireland, Wales, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands, but the searchable collections above are almost all England and Wales. Every figure here is the site's own statement from its home and collections pages; none has been measured against a known entry. Pages carry advertising and affiliate links to commercial genealogy services, which it discloses in a banner.
providers.triageNote: Added 2 November 2026 at David's request, from the site's own home page and collections list (https://ukga.org/browse.php), read in the browser. The server answered an automated fetch of /search.php with HTTP 429, which was left alone; nothing here comes from a search. Not yet measured: run a control surname in a parish the site lists before quoting any nil from it.

providers.name: Javna ustanova Spomen-područje Jasenovac — poimenični popis žrtava KL Jasenovac 1941.–1945.
providers.what: The Jasenovac Memorial Site's own name-by-name list of victims of the Jasenovac camp complex, 1941–1945, searchable on its website (page «Pregled i pretraga poimeničnog popisa žrtava KL Jasenovac 1941.-1945.»). Search fields: surname, first name, municipality of birth, place of birth, year of birth and camp (Jasenovac, Stara Gradiška); each result shows father's first name, birth year, municipality and place of birth, nationality, manner of death, who caused it, year and place of death, camp and execution site. The page states no login. A separate form on the site requests a printout of the data. It is the Memorial Site's list, not the Belgrade Museum of Genocide Victims' register (see muzej-genocida): the two are compiled separately and are best searched both. The institution's annual reports give 83,747 names in 2016 and say the list is still being added to; the page itself states no total. Read from the site on 2026-11-04; what an ordinary visitor pays and how the list is paged was not checked. Interface in Croatian.
providers.triageNote: Home page and victim-list search page read on 2026-11-04. Wikidata Q16087601 is the item labelled «Jasenovac Memorial Site»; whether it is the institution or the site was not checked. Access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Holocaust Survivors and Victims Names Database — United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
providers.what: The US Holocaust Memorial Museum's names database: a name record for each person who appears in a document in its collections, its Survivors' Registry and records from other organisations (census records, registration forms, ghetto and camp lists, death lists). Covers Jews, Roma and Sinti, Poles and other Slavic peoples, Soviet prisoners of war and political prisoners. Two searches: Names (last and first name, each Exact with wildcards, Fuzzy, or D-M Soundex for Eastern European and Yiddish variants) and Lists and Sources (title, author, year, place, provenance, keywords). The page says some resources are not online and that the full database can be used in the Museum's reading room. Its record total and whether an account is needed were not stated on the page. Read on 2026-11-04.
providers.triageNote: Database page read on 2026-11-04. Access class and record count still need a person.

providers.name: Archives of the Auschwitz-Birkenau State Museum
providers.what: Original camp records of Auschwitz, spring 1940 to January 1945: records of the six camp chancellery departments (commandant's orders, prisoner personal files, death certificates, daily prisoner count books, camp hospital record books), censored prisoner letters and postcards, SS Hygiene Institute and Central Construction Board records, resistance materials including illegally compiled lists of deceased women prisoners, and trial records (mostly copies). Also copies of transport lists of Jews deported from Drancy, Westerbork, Theresienstadt and Berlin, mostly copies of prisoner transfer lists for other camps (original Mauthausen prisoner file cards are held), records of about a dozen sub-camps (fullest for Jawischowitz and Janinagrube), the postwar Bellert hospital book and lists of liberated prisoners by nationality. For Soviet prisoners of war: 7,646 camp record sheets (scanned, with a 1990s database of 7,646 personal records) and a 470-page book of deceased Soviet POWs (database of 8,333 personal records; documents at least 8,320 deaths from 7 October 1941 to 28 February 1942). Does not hold a full set of Jewish deportee registrations. The collection page describes no online search tool and no request procedure; its Contact page is linked but the office for archive requests is not named.
providers.triageNote: Collection overview and the Soviet POW data page were read. No search form or request route was seen; a person must find out from the Museum how to ask for a named prisoner, and whether the 'Central Register of Prisoners' database is public.

providers.name: USHMM - Primary Source Databases (list of electronic resources)
providers.what: A curated list of 39 databases and archives about the Holocaust and Nazi-era persecution, grouped as Camps, First-Person Accounts, Life Under the Nazi Regime, Propaganda, Refugees, Resistance, United States, War Crime Trials and Additional Resources. Name-bearing entries include Arolsen Archives, Kazerne Dossin deportation lists and victim photographs, the Fortunoff and USC Shoah Foundation testimony archives, JDC Archives, DigiBaeck (Leo Baeck Institute), a Nuremberg-laws index of Jews stripped of German nationality, 'The Jewish Question: Documents from the BDC' (Gale), Shanghai Municipal Police files on individual Jewish refugees (Gale) and the Dachau trials records (Gale). Most entries are intended for use inside the Museum; only some are marked as available to researchers outside it, and most carry no access note. It is a pointer list, not a name search.
providers.triageNote: The full list was read. Many items are Gale or Adam Matthew subscription products hosted for Museum visitors; what a home user pays or needs was not seen. Useful as a map of further sources.

providers.name: Gedenkbuch - Opfer der Verfolgung der Juden unter der nationalsozialistischen Gewaltherrschaft in Deutschland 1933-1945 (Bundesarchiv)
providers.what: Searchable memorial database of Jewish victims of persecution in Germany 1933-1945, run by the Bundesarchiv. A single name field (first name, surname or birth name; terms combined with AND; case and accent insensitive; * and ? wildcards) or an advanced search by places (birth, residence, deportation) and dates (birth, deportation, emigration). Results are 10 per page, sorted alphabetically by surname and exportable as CSV. German with an English interface. Lists victims of the persecution of Jews in the German territory of 1933-1945 only; does not claim to cover non-Jewish victims. The page does not say whether it is free of charge or how many names it holds.
providers.triageNote: Search page was read. Entry counts and cost are not stated. The Atlas already has a 'bundesarchiv' row for the main site; this is the separate apps.bundesarchiv.de service.

providers.name: Digitaal Joods Monument (Jewish Cultural Quarter)
providers.what: Online monument with an individual page for each Dutch Jew, Roma or Sinto (and those who fled to the Netherlands) who was persecuted and did not survive the Holocaust; described as covering more than 109,000 people. A name is added when the death is certain. Maintained by the Jewish Cultural Quarter, Amsterdam; English and Dutch versions; a search page and a login/sign-up option exist, and visitors can contribute (User contributions). Related sources it describes: the 'In Memoriam' book of 101,414 Jews deported from the Netherlands with no known grave, and the National Database of Victims of Persecution (NDVS), run by the Jewish Museum and the Westerbork Camp Memorial Center. The pages read do not say what a free visit includes or what the login adds.
providers.triageNote: Home page and a search-engine summary of its about/FAQ pages were read; the about and FAQ pages themselves returned only navigation. Per-person fields and costs still need a person to check.

providers.name: Oorlogsgravenstichting (Dutch War Graves Foundation)
providers.what: Dutch foundation, active since 1946, that has registered about 180,000 people in the Netherlands as war victims (including those who died in the Second World War and in later conflicts) and maintains about 50,000 Dutch war graves worldwide. Collects and shares victims' life stories. The site has a search box for a person, location or story and a separate exact-search page. The home page read is in Dutch; no English version was seen.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Search fields and what a person record shows were not seen; whether it includes camp deaths of Dutch victims abroad needs a person to test.

providers.name: Dokumentationsarchiv des oesterreichischen Widerstandes (DOeW) - Opfersuche
providers.what: Austrian resistance and persecution research archive (research archive, library, photo archive) with an online victim search covering Austrian Shoah victims, Spiegelgrund victims, deaths from political persecution 1938-1945, and men and women registered by the Gestapo Wien (some of whom survived). The site states a total of 78,743 entries and says the databases are a work in progress. Basic search by first and last name (umlauts and the eszett match alternative spellings); extended search by residence, birth date, birthplace with a phonetic option; wildcards * and ?. Does not claim to list every Austrian victim.
providers.triageNote: Home page and search help text read. Direct URL of the search form was not captured, so deepLink is null. Cost not stated.

providers.name: KZ-Gedenkstaette Dachau - Archive, Digital Memorial Book and prisoner information requests
providers.what: Memorial site archive with a Digital Memorial Book, 'The Victims of the Dachau Concentration Camp 1933-1945' (people who died in Dachau, its satellite camps and on the death marches, to 31 July 1945; the memorial estimates about 41,500 murdered, many nameless, and the book does not include those who died in other camps or on transports between them). Linked at gedenkbuch.kz-gedenkstaette-dachau.de/en. Information on individual prisoners is requested through an online form that asks for the requester's relationship to the person and any known birth data; the form gives no response time, fee or eligibility rule. Also lists an audio and video archive and a library.
providers.triageNote: Research menu, Digital Memorial Book page and request form were read; the Memorial Book search itself was not opened.

providers.name: Buchenwald Memorial - Online Books of the Dead
providers.what: Two online books of the dead for research on people who died at Buchenwald: a book for the concentration camp 1937-1945 (more than 56,000 dead; excludes people deported from Buchenwald who died in other camps) at totenbuch.buchenwald.de, and a database of more than 7,000 names for Soviet Special Camp No. 2 (1945-1950), based on the camp's death registers and camp journal, at totenbuch-speziallager.buchenwald.de/recherche/. The memorial site also lists an online photo archive, collections and a library. The page gives no search fields; the English site names no general archive-request route other than a contacts page.
providers.triageNote: Online Books of the Dead page was read; the book sites themselves were not opened. Contact emails for each book are on the page.

providers.name: Mauthausen Memorial - Collections database, Memorial Book and person searches
providers.what: Memorial's person-search guidance recommends starting with the Arolsen Archives online database, then sending a research request by web form with as much information as possible on the person (open to relatives, people asking about a specific person, and researchers on SS personnel). A central collections database at collections.mauthausen-memorial.org (documents, photographs, oral history, artefacts, library) is online without registration since January 2026; the page does not say whether it can be searched by name. For people who died at Mauthausen and its satellite camps, an online Memorial Book for the Dead is at raumdernamen.mauthausen-memorial.org. A page of fees for use of the collections exists; the amounts were not seen.
providers.triageNote: Searching-for-persons and collection-databases pages read. Fees, and whether the collections database searches names, are not stated.

providers.name: Stutthof Museum in Sztutowo - Archives and searching for former prisoners
providers.what: Museum archive that issues official certificates of a person's stay in the camp, to former prisoners, their families, and Polish and foreign institutions. Records are only partly preserved; the museum has identified about 75% of prisoners by name. An online search covers only a fragment of the list (fields: surname, first name, camp number, date and place of birth, place of residence, occupation); scans exist only for record-book documents with reference numbers starting I-IIE-. A request uses an 'Investigation card' PDF sent to poszukiwania@stutthof.org or by post, giving the person's name, surname and date of birth. The museum sent 36,767 names of Polish prisoners to the straty.pl victims database.
providers.triageNote: Search-for-prisoners page read. The online search form was not opened; fee for certificates not stated.

providers.name: KZ-Gedenkstaette Neuengamme - Archive and Death Register 1940-1945
providers.what: Archive of the Neuengamme concentration camp and its satellite camps, also resistance and persecution in Northern Germany and Hamburg under the Nazis. Holds documents, photographs, plans, drawings, audio and visual media and objects, including death registers and infirmary laboratory records hidden by prisoners in April 1945, personal documents, survivor testimonies and interviews. Answers relatives' requests about a prisoner's fate through an online archive request form, compiling information from several archives into a person-related database. An online Death Register 1940-1945 is listed. Use of the collection needs a written request explaining the research project and an appointment (Monday to Friday, 9-17). Does not offer open walk-in access to the collection.
providers.triageNote: Archive page read. The death register page itself was only seen in a search listing, not opened; its search fields and counts are unverified.

providers.name: Terezin Initiative Institute - holocaust.cz (victims and documents databases)
providers.what: Czech Holocaust documentation site of the Terezin Initiative Institute, in Czech, English and German. Its home page links a victims database (entries with birth date, places such as Terezin, Treblinka or Auschwitz, and a status of died), a document database of scans such as passport applications, identity-card applications and inquiries about a person, a Terezin ghetto section, a section on the persecution and genocide of Roma and Sinti in the Czech lands, and survivor testimonies. The home page text states no counts and no search instructions.
providers.triageNote: Home page only; the victims and document database URLs were not captured, so deepLink is null. A person should confirm search fields and counts.

providers.name: IPN - Straty osobowe i ofiary represji pod okupacja niemiecka 1939-1945 (straty.pl)
providers.what: Institute of National Remembrance documentation programme building a named list of citizens of the Second Polish Republic who were repressed or killed under German occupation: soldiers, prisoners of war, prisoners of camps and prisons, and Holocaust victims. Entries carry personal data, the type, cause and circumstances of repression, the source and descriptive notes such as biographies. Search by person name or by place and type of repression; a questionnaire lets relatives report information. States 5,565,892 victims and repressed persons in total, 5,059,663 known by name and 506,229 anonymous. Polish-language page; whether other languages and any cost exist is not stated.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; it does not name straty.pl but the domain was fetched directly and the Stutthof museum links to it. Counts are the page's own figures and cover the whole programme, not only Jewish victims.

providers.name: OBD Memorial - united databank of Soviet war losses (Russian Ministry of Defence)
providers.what: United databank on defenders of the Fatherland reported dead or missing in the Great Patriotic War and afterwards: records of persons, burials and documents on irrecoverable losses. Source areas include reports on irrecoverable losses, hospital and medical battalion documents, casualty updates, burial name lists, prisoner-of-war documents, de-listing orders, card indices, and digital and printed Memory Books. Fields searched include surname, first name, patronymic, year and place of birth, rank, last place of service. Quick Search is Russian only; Advanced Search adds source choice and extra areas for authorised users; a tab finds soldiers by reconsignment points when the unit is unknown. Not the same organisation as the human-rights group Memorial. Soviet POW material includes records that matter for POWs held in German camps.
providers.triageNote: The English help page was read; the main info page returned an error to the fetcher and the search interface was not opened. A person should test it, and confirm whether an account is needed beyond 'authorised users'.

providers.name: Mosaic of Victims - Hungarian Roma in the Second World War (National Archives of Hungary)
providers.what: Online resource of the National Archives of Hungary, made under an IHRA grant, with three databases of Roma victims: Roma deported from Hungary in 1944-1945 to Dachau, Buchenwald, Bergen-Belsen, Mauthausen, Natzweiler, Ravensbruck and subcamps (1,470 deported persons as of February 2023, with more still being identified); Hungarian Roma soldiers and civilian victims 1939-1945; and victims of ten mass executions between September 1944 and March 1945. Identifications relied on surnames, mothers' surnames, traditional Roma occupations and places of residence assessed case by case, and the page warns that not every person labelled Roma in camp records was Roma. The databases are hosted on the Archives' online portal; no search instructions were given on the page read.
providers.triageNote: Page read. The portal and search form were not opened; no count for the soldiers and civilians database.

providers.name: Kazerne Dossin - Memorial, Museum and Documentation Centre on Holocaust and Human Rights
providers.what: Belgian memorial at the former Dossin barracks, from which 25,490 Jews and 353 Roma were deported on 28 transports between 1942 and 1944, mostly to Auschwitz-Birkenau. The home page offers an online archive and a reading room for research and for questions about a family member's experience, and a contact page. An image bank at beeldbank.kazernedossin.eu is described by the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum as holding original documents on the Holocaust in Belgium (official records, personal documents, memoirs, oral histories), with deportation lists and victim photographs openly accessible and other collections needing a visit and registration for unaffiliated researchers. The image bank site itself loaded only a 'Loading Application' screen.
providers.triageNote: Main site read; the image bank description is second-hand from USHMM's list and its own page did not render. Needs a person to confirm what is searchable by name.

providers.name: Fortunoff Video Archive for Holocaust Testimonies (Yale University Library)
providers.what: Archive of over 4,400 testimonies of Holocaust survivors, witnesses and liberators. Searchable remotely through the Aviary platform (instructions on registering in Aviary are on the archive's site), with a Visual Search tool and a Publication Database of texts that cite testimony. Also available at access sites worldwide (generally universities, museums and memorials). Quoting testimony in publications needs permission; using video or audio excerpts in films or podcasts needs a licence. The page does not state what an individual Aviary account costs or who is eligible.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Interview-level search by name or place was not tried.

providers.name: DigiBaeck - Leo Baeck Institute digital collections
providers.what: Digital collections of the Leo Baeck Institute documenting German-speaking Jewry in the modern era: personal documents, correspondence, family and community histories, genealogical materials and business records; about 5,000 memoirs and manuscripts; over 5,000 art items and objects; over 25,000 photographs; over 1,600 rare books and over 200 periodicals fully online; interviews including over 1,000 Austrian Heritage Collection interviews and oral histories with 253 German-Jewish refugees. Searched by a keyword box or browse links; only digitised items are returned. The site is available in English and German. The page does not state whether access is free or whether a surname search of family collections is supported.
providers.triageNote: Landing page read. Not a 1941-45 source as such; useful for emigre families from Germany, Austria and Bohemia.

providers.name: ICRC Archives - Central Agency tracing files, Second World War
providers.what: The International Committee of the Red Cross holds data on individuals collected by it and its tracing agencies in conflicts since 1870, to restore family links and protect prisoners of war, civilian internees and war victims: card files, lists, individual files and general documents. Documents become public after 70 years under conditions set out in a linked PDF. A search-engine summary of other ICRC pages reports the Agency's card index passed 36 million cards by June 1947 and that new research requests are currently paused with a notice pointing to tracing.archives@icrc.org; that status was not confirmed on the page read. Individuals are found through nominal lists plus birth date and place, father's first name and POW number.
providers.triageNote: Access page read; request process and current status are not on it. The pause notice came from a search snippet and must be checked at icrc.org before anyone submits a request.

providers.name: Memorial de la Shoah (Paris) - Documentation Centre
providers.what: Paris memorial with a documentation centre made up of archives, a photo library, a library and audiovisual collections, plus archives of its temporary exhibitions. An online documentation portal is described as searching for people, documents, photos, films, books and posters, and a form lets visitors request information about a person. Entry to the memorial is free with no reservation. The page read states no holdings counts and does not mention a list of names of people deported from France.
providers.triageNote: English home page read; the portal and request form were not opened. Needs a person to confirm what the portal holds for named deportees.

providers.name: Commonwealth War Graves Commission
providers.what: The Commission founded by Royal Charter in 1917 on behalf of the governments of Australia, Canada, India, New Zealand, South Africa and the United Kingdom. Its site states a database of 1.7 million men and women of the Commonwealth who died in the two world wars, searched through a War Dead search box, with separate searches for cemeteries and memorials and an archive of over 60,000 items (correspondence, maintenance and tour reports, staff records, photographs, press cuttings). For the Second World War the roll also includes Commonwealth civilians who died between 3 September 1939 and 31 December 1947 through enemy action, Allied weapons of war or in an enemy prison camp (the Civilian War Dead 1939-1945, whose roll is held at Westminster Abbey); the Find War Dead search reaches them under its Served In menu. It does not hold German, Soviet, Polish or other non-Commonwealth dead, and service records themselves are held by national archives, not by the Commission.
providers.triageNote: About us and Find records pages and a search summary of the Find War Dead page read; the Find War Dead page itself returned 403 to the fetch, so fields and any charge are unconfirmed. A person must run the search and say what it costs.

providers.name: Volksbund Deutsche Kriegsgräberfürsorge - Gräbersuche online
providers.what: The German War Graves Commission's online search for German war dead and missing from both world wars and victims of tyranny. The page states 5,428,382 war dead and missing persons in the database (figure shown on 4 November 2026) and that about 450,000 further names are expected in the coming years. Searched by first name, last name (no titles or nobility), date of birth, place of birth and date of death or going missing; wildcards are allowed in names and place; at least a first name, last name or place of birth is needed. Results may have gaps because place of birth is not known for every war dead; a search form is offered for people not yet in the database. It documents German war dead and does not cover other nations' dead.
providers.triageNote: The Gräbersuche page was read in full. Whether the search is free is not stated there. A person should try a search and check which graves and cemetery details are returned for the Second World War.

providers.name: ICRC Tracing Archives (Second World War Central Agency)
providers.what: Archive of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Geneva with the files of its wartime Central Agency for prisoners of war and civilian internees: nominal lists, transfer lists between camps, proof of detention in specific camps, liberation lists and death certificates, and index cards filed alphabetically by nationality that numbered more than 36 million by the end of the war. The ICRC's general access page says documents become available to the public after 70 years under conditions. Service status as stated on the ICRC blog on 19 January 2026: the online request form is unavailable, requests for Second World War information in collections open to the public are under a moratorium with no further requests processed until further notice, and only requests for administrative or compensation files and for identifying biological parents are accepted (by email to tracing.archives@icrc.org, duly justified). A digitisation programme begins in 2026. It is a request service, not a searchable index.
providers.triageNote: ICRC blog FAQ (19 January 2026) and the Access to the ICRC's Agency archives page read. The moratorium may have been lifted since; a person should check the ICRC page before advising a family to write.

providers.name: DRK-Suchdienst (German Red Cross Tracing Service)
providers.what: The German Red Cross tracing service, whose Munich office has been the central information and documentation centre since 1982 and holds a central name card index there. Its site offers an online tracing request for relatives missing in connection with the Second World War or the division of Germany. The home page does not state the size of the card index, who may apply or any fee. It is a request service, not a searchable online index.
providers.triageNote: English home page read; eligibility, cost and the request form's questions were not on it. A person should read the contact page and the request form.

providers.name: Žrtve II. svetovne vojne (SIstory, Institute of Contemporary History)
providers.what: Collection of victims of the Second World War in Slovenia compiled by the Institute of Contemporary History (INZ) in Ljubljana and published on the Zgodovina Slovenije portal; the SIstory front page links a 'Popis žrtev 2. svetovne vojne' and a dataset 'Smrtne žrtve druge svetovne vojne'. A Slovenian government notice of 1 October 2026 states that the collection lists more than 101,500 people who died during and directly after the war, calls it regularly updated and scientifically ordered, gives its address as sistory.si/ww2, and says it can serve as evidence in procedures to establish a death in the civil register. Its fields were not visible to the fetch. The interface is Slovenian.
providers.triageNote: SIstory home page and the gov.si notice read; the ww2 page itself returned no readable text, so fields and search method are unconfirmed. A person should open sistory.si/ww2 and note how records are searched.

providers.name: Australian War Memorial - Roll of Honour and Commemorative Roll
providers.what: The Roll of Honour names members of the Australian armed forces who died during or as a result of war service; for the Second World War the eligible period is 3 September 1939 to 30 June 1947. Each record gives personal particulars, unit and date of death, with cause and place of death and cemetery or memorial details on some, and more than half of records carry a scanned Roll of Honour circular (for the Second World War completed by the Directorate of War Graves Services, not by next of kin). The Commemorative Roll covers Australia-linked people who died in the same wars outside the Australian forces. The AWM's Second World War research guide also points to the AWM232 series on prisoners of war and missing persons (over 23,000, Far East and South West Pacific, to 30 June 1944), the University of Melbourne Archives enquiry cards of the Australian Red Cross (60,699 cards), the DVA WW2 Nominal Roll and the National Archives of Australia service records. The page states no count of names.
providers.triageNote: Roll of Honour page and the Second World War research guide read; the Commemorative Roll page and the search form were not fetched. A person should run a search and check which fields appear.

providers.name: Auckland War Memorial Museum - Online Cenotaph
providers.what: National biographical database of people who served for Aotearoa New Zealand, with World War II 1939-1945 as one of the conflicts that can be filtered. Searched by name or service number and by keyword. Records and stories are contributed by researchers, enthusiasts, veterans and families, so entries differ in depth. The page states contribution figures (94,032 images, 175,136 notes and details) but no total number of records and no WWII record count, and it does not say whether searching costs anything.
providers.triageNote: Front page of the Online Cenotaph read. Cost and the fields in a record need a person to run a search.

providers.name: Popravení za války (Czechoslovak citizens executed under Nazi rule, ÚSTR)
providers.what: Database run by the Czech Institute for the Study of Totalitarian Regimes (ÚSTR), with the Gedenkstätte Münchner Platz in Dresden (Stiftung Sächsische Gedenkstätten) as project partner, of Czechoslovak citizens executed on sentences of German Nazi courts, whatever their nationality or offence. Records give personal data and details of imprisonment, trial, execution and burial of the remains. The page says the pilot database for people executed in Dresden holds almost 900 people and that others are to be added gradually; no overall total is stated. Sections also cover places of execution, stories, farewell letters and sources. The site is in Czech. It does not cover Czech soldiers who fell in service or civilians killed in other ways.
providers.triageNote: Front page read; the date range and the fields searchable were not stated on it. The ministry database for fallen Czechoslovak soldiers at the Military History Archive could not be read (see notRead).

providers.name: American Battle Monuments Commission
providers.what: US federal agency that states 26 permanent American military cemeteries and 31 federal memorials, monuments and markers in 17 countries, honouring more than 200,000 fallen service members. People are searched through its Burial Database at weremember.abmc.gov; the footer also links a World War II Registry at wwiiregistry.abmc.gov. The home page gives no Second World War count and no step-by-step search instructions. It covers Americans buried or commemorated overseas and does not hold service files, which are with the National Archives.
providers.triageNote: Home page read only; the burial database and the registry were not opened, and the decedent search page returned 404. A person should run a search at weremember.abmc.gov.

providers.name: Australian War Memorial
providers.what: The First World War research guide lists: the First World War nominal roll (about 324,000 AIF personnel, recorded for repatriation), the embarkation roll (about 330,000 AIF personnel leaving Australia), the Roll of Honour (died during or as a result of service), the Commemorative Roll (died in wars but not eligible for the Roll of Honour), digitised Australian Red Cross Wounded and Missing Enquiry Bureau files (about 32,000 servicemen reported missing or wounded after July 1916; not every casualty has a file), the AN&MEF nominal roll, official casualty lists, unit war diaries, honours and awards, and published unit histories. Service records themselves are held by the National Archives of Australia and digitised there. Searched through Collections Search by name.
providers.triageNote: Research guide read in full. The guide does not say whether the rolls and databases cost anything. A person still needs to run a name search and note which roll and file number the entry points to.

providers.name: MémorialGenWeb
providers.what: Volunteer French site recording people who died for France in conflicts, civilian war victims and foreign soldiers who died on French territory. Holds war memorials and the names inscribed on them (with a photo database visitors can add to), SépulturesGenWeb for graves of these soldiers, records of people who died in deportation 1939-1945, old postcards of memorials, a glossary of regiments and downloadable documentary files. Run by the Association des Contributeurs et Administrateurs MémorialGenWeb, all volunteers; content is licensed Creative Commons BY-NC-SA 3.0. No totals of names or monuments are stated. It is a monument-and-grave index, not a service-record file.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Whether the site is free to use is not stated. A person needs to run a surname and village search and check how each memorial name is sourced.

providers.name: Verein für Computergenealogie — Verlustlisten (des.genealogy.net)
providers.what: Volunteer-transcribed databases of the printed First World War casualty lists, run by the Verein für Computergenealogie on its Data Entry System. One project covers the Austro-Hungarian Verlustlisten, built with the Austrian association Familia Austria (search fields: surname, first name, officer or enlisted, rank, unit, country, district, home place, birth year, status, event date and place, issue, date, page); a 2020 report put the 2 millionth entry at over 26,900 of about 37,000 pages complete, and a 2017 report said the booklets came from the Österreichisches Staatsarchiv and were scanned and run through OCR by Familia Austria. A separate project covers the German Reich Verlustlisten (fields include surname, first name, place, list, status, rank, birth date, edition, date, page). The lists record dead, wounded, missing and prisoners, not only deaths. The record count is not stated on the search pages.
providers.triageNote: Search interfaces for both projects read; the German project address is https://des.genealogy.net/eingabe-verlustlisten/search/index. Whether searching is free is not stated and login is optional. The GenWiki page on the German lists was blocked by bot protection and not read. The 'at' point is Vienna for the Austro-Hungarian lists only; the association itself is German.

providers.name: Kriegsarchiv — Österreichisches Staatsarchiv
providers.what: The Kriegsarchiv (Vienna) holds Austro-Hungarian military records. For soldiers who died 1914-1918 the Kriegsarchiv's own research page names: the printed casualty lists (digital copies at the Upper Austrian State Library, and the 'Nachrichten über Verwundete und Kranke' in the Czech Digital Library; they cover wounded and prisoners as well as the dead, with surname, first name, rank, birth year, home municipality and unit); the Totenkartei card index of the First World War (incomplete; images listed on FamilySearch); digitised Kriegsmatriken death registers for hospitals in Vienna and Lower Austria and for regiments recruiting in Vienna, Lower Austria and the Pressburg/Bratislava area; a Hungarian National Archives war-dead database; and ten volumes of post-war Ehrenbücher covering nine provinces. There is no general index of the deceased, and the original casualty reports are no longer available in the reading room.
providers.triageNote: Two Kriegsarchiv guidance pages read (soldiers who died; overview of researching in the Kriegsarchiv). Fees are not mentioned. The linked external databases (Upper Austrian library, Czech library, Hungarian archive, FamilySearch Totenkartei) were not opened. Search results also report 709 volumes of Verlustlisten 1914-1919 and a prisoner-of-war index that staff do not search; these come from the archive's pages in search results and need a person to confirm.

providers.name: Ireland's Memorial Records online (In Flanders Fields Museum)
providers.what: Search site for Ireland's Memorial Records, the register of Irish First World War dead compiled by the Irish National War Memorial Committee and published in 1923 in eight volumes, about 49,000 names (49,435 in one account). The site appears to be run by the In Flanders Fields Museum in Ypres, which holds an original set; it adds corrected burial or commemoration details for more than 10,000 men recorded as dying in France who fell in Belgium. Entries usually carry rank, regiment, service number and date of death. The register is incomplete and contains omissions, duplicates and errors, mostly for the Navy, Air Force and colonial regiments, and it left out Irish-born men who served in non-Irish units.
providers.triageNote: Landing page and the Wikipedia summary read. The operator is not named outright on the page and cost is not stated. A person needs to run a name search.

providers.name: Vojaške žrtve 1. svetovne vojne na Slovenskem (Institute of Contemporary History, Ljubljana)
providers.what: National database of soldiers who died within the present borders of Slovenia between 28 July 1914 and 4 November 1918, including volunteers and prisoners of war and people who died of war-related causes afterwards. Described as freely accessible. Coordinated by the Inštitut za novejšo zgodovino with 16 partner organisations; work began in spring 2015; presented publicly on 13 November 2018 with data on 26,224 people, and it may contain duplicates that cannot be identified from incomplete records. It records where men died on Slovenian territory, not Slovenes who died elsewhere.
providers.triageNote: Description read on the institute's collections page, which gives the address https://www.sistory.si/eng/ww1; that page returned no text to the fetch tool, so its search fields could not be read and no deep link is claimed. The 2018 count is from a search result quoting a scholarly article on the database.

providers.name: Caduti della Grande Guerra (Albo d'Oro)
providers.what: Online database of the Albo d'Oro of Italian military personnel who died in the First World War: the records of the fallen from the 28 volumes published by the Ministry of War, plus three appendices for the Veneto. Site edited by the Associazione Storica Cimeetrincee, copyright held by Istoreco Reggio Emilia, patronised by the Ministry of Defence. Menu offers a name search (Ricerche) and a page of search criteria. No total of names is stated. The Albo is the only official list of Italian dead but contains omissions and errors, and the Ministry of Defence also publishes a name search on difesa.it.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; the search pages themselves were not opened. The copyright notice bars use or distribution of the data and images without authorisation from Istoreco, and cost is not stated. The difesa.it Albo d'Oro page returned 404 and was not read.

providers.name: SlaveVoyages
providers.what: Free online databases on the Atlantic slave trade. The Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database (first made freely available in 2008) and the Intra-American Slave Trade Database (added 2020) record voyages. The People of the Atlantic Slave Trade section (2021) holds the African Origins Database, listing nearly 100,000 Africans freed from slave ships in the last sixty years of the trade, and the Oceans of Kinfolk Database, naming more than 63,000 people trafficked to New Orleans. Voyage-level records are not lists of every enslaved person carried.
providers.triageNote: Introduction page of the legacy site read; the page links to database, guide and download sections but does not explain how to search. Current database interface not read. A person needs to run name and ship searches and read the guides.

providers.name: Enslaved.org
providers.what: Linked-data site that searches across many datasets about enslaved people, people who enslaved others and people in the slave trade, with datasets contributed through the Journal of Slavery and Data Preservation, drawn from documents dated from the 15th to the early 20th century. The home page lists 731,500 people, 474,012 events, 10,381 places and 3,940 sources. Search is by a home-page search bar and an Advanced Search page, with browsing by people, events, places and sources.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. The page does not name the operating body (funders and partners shown include Matrix at Michigan State University, the Hutchins Center at Harvard and UC Riverside). A person needs to search surnames and given names; entries are only as complete as the contributed datasets.

providers.name: Documentation Center of Cambodia (DC-Cam)
providers.what: Documentation Center of Cambodia databases on the Khmer Rouge period (1975-1979). The catalogue page describes four databases searched separately: Biographic (30,442 biographies of victims, Khmer Rouge cadres and soldiers, and Tuol Sleng (S-21) prisoners), Bibliographic (2,963 records of confessions, interviews, books and primary documents), Photographic (5,190 photographs of Tuol Sleng prisoners) and Geographic (prisons, execution sites, mass graves and memorials). Not a list of all victims.
providers.triageNote: Catalogue page read; counts are as stated on that page, which describes the four databases. Individual record pages and the current search form not read. A person needs to search names in the Biographic and Photographic databases.

providers.name: Irish Famine Memorial (Australia) — Orphan Database
providers.what: Site of the Great Irish Famine Commemoration Committee (Sydney, Australia). Links to an Orphan Database of the young women who emigrated from Irish workhouses to Australia under the Earl Grey Scheme, 1848-1850; the page states that over 4,000 young women arrived. The home page does not state how the database is searched, its fields or its number of entries.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; the database pages and its key were not read. A person needs to open the database and check each girl's record against workhouse and ship records.

providers.name: Parks Canada — Grosse-Île and the Irish Memorial, list of names
providers.what: Parks Canada page for the Grosse-Île memorial (erected 1998) listing the people who died on Grosse-Île or on the ships, including immigrants, employees and sailors. States that 7,553 people are buried there and that 1,545 of them are unknown. Names are grouped on pages by year range, 1832-1836 to 1924-1934, with no keyword search described; only deceased persons are listed. Irish Famine arrivals of 1847 are among the quarantine-station dead.
providers.triageNote: Page read. A person needs to open the year-range pages for 1847 and then continue to Quebec arrival and church records for those who survived the station.

providers.name: Armenian Genocide Museum-Institute (AGMI)
providers.what: Museum-Institute in Yerevan. Its statement page lists an archival collection of photographs, memories, diaries, albums and documents, a collection of unpublished survivor memoirs, a library and journals. A Database of Victims and Survivors and an indexed database of survivor testimonies are described as planned, not as live. No name search is described.
providers.triageNote: Statement page read. Whether any name database is public now is not shown; a person needs to write to the Institute (contact address on the site) with the family name, village and Ottoman province.

providers.name: Matenadaran (Mesrop Mashtots Research Institute of Ancient Manuscripts)
providers.what: Manuscript institute in Yerevan with a Depository of Manuscripts, an Archive Department, a library and a Department of Digitization. Its Digital Resources menu lists a Digital Library, the Main Catalogue of manuscripts, old printed books and maps. An AGBU article states that Catholicos Khrimian's archive here holds over 8,000 letters, testimonies and documents written by peasants between 1893 and 1907 about the Hamidian massacres of 1894-1896.
providers.triageNote: Home page and the AGBU 'Letters of Last Hopes' article read. The home page does not mention the Khrimian archive and no finding aid for it was seen; whether it is searchable online is not stated. A person needs to ask the Archive Department.

providers.name: SEYFO Center
providers.what: Assyrian genocide (Seyfo) documentation site. Its Archives section lists book collections (Assyrian Genocide, Genocide Related, Ottoman History), British and French documents, themed collections, articles, photographs and videos, plus Interviews and Survivors categories. The home page does not describe name lists or a search function.
providers.triageNote: Home page navigation read; no collection pages opened. A person needs to open the Archives and Survivors sections and check for lists of villages or names.

providers.name: Centre for Asia Minor Studies (Athens)
providers.what: Athens research centre whose archives, per its home page, include an oral tradition archive, manuscripts, codices of Orthodox communities and parishes, maps and sketches, documents and photographs. A catalogue (OPAC) is at kms.openabekt.gr and a Digital Archives Platform at archives.kms.org.gr. The Leventis Foundation page states that the oral tradition archive records accounts of 5,000 Greek Orthodox refugees from Cappadocia, Pontus and Ionia and that over 150,000 handwritten pages were digitised.
providers.triageNote: Home page and the Leventis Foundation description read; neither says whether the catalogue or platform can be searched by name. A person needs to check the platform by village of origin and refugee surname.

providers.name: Pennsylvania State Archives
providers.what: State archive of Pennsylvania. Its 1918 influenza research guide lists few sources: the Cadaver Receiving Books, 1901-1965 (7 volumes; entries for October to December 1918 name influenza victims, mostly from Philadelphia, with age and occupation; digital images online through the PA Digital Archives) and field-hospital patient listings from the War History Commission file (July 17 to October 31, 1918) with names and serial numbers. Other series listed are governor, state police and papers correspondence without individual victims.
providers.triageNote: Research guide read; the page does not describe a general name search for the other series. Death certificates were not read on the archives' own pages. A person needs to check the death-certificate indexes and the online catalogue.

providers.name: The London Archives
providers.what: Archive at 40 Northampton Road, London EC1R 0HB. The home page states that the catalogue can be searched at any time, that entry is free and that a History Card is needed to view original documents. The home page does not mention parish registers.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. The page does not describe holdings; whether the City parish registers and the 1665 plague-year burial entries are held here and how complete they are needs checking in the catalogue by a person.

providers.name: The 1947 Partition Archive
providers.what: Oral history archive of witnesses and survivors of Partition and the Second World War. The home page links to Browse collections and Explore stories, offers requests for copies of an interview, and gives its book as 10,000 Memories. Its counters were not populated when read. Does not hold registers or lists of the dead.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; the Archive Access page and the search function not read. A person needs to search by village or city of origin and request interview copies.

providers.name: International Commission on Missing Persons (ICMP)
providers.what: Treaty-based organisation on missing persons. The home page lists Bosnia and Herzegovina as a State Party, a Western Balkans programme office in Sarajevo, an Online Inquiry Center where a missing person can be searched by first name, middle name, surname or nickname, and a public database that the page says contains 11364 records of missing persons. The page does not say how that database relates to the Bosnian war.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; the database itself not searched. A person needs to use the Missing Person Inquiry and the Bosnia programme pages.

providers.name: IRMCT Unified Court Records (ICTY and ICTR public judicial records)
providers.what: Search portal for the public judicial records of the Mechanism for International Criminal Tribunals and the public judicial archive records of the ICTR and ICTY, as described by the ICTY legacy site. A separate Case Law Database covers the tribunals' jurisprudence. Witness evidence, exhibits and judgments name victims and villages; it is not an index of victims.
providers.triageNote: The portal was not opened; its description was read on the ICTY legacy home page, which does not mention Bosnia-specific records. A person needs to search by case, municipality and exhibit.

providers.name: USC Shoah Foundation — Visual History Archive (non-Holocaust genocide collections)
providers.what: Video testimony archive. Besides the Holocaust, the page lists collections on the Cambodian Genocide, Genocide Against the Tutsi in Rwanda, the Armenian Genocide, the Guatemalan Genocide, the Nanjing Massacre, anti-Rohingya mass violence, Northern Syria and War and Genocide in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Overall figures on the page are 60,394 video testimonies in 45 languages; per-collection counts are not given. Access is through vha.usc.edu, with a request form for family copies.
providers.triageNote: Page read; the archive's search interface and access terms not read. A person needs to search testimony by place of origin and name of interviewee or relatives named.

providers.name: Open List (Открытый список)
providers.what: Community wiki-style database of people repressed for political reasons in the USSR, 1917-1991. The page reports 3,380,986 person records when read. Search is by surname, first name, patronymic, birth and death dates and place of residence, with * as a placeholder for an unknown name. Volunteers and researchers add and edit entries; versions exist in Ukrainian, Georgian and Belarusian. Entries are not independently verified records.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. The operating body is not named on the page. A person needs to search with Russian spellings and patronymic and check each entry's cited source.

providers.name: Hoover Institution Library & Archives
providers.what: Stanford research archive of nearly 7,000 collections on war, revolution and peace; reading room by reservation, with an Aeon account for requests. Its research guide on the American Relief Administration Russia records states that they document the 1921-1923 famine mission, with statistics and eyewitness accounts from the Volga region, Siberia, the Caucasus, Ukraine and Belarus, letters of gratitude from Soviet citizens, and related files of the Jewish Joint Distribution Committee, American Friends Service Committee and YMCA. The guide mentions no lists of names.
providers.triageNote: Library page and ARA guide read. A person needs to read the full finding aid for beneficiary or staff lists and ask Hoover reference staff.

providers.name: National Museum of the Holodomor-Genocide
providers.what: Museum in Kyiv. The English home page links to a Book of Remembrance, a Martyrology on victimsholodomor.org.ua, a Register of Burial Sites on an external map (map.memorialholodomor.org.ua) and survivor testimonies, and has a form for families to send memories and photographs. The page does not state counts or how names are searched.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; the linked martyrology site returned an access error and the burial map was not opened. A person needs to open those resources and search by village.

providers.name: Hiroshima National Peace Memorial Hall for the Atomic Bomb Victims
providers.what: Hall that registers the names and photographs of atomic bomb victims and displays and preserves them. It also holds survivor testimony videos and the Atomic Bomb Memoirs collection, with translations. The page says memoirs contribute to a database but does not describe it or any search function.
providers.triageNote: Home page read; no search method shown. A person needs to ask the hall whether a named victim is registered. The city's separate register of A-bomb victims (names in books under the Cenotaph) is a different record.

providers.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum
providers.what: Museum holding belongings left by victims, A-bombed artifacts and survivor testimonies, with a Peace Database for materials it manages and an online survivor testimony section. A notice on the page announces a temporary suspension of the Peace Database search function and of new applications to use atomic bomb-related materials. The page does not mention a list of victims' names.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Database not opened and its suspension means availability must be checked. Not a name register.

providers.name: Nagasaki National Peace Memorial Hall for the Atomic Bomb Victims
providers.what: Hall offering testimonial materials, survivors' testimony videos and translated memoirs, and accepting photographs of the deceased. The page states 204,708 deceased victims registered with Nagasaki City as of August 9, 2026. It does not say the hall holds a names register or describe a search; a Global Network site linked from it provides testimonies and memoirs.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. A person needs to ask the hall or Nagasaki City about the register of victims.

providers.name: Center of the Tokyo Raid and War Damages
providers.what: Museum in Tokyo with exhibits on air raids and wartime civilian life, a reference room with publications, photographs, and a link to the 都内戦災殉難者霊名簿, a register of names of Tokyo war casualties. The page does not say whether collections are searchable and does not describe survivor testimonies.
providers.triageNote: Home page read (Japanese terms as shown on the page); the register was not opened. A person needs to telephone or write to the centre (number on the site) to ask how names are checked.

providers.name: Libraries Tasmania (Tasmanian Archives and Names Index)
providers.what: State library and archives of Tasmania. The home page offers five searches: Library Catalogue, Tasmanian Archives (government and non-government records), Names Index (historical records about people), website, and a combined search; it links to family history and to a Tasmanian Aboriginal history page. Its guide to Tasmanian Aboriginal people lists series CBE1 (minutes of the Committee for the Care and Treatment of Captured Aborigines, 1830-1833), CSO89 (reports on the Oyster Cove establishment, 1855-1869), LSD51 (Cape Barren Island administration) and orphan school registers SWD28 and SWD26.
providers.triageNote: Home page and the Aboriginal people guide read. The guide does not name Black War, Flinders Island or Robinson papers. A person needs to search the Names Index and Archives catalogue and read the Aboriginal history page.

providers.name: Africa Archives (Belgian Federal Public Service Foreign Affairs)
providers.what: Belgian colonial public records, 1885 to 1962, from the Independent State of Congo (Congo Free State), the Ministry of Colonies and African Affairs, and Belgian Congo and Ruanda-Urundi. Topics include politics, administration, justice, security, mining, education, religion and civil status records; about 90 private bequests and microfilms of private papers are also held. Being re-inventoried and transferred to the National Archives of Belgium 2 (Joseph Cuvelier repository); transferred records are consulted by appointment, others in the Foreign Affairs reading room on request.
providers.triageNote: Page read; lists of transferred archives are PDFs and the page does not say catalogues are searchable online. A person needs to request the relevant lists and ask about civil status series.

providers.name: Muktijuddho e-Archive
providers.what: Digital library on the 1971 Liberation War and genocide. The menu lists a freedom fighters' list, books and documents, audio-video, a newspaper archive, photographs, a 1971 genocide and torture archive and an English section. It has a search box and a catalogue. The page states no totals. Does not hold death registers.
providers.triageNote: Home page read (Bengali menu); list contents and search results not opened. A person needs to search the freedom fighters' list and the genocide and torture archive.

providers.name: China Unofficial Archives (Minjian Danganguan)
providers.what: Non-profit bilingual digital archive of censored and suppressed Chinese history, free to browse. Holds books, films, official documents, articles and newsletters, including material on Mao-era persecution and the Cultural Revolution and a survivor memoir of the Great Famine period. The page lists no victim lists.
providers.triageNote: Home page read. Individual items not opened. Document and memoir collection, not a register of victims.

providers.name: Documenta - Centre for Dealing with the Past (Human Losses in Croatia 1991-1995)
providers.what: Zagreb NGO. Its home page lists the programme Documenting Human Losses in Croatia during the War 1991-1995, oral-history recording and war-crimes trial monitoring. Its news page on the Lika-Senj County results (29 June 2026) says the database holds 21,851 confirmed victims, 43,121 documents and 8,368 witness questionnaires; a victim counts as confirmed when three independent sources support identity and circumstances, and the list covers people whose residence and place of suffering were in Croatia, of any nationality or status. It calls the list not exhaustive and says no complete public list of all victims exists. Results are published as county tables; a single by-name search was not found on the pages read.
providers.triageNote: Read 2026-11-04: the home page, the project page and the Lika-Senj news page. The home page does not say whether names are searchable. A person needs to ask Documenta (Selska cesta 112c, Zagreb) for the county table that covers the place of death.

providers.name: Knjiga osoba nestalih na području Republike Hrvatske (Ministry of Croatian Veterans, with the Croatian Red Cross)
providers.what: Book of Missing Persons on the Territory of the Republic of Croatia, 3rd edition, April 2012: compiled by the Croatian Red Cross Tracing Service and the ministry's Administration for Detained and Missing Persons and cross-checked by the ICRC, the Serbian Red Cross and the Serbian Government commission. Names of people with an open tracing request are listed alphabetically and by place of disappearance; the foreword gives 1,868 people still missing and 454 open requests to trace remains at 30 April 2012, from the 1991-1995 war. It lists the missing only, not the dead whose fate is known. The PDF says printed copies can be seen at Croatian Red Cross tracing services and ICRC offices; a later edition was not found.
providers.triageNote: Read 2026-11-04: the PDF's title page, foreword and how-to-use page (188 pages); the name pages were not read. The ministry home page links a section on searching for people missing in the Homeland War (branitelji.gov.hr/o-ministarstvu/djelokrug/mjere/nestale-osobe/811) that was not opened.

providers.name: Documentation and Information Centre Veritas (Belgrade) - Serb victims of the war in Croatia
providers.what: Belgrade documentation centre headed by Savo Štrbac. Its Spiskovi (lists) section is built round Serb victims of the war and its aftermath in Croatia and the former Republic of Serbian Krajina, 1990-1998: a list of killed and missing, a list of Serb victims of Operation Storm, maps of refugee-column routes, and lists of Serbs prosecuted or imprisoned in Croatia. Serbia's pleadings at the ICJ cited its count of 6,792 killed and missing as of 31 October 2009. It covers Serb victims only; the pages read do not show whether the lists can be searched by name.
providers.triageNote: Read 2026-11-04: the home page and the English front page; the lists themselves were not opened. A person needs to open the killed-and-missing list and look up the village of death.

providers.name: Humanitarian Law Center (Belgrade and Pristina) - Kosovo Memory Book and human-losses databases
providers.what: Human-rights NGO. Its Kosovo Memory Book lists 13,625 individuals killed or missing in connection with the Kosovo conflict from 1 January 1998 to 31 December 2000, from 42,819 documents (13,535 individuals from 31,600 documents at its February 2015 launch); it includes victims of war crimes, people who died in combat and the forcibly disappeared. The site also lists databases of human losses of Serbia and Montenegro in the wars in Slovenia, Croatia and Bosnia, in the NATO bombing and in Macedonia, a register of Croatian citizens of Serbian ethnicity killed in Croatia, and a search of the 1991-1995 losses of Serbia and Montenegro. The Kosovo Memory Book page has no search form of its own and points to kosovomemorybook.org, which did not load for this check.
providers.triageNote: Read 2026-11-04: the home page, the Kosovo Memory Book page and the 2015 release. No database was searched. A person needs the Kosovo Memory Book or the 1991-1995 losses search and the victim's name and place.

providers.name: Government Commission on Missing Persons (Kosovo)
providers.what: Kosovo government body whose duties are set by Law No. 04/L-023 on Missing Persons and Regulation 15/2012; ICMP says it helped establish the commission in 2006. The site's menu has sections on missing persons, a location tracker, legislation, the commission's mandate and composition, regional cooperation, announcements, a Databaza and contacts, a link to start a case, and a free phone line (0800 01 600). The page as read shows no list of names and no case count, so what the database holds is not established.
providers.triageNote: Read 2026-11-04: the front page only, in Albanian. The Databaza and the start-a-case page were not opened. A person needs to use the case link or the phone line to report or ask about a missing relative.

providers.name: Kosovo Specialist Chambers and Specialist Prosecutor's Office (The Hague)
providers.what: Temporary court in The Hague, set up under an international agreement, a Constitutional Amendment and a Kosovo law, for crimes against humanity, war crimes and other crimes under Kosovo law committed or begun in Kosovo between 1 January 1998 and 31 December 2000. The home page says court records are public through a Public court records database and that hearings can be streamed. Judgments and filings name victims in the cases tried (Thaçi et al.); it is not an index of the dead, and the records database was not opened.
providers.triageNote: Read 2026-11-04: the English home page only. The Public court records database was not opened. A person needs to search by case name and then by village or victim named in the judgment.

providers.name: Registro Unificado de Victimas del Terrorismo de Estado (RUVTE) - Archivo Nacional de la Memoria
providers.what: The Argentine state's unified register of victims of state terrorism and of clandestine detention centres, covering 28 June 1966 to 10 December 1983, kept by the National Memory Archive. The page also describes a genetic-identification area that takes samples from relatives of the disappeared, with the Argentine Forensic Anthropology Team. The page links a 2015 report on disappearances and killings; whether a name search is open to the public was not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Ensaaf (Punjab disappearances and extrajudicial killings documentation)
providers.what: A US-registered human-rights group that documents unlawful killings, enforced disappearances and illegal cremations in Punjab, India, in 1984-1995. Its site reports 4,466 documented unlawful killings and 848 enforced disappearances and links to a Victim Data site and a Testimonies site; those two sites were not opened, so whether names are searchable is not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Biblioteca Virtual de la Verdad y Reconciliacion, Peru (1980-2000)
providers.what: An online library on the 1980-2000 violence in Peru, with sections for books, documents and news, video and film, photographs and art, kept to preserve historical memory. Its front page cites the Truth and Reconciliation Commission's estimate of about 70,000 deaths. It does not say it holds victim lists or a database searchable by name.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: ICRC in Lebanon (missing and forcibly disappeared persons, Law 105)
providers.what: The International Committee of the Red Cross's Lebanon country page, which says it worked in Lebanon through the 1975-1990 civil war and lists a guide to Law 105 of 2018 on the Missing and Forcibly Disappeared Persons. Where families register a missing relative was not shown on the page.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Colonial Frontier Massacres in Australia, 1788-1930 (University of Newcastle)
providers.what: A map, timelines and a site list of frontier massacres in Australia from British colonisation to 1930, with the sources used for each site listed on its page. The home page says thousands of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people were killed and that it includes only massacres with sufficient evidence; it does not list victim names or state a total.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Service historique de la Defense (France)
providers.what: The French Ministry of the Armed Forces' historical service, with sites at Vincennes, Cherbourg, Brest, Lorient, Rochefort, Toulon, Caen, Pau and Chatellerault. The home page names officers' individual files among its most consulted holdings and offers a search of its archive inventories and access to digitised archives; the page read does not say what it holds before 1789.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Service historique de la Defense (Vincennes)
providers.what: The French defence ministry's historical service. Its homepage lists individual files of officers among its most-consulted inventories, a browser for conflicts and operations, simple and advanced search, search by thematic plan and a link to digitised archives, and announces a large digitisation of the GR 16 P sub-series at Vincennes. The homepage does not say which periods the officers' files cover, whether any soldiers of the Revolution and Empire or of the conquest of Algeria are searchable by name, or link to a database of them.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Archivo General de la Nacion (Venezuela)
providers.what: The national archive of Venezuela. Its homepage has menus for holdings (fondos documentales), catalogues, indexes, inventories and files (expedientes), and carries news of independence-era documents such as Bolivar's 1819 Angostura speech, with links to the Archivo del Libertador and Archivo Zamora portals. The homepage does not describe what the holdings contain for 1810-1823, whether any civil or military registers are among them, or what can be searched online.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: General State Archives of Greece (GAK)
providers.what: The Greek national archives service. When read, its portal showed a notice that the site was being updated and named three digital services: the National Archives Inventory, a Digital Archives Portal for 1922, and @rchiomnimon, a collection of digital archival material. The page does not say what they hold for the war of 1821 or whether any register of fighters or of the dead is searchable.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: National Park Service - Civil War Soldiers and Sailors System
providers.what: A database of service records of over 6 million Union and Confederate soldiers, unit histories of over 4,000 regiments, battle descriptions, a list of 18,000 African American sailors, and selected prisoner-of-war and cemetery lists. The prisoner and cemetery lists are partial, it does not list all sailors, and the page says it is no longer maintained or updated.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Iraq Body Count
providers.what: Public record of violent civilian deaths in Iraq since the 2003 invasion, built from cross-checked media reports and hospital, morgue, NGO and official figures. It documents 200,065 to 226,628 civilian deaths and about 300,000 violent deaths including combatants. It counts violent deaths only and does not claim to be complete.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Airwars
providers.what: Not-for-profit monitor founded in 2014 that tracks, assesses and archives claims of civilian harm in conflict: the US-led coalition in Iraq and Syria, US forces in Yemen, the Russian military in Ukraine and the Israel and Gaza war from 2023. Its site mentions a Casualty Archive but does not describe what it holds, and it is not a register of all the dead.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Yemen Data Project
providers.what: Data on air raids and their civilian casualties in Yemen: all 25,054 Saudi-led coalition raids from 25 March 2015 to April 2022, with a downloadable dataset, and databases for US-UK and US strikes in 2024 and 2025. The pages report counts of dead and injured and do not mention individual names.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Book of Memory of the Fallen for Ukraine (Книга пам'яті полеглих за Україну)
providers.what: Searchable database with an individual profile for each person who died defending Ukraine since 2014: full name, nickname, birth and death dates and, for some, a photo. It can be filtered by service branch, rank, date of death, military operation, birth region and foreign citizenship. Founded 22 July 2014 and updated in 2025; it covers those who died on the Ukrainian side only.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Residual Special Court for Sierra Leone (archives of the Special Court)
providers.what: Manages the archives of the Special Court for Sierra Leone: case records, hearing videos and transcripts. The site also has a page for the Truth and Reconciliation Commission report. The pages seen do not mention witness statements or lists of the dead.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: WarVictimSampo 1914-1922 (Sotasurmat 1914-22), Aalto University
providers.what: Semantic portal of Aalto University's Semantic Computing Research Group built on the National Archives of Finland's Sotasurmat 1914-22 database: some 40,000 death records for 1914-1922, most of them from the Finnish Civil War and the rest from the First World War and the Kindred Nations Wars, with about 1,200 battles and prisoner camps. Read from its project page; the search itself was not opened.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Todos (...) los Nombres
providers.what: Spanish-language database of victims of Francoism in Andalusia, Extremadura and North Africa, run by the Andalusian branch of the CGT union and the association Nuestra Memoria. It reports 120,508 victims, searchable by surname, first name, nickname and municipality, with a map of mass graves and some 1,184 short biographies; free, under a Creative Commons licence. It covers a region, not all of Spain.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: National Revolutionary Martyrs' Shrine (Taipei), Ministry of National Defense
providers.what: Site of the shrine run by the Armed Forces Reserve Command of Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense, in Chinese with an English version: profiles of martyrs and a link to a separate Ministry database of martyrs' names. The name lookup was not opened, so what years and wars it covers is not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: Centro Nacional de Memoria Historica (Colombia)
providers.what: Colombian government body for the memory of the armed conflict. Its Archivo de los Derechos Humanos takes enquiries by email and web form, and its Observatorio de Memoria y Conflicto reports a headline count of deaths in the armed conflict and its origins (282,879, as of 31 March 2026). The home page read does not name the victim databases or say how they are searched.
providers.triageNote: Added with the wars research; access class still needs a person.

providers.name: One Search, Family History Indexes — State Library of Queensland
providers.what: The State Library of Queensland's catalogue (Primo), searched with its Family History scope. What was seen on 8 Nov 2026: a search for the exact phrase "convict transportation registers" returned 123,888 results, each an INDEX RECORD for one convict, such as a name, the ship and the sailing date, filed under 'Criminal : Convict transportation registers [HO 11]', the British Home Office series of convict registers, attributed to the Home Office and the State Library of Queensland. The library's own guide says the index was transcribed from microfilm of HO 11 and covers more than 123,000 of the 160,000 convicts transported between 1787 and 1867, searchable by convict name, ship or date.
