It is an index of people in an official register, not a copy of the register's pages and not a record of anyone's later life. The same scope also reaches other family-history indexes; only this one set was looked at.
providers.triageNote: Suggested by David. The deep-linked search loaded in a normal browser with no sign-in and listed results, so the result list is open; whether each 'Available online' item opens without an account was not tested, so `access` is the class of what was seen (an index record) and nothing about cost or images is claimed. Not yet checked: the other indexes in the Family History scope, and whether the register images themselves are on the National Archives (UK) site.

providers.name: eGGSA Church and Burial Registers (BDM project), transcribed registers
providers.what: A volunteer transcription project run under the Genealogical Society of South Africa's electronic branch. Its pages link to separate baptism, marriage and burial searches. The page names the Cape Town Dutch Reformed registers of the 1600s and the Stellenbosch Dutch Reformed registers from 1688 to 1794, and a related page says Stellenbosch burial registers 1765 to 1946 are searchable. Entries are typed as written, merged into one format, and each carries its source. The page says the information is free to all but not for commercial use. I did not run a search, and the page does not list every congregation or the full year range.
providers.triageNote: Opened the BDM introduction page and the Stellenbosch introduction page on 2026-11-08 (text read; no search run). Separate address from the existing eGGSA row, which points at the society's home page.

providers.name: eGGSA Passenger List Project (South Africa)
providers.what: A volunteer project that transcribes passenger lists found in South African archives. The page lists Natal Immigration Board lists for immigrants 1850 to 1911 from the Pietermaritzburg repository, twenty ship lists from an 1859 to 1864 emigration scheme, Western Cape Archives public-works series covering 1873 to 1885, and published lists of departures from British ports in the 1880s. Only the typed data is published, not the images, because of agreements with the archives. A separate Search Passenger Lists page does the searching and a page lists voyages done so far. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the project page on 2026-11-08 and read the source and year list; did not open the search page or test results.

providers.name: eGGSA 1820 Settler Correspondence
providers.what: A transcribed archive of letters about the 1820 Cape settler scheme, taken from digital photographs of bound volumes at the UK National Archives, Kew (class CO48), with some Cape Archives volumes added in 2016. The site says it holds several thousand letters. Letters are grouped one page per writer, browsable by surname before and after 1820, and a search box covers every name mentioned in the letters, not only the writers. There are also pages on settler places, settler returns and data tables, and Kew page numbers are given where they exist. The site says it is free to browse; I did not test the search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read its description of the series and layout; did not test the search box.

providers.name: eGGSA South African Newspaper Extracts
providers.what: Volunteer transcriptions from about forty South African newspapers, including Cape, Natal, Eastern Cape and Transvaal titles. Year ranges differ by title; the page gives for example 1824 to 1856 for one Cape commercial paper and 1852 to 1856 for a Graaff-Reinet paper, and recent additions are 1870s Eastern Province issues. A search engine covers all titles with filters and exact, any-word, prefix, wildcard and fuzzy modes, and there is a separate section of obituaries and snippets. The page does not say which kinds of notice are extracted, so check a title before relying on it. The pages say the transcriptions are free to browse.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; read the title list and search modes; did not run a search or open an extract.

providers.name: eGGSA Gravestones photographic database
providers.what: A gravestone photograph database for South Africa, with a separate section for each of nine provinces plus a location-unknown section and a worldwide section for South Africans buried abroad. Each province has its own search and there is no single search across all of them yet. Photos are donated by volunteers, and the page warns that some are personal selections rather than whole cemeteries. The terms allow limited personal use with credit but forbid commercial copying. A page of newly added cemeteries for 2026 is linked. I did not run a search or open a photograph.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the coverage and terms text; did not open a province search.

providers.name: eGGSA Family Bible Collection (South Africa)
providers.what: A gallery of photographs of family register pages from family Bibles and original family registers, held as fragile objects and shared so researchers can see them. The page says every entry lists its surnames and that all surnames are searchable through a Search the Bibles Collection link. Entries run, by the page's own spread, from roughly the early 1700s to the late 1900s and the gallery is about twenty pages long. Use is free to browse but copying for commercial gain is not allowed. I did not run a search or check whether the pages are transcribed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; did not run the surname search.

providers.name: eGGSA Archive Documents gallery
providers.what: A gallery of photographed archive documents, organised by repository: Free State Archives Repository (198 items shown), Pietermaritzburg (143), the National Archives repository in Pretoria (1), Cape Town, and a VOC set of ships' pay-ledger accounts dated 1662 to 1805. Most are photographs of documents from South African archives. Each picture can be fetched in two sizes. The page also describes a service that arranges photographing of documents at the Bloemfontein, Pietermaritzburg and Durban archives. The collection was recently moved to new software and is still being checked. I did not open an album.
providers.triageNote: Opened the gallery home page on 2026-11-08 and read the repository list; did not open an album or the ordering service.

providers.name: South African Records Transcribed (eGGSA)
providers.what: A menu-driven site of transcriptions of early South African documents. The page lists Cape Town Dutch Reformed baptisms 1653 to 1756, marriages 1656 to 1803 and memberships 1665 to 1832, Stellenbosch baptisms 1688 to 1815 and marriages 1689 to 1815, Drakenstein baptisms 1694 to 1713, Cape freeburger lists, slave baptisms from the Amsterdam church council, Orphan Chamber and Court of Justice transcripts, and indexes to VOC papers at the Dutch National Archives. It also points to the 1925 to 1931 voter rolls on FamilySearch. The page says the information is free but not for commercial use. I did not open an individual register page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the collection list; sub-pages were not opened. A sub-page I tried by guess returned 404.

providers.name: Stamouers, South African Progenitors (eGGSA)
providers.what: An eGGSA project publishing articles on the founding ancestors of South African surnames, mainly families with a living male line in South Africa. Articles are arranged alphabetically by surname range, with background sections on the Cape church, the Dutch East India Company, Huguenots, burgher arrivals, slaves and Khoi-San people, and ship pay ledgers. The core period is the 1650s to 1750s with later chapters to the 1820 settlers. The site has no search tool on the page I read, so browse by surname range. It says it does not vouch for accuracy and asks users to verify.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open a surname article.

providers.name: AngloBoerWar.com (Anglo-Boer War research site and forum)
providers.what: A volunteer-run research site on the Anglo-Boer War of 1899 to 1902 that also covers frontier wars from 1779 and the 1906 Natal rebellion. The front page counts about 753,000 soldier records, 146 full-text books, thousands of articles, tens of thousands of images, unit pages, a gazetteer, medal and award pages, a ship list and a large forum. A Name Search page looks up a name, unit or mention in despatches, and units, places and medals can be browsed. The site says use is free and an account is optional. I did not run a name search, and a guessed name-search address returned 404.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the counts and sections; did not run a search.

providers.name: South Africa War Graves Project
providers.what: A volunteer project to photograph the graves and memorial names of South African and Rhodesian service dead, from the Anglo-Boer War through the Bambatha rebellion, the world wars, Korea and the Border War to modern police casualties. The page counts about 41,000 known graves and over 28,900 photographed, and says an online database opened on 9 November 2013 and is updated daily. The site gives an advanced-search link and says photos will be freely available to families. The copyright line and daily-rate note on the page I read are dated to 2017 and 2018, so currency is unchecked. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; did not run a search or confirm the database is still updated.

providers.name: The Huguenot Society of South Africa (Franschhoek)
providers.what: The society that supports the Huguenot Memorial Museum at Lambrechts Street, Franschhoek. Its page says it keeps and updates records of Huguenot settlers and their descendants at the museum and maintains a database for Huguenot-directed research. It publishes an annual Bulletin, a genealogy book series, and a register of Huguenots who came to the Cape as a free PDF, and sells a CD of Bulletins from 1963 to 2004. A research-articles page lists journal papers from 1973 to 2023, family biographies A to Z, and PDF lists such as people who left the Cape. Membership is open to anyone. I did not open the PDFs or test how the database can be consulted.
providers.triageNote: Opened the society page and the research page on 2026-11-08 (second page was long; only the first part was read). Did not open the register PDF or the database.

providers.name: Cory Library for Historical Research, Rhodes University
providers.what: A research library and archive on the ground floor of the Eden Grove building at Rhodes University in Makhanda, Eastern Cape. Its site lists the Methodist Church archives, the Lovedale collection, the Goldfields collection, Rhodes University archives, a teachers' training college collection, photographic slides and its own digital collections. Visitors can search through the university library catalogue and there is a Finding Aids section and an online-newspapers section. The page gives opening as closed at weekends and public holidays and describes deposit policies. I did not open a finding aid, so I cannot say which parish or settler series are described.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the collection and catalogue links; did not open a finding aid or the digital collection.

providers.name: History Society of Zimbabwe (Heritage of Zimbabwe journal)
providers.what: The learned society for Zimbabwean history, founded in 1953 as the Rhodesia Africana Society, renamed Rhodesiana Society in 1958 and History Society of Zimbabwe in 1981. It runs regional branches, talks and outings. Its journal began as Rhodesiana in 1957 (40 volumes to 1979) and continues as Heritage of Zimbabwe, with volume 35 in 2016. Web-search listings showed issue PDFs on the same site, but the page I read does not say whether back issues are online, so I did not rely on that. Useful for local-history background and family context rather than name indexes.
providers.triageNote: Opened the society history page on 2026-11-08; did not open an issue PDF or confirm that back numbers are online.

providers.name: JewishGen Southern Africa SIG (SA-SIG)
providers.what: The Southern Africa special interest group hosted on JewishGen. Its page lists articles on Southern African Jewish history, community and synagogue directories, cemetery lists, marriage records and military records, a daily discussion group, a newsletter, and the Rootsbank research project on about 15,000 families who moved to Southern Africa between 1850 and 1950, run with a Cape Town university. The page says access to the group's material needs SIG membership, and that the site search engine was marked as not working as of April 2016. I did not open a record list, and the page may be old.
providers.triageNote: Opened the SA-SIG home page on 2026-11-08 and read the section list; did not open a database page. The page itself carries an April 2016 note on search.

providers.name: Basel Mission Archives online catalogue (Mission 21)
providers.what: An online catalogue of the Basel Mission Society archive. The home page counts some 30,000 images and 6,700 maps, sketches and plans, plus references to written records, from the 19th and 20th centuries; the image titles name places such as Accra and Cannanur. A How to use page says to start with Search in Catalogue, that keyword or full-text queries need four characters, that results can be filtered by maps, text or images, and that the archive plan can be browsed from main stocks, with written documents arranged by region. Keyword browsing is offered by place, institution and photographer. The site says the material is shown unchanged and carries a warning about outdated attitudes. I did not search and did not see a statement on registers or access rules.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and How to use page on 2026-11-08; did not search or open a record. Town is taken from the Basel Mission name; the pages did not state it.

providers.name: Cercle de Genealogie Maurice-Rodrigues (CGMR), Mauritius
providers.what: An association for Mauritian genealogy. Its site says all its records are online in a separate ExpoActes database at cgmrgenealogie.org, grouped into categories such as births, deaths and places, and it holds cemetery records from Mauritian cemeteries, said to run to thousands. It runs a volunteer help forum (free registration), and advises having dates and places of birth and death ready. The site points researchers on to the civil status office and the national archives. The page does not state the years covered or the record counts, and does not say whether the database needs an account. I did not open the database.
providers.triageNote: Opened the site home page on 2026-11-08; did not open the ExpoActes database.

providers.name: The Kabristan Archives (memorial inscriptions: Indian sub-continent, Sri Lanka, Ireland, Jamaica)
providers.what: An archive of memorial inscriptions from graveyards, including some that no longer exist, covering Ireland, the Indian sub-continent, Sri Lanka and Jamaica. The site lists burials, marriages, birth and baptism entries and a Ceylon Roll of Honour for the First World War, with about 141,000 entries in total and no as-at date. There is a search page and a way to browse by region, and a publications section. Copies of a memorial inscription are offered at a stated price including postage. I did not run a search so I cannot say what the free search shows.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08; did not run a search.

providers.name: Genealogy Sri Lanka (Kabristan group)
providers.what: A family history site for Sri Lanka (formerly Ceylon), part of the Kabristan group of genealogy sites. Its home page counts about 33,000 births and baptisms, 16,800 marriages, 32,000 deaths and burials and 2,351 First World War Roll of Honour entries, and lists transcribed church register CDs and books. Indexes to Ceylon births, marriages and deaths are held on the sister Kabristan Archives site. The page has no search tool of its own and asks visitors to send queries by the contact page. Years covered and prices are not stated.

providers.name: BACSA Burials Database (British Association for Cemeteries in South Asia)
providers.what: A unified index of burials in European cemeteries in India and South Asia and of memorial inscriptions elsewhere for people who lived or served there, built from the association's cemetery record books and other compiled data. The page calls it a work in progress with volunteers still transcribing. Quick Search has first name, surname, place, county, year range and category fields with default, exact and variant matching, plus Find a person and Advanced search. The page does not give a record count and does not say whether searching needs membership. It sits on the same hosting as the FIBIS database, but is a separate database. I did not run a search.

providers.name: Abhilekh Patal, National Archives of India digital portal
providers.what: The National Archives of India's online portal (Portal for Access to Archives and Learning). The index to the collection sits under Reference Tools. Pages from digitised records can be ordered through a Page on Demand service and undigitised records through Digitize on Demand. The page does not describe how to search or whether an account is needed. The portal itself returned no text to my fetch, so I read only the National Archives' description of it.

providers.name: JACAR, Japan Center for Asian Historical Records
providers.what: A digital archive that lets users view images of official documents from the National Archives of Japan, the Diplomatic Archives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the National Institute for Defense Studies, on modern relations between Japan and its Asian neighbours. The English home page offers a database search, a search guide, advice on using the database in English and a Japanese-English translation collection, plus web exhibitions. Another page lists the records available for viewing and the documents that can be accessed. Useful for military, diplomatic and consular files rather than civil registers. I did not run a search or open an image.

providers.name: Public Records Office, Government Records Service, Hong Kong
providers.what: The designated archives of the Hong Kong government. Its Search our holdings page says it holds over 1.9 million records dating from the mid-19th century, in three groups: archival items (government series HKRS and private papers and copies of overseas records, HKMS), library items from the Central Preservation Library for Government Publications, and the Carl Smith Collection of data cards compiled from original records, newspapers and publications. Holdings are searched through the online catalogue called @PRO, for which user-account registration guides are published, and records can be reserved. There is also an Online holdings page with digitised photographs and albums marked for private study only. I did not open the catalogue.

providers.what: The archive of Academia Sinica's Institute of Taiwan History in Nangang, Taipei, with a resources page listing its databases. providers.name: Jokbo (Korean genealogy) database, Jon'gyeong'gak, Sungkyunkwan University
providers.what: An online database of Korean clan genealogy books (jokbo) built by the Academy of East Asian Studies at Sungkyunkwan University. The introduction says it can be searched by family title, name or nickname, civil-service exam record, official post, birth and death years and ancestral residence. It describes browsing by family name or ancestral home, reading prefaces in Chinese characters with Korean translation, viewing descendants by generation, and opening original pages, with statistics on births, deaths, exams and marriage ties between families. providers.name: Korean History Database (National Institute of Korean History, db.history.go.kr)
providers.what: The source database of the National Institute of Korean History, grouped by period from ancient to contemporary. It includes the Joseon royal annals and the royal secretariat diary for the Joseon period, and modern and contemporary sections with newspapers, independence-movement records, US military government papers, staff directories (the closest to personnel records) and a person database for modern times. Search is by main box or advanced search with date filters, synonym and variant-character matching, a thesaurus search, and browsing by period or alphabet. Some databases sit on separate sites. The page does not mention clan genealogies or exam rosters. I did not open a record.

providers.name: NewspaperSG (National Library Board, Singapore)
providers.what: The National Library Board's digitised newspaper archive for Singapore, with a catalogue of titles in English, Malay, Chinese, Tamil and other languages. The home page offers keyword and advanced search, browse by publication date, a Search Term Visualiser and saved citations, and Today in History pages with issues back to 1827. The page shows preview-only years but I did not test whether article images open without sign-in.

providers.name: Israel Genealogy Research Association (IGRA)
providers.what: The largest genealogical society in Israel, by its own description, and a member of the international association of Jewish genealogical societies. providers.name: Museu da Imigração do Estado de São Paulo, Acervo Digital (Memória da Imigração) / Immigration Museum digital collection
providers.what: Online database of the Museu da Imigração, built with the Arquivo Público do Estado de São Paulo from the papers of the old Hospedaria de Imigrantes (the state immigrant hostel). The page says it holds over 250,000 images, free to view and download, in separate categories each with its own search page: matrícula registers (book pages viewable, searchable by surname), about 32,000 cartas de chamada (letters guaranteeing support for relatives arriving), SACOP petitions about transport costs, maps, about 8,000 pictures, immigrant-community newspapers and ship passenger lists. providers.name: Museu da Imigração, Jornais das colônias de imigrantes / immigrant-community newspapers

providers.name: Arquivo Público do Estado de São Paulo, Pesquisa e certidões de imigração / immigration search and certificates
providers.what: Service of the state archive of São Paulo that issues certificates from three immigration series: the registration books of the Hospedaria de Imigrantes (1882-1973, with the online database covering up to 1958 while later books are still being digitised and indexed), the passenger lists of ships docking at the Port of Santos (December 1888 to December 1978), and the registration cards of the foreigners' police office for the capital and Greater São Paulo (1939-1984). The page tells users to search the database first to confirm a record exists, notes that gaps are common, and says an absent result does not prove an arrival did not happen. Certificates are issued digitally after a request that requires a login and a payment of R$ 65.16 per certificate (the fee shown on the page), within up to 30 days. For arrivals through other ports it points to the Arquivo Nacional in Rio de Janeiro. Text is Portuguese. I did not open the search database itself.

providers.name: Archivo General de la Nación (Argentina), Consulta de antecedentes migratorios / arrival ledgers search
providers.what: Search tool for people who arrived by sea at the Port of Buenos Aires, drawn from the 'Libros de entrada de pasajeros vía marítima' made by the Dirección Nacional de Migraciones. providers.name: Archivo General de la Nación (Uruguay), Información de ingreso de inmigrantes / immigrant arrivals request
providers.what: Government procedure page for requesting information from the Archivo General de la Nación's databases on immigrants who arrived in Uruguay by sea. providers.name: Archivo Nacional de Chile, Bienes Raíces, Comercio y Minas (documentos.archivonacional.cl) / property, commerce and mining registers
providers.what: Digitised catalogues of registers transferred to the Archivo Nacional from the Conservadores. The page gives about 3,150,616 records for Bienes Raíces from 81 localities (1837-1985), about 125,988 for Comercio from 68 localities (1867-1985) and about 562,274 for Minas from 70 localities (1820-1986). You find a document in the database, add it to a shopping cart and request copies or certificates, which are signed electronically and emailed. Login is by a simple registration (name, national ID number, email, phone) or the state Clave Única; each catalogue has its own usage guide. The page states no prices. Useful for land and business transactions that name owners, sellers and heirs; it is not a civil register. Spanish.

providers.name: Archivo Nacional de Chile, Jesuitas de América (Junta de Temporalidades) / Jesuit records catalogue
providers.what: Digital catalogue of 433 volumes of the Fondo Junta de Temporalidades de la Compañía de Jesús held by the Archivo Nacional Histórico, dated 1561 to 1800. The volumes concern Jesuit activity in Chile, the Antilles (mainly Cuba), Argentina, Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador, Spain, Mexico, Peru, the Philippines and Venezuela. The page reports 271,426 digital images across the volumes, and offers a general search box plus a login link whose purpose it does not explain. The records are about the order's properties, accounts and expelled members' estates, so they suit colonial-era property and community history more than parish genealogy; I saw no statement about person-level indexing. Spanish.

providers.name: CubaGenWeb, sources for Cuban and Hispanic genealogy
providers.what: Volunteer-run guide page of the CubaGenWeb site, last updated October 2020 and copyrighted 2007-2020. providers.name: AlleSurinamers.org (Stichting voor Surinaamse Genealogie) / sources for Surinamese family history
providers.what: Source website of the Surinamese genealogy foundation, in Dutch, that brings the main sources for Surinamese family research together with explanations. It sorts them into searchable databases, digitised archives and special collections. Databases it names include censuses of 1811, 1921 and 1950, civil registry records, emancipation and manumission records, slave registers 1830-1863, wijkregisters 1828-1847, immigrant records for Chinese, Hindustani and Javanese workers, plantation and head-tax lists and an index of Japanese internment cards (1942-1945). Digitised archives it names include notarial archives (1699-1845), orphan chamber registers (1788-1877) and church registers, with passenger lists for 1728-1960 and a transcribed Roman Catholic register of 1786-1830. It also carries a ten-step beginner's guide and a handbook to the civil registry. The page does not say what each linked database costs.

providers.name: Stichting voor Surinaamse Genealogie (SSG) / Foundation for Surinamese Genealogy
providers.what: Website of the foundation that supports Surinamese ancestry research and runs AlleSurinamers.org. It offers a ten-step starter guide, a page linking to Surinamese family research sources, plantation lists and an expert question desk. providers.name: Bermuda Archives (Government of Bermuda)
providers.what: Government page for the Bermuda Archives, set up in 1974 under the Bermuda Archives Act. providers.name: National Archives of Trinidad and Tobago, General Registers of Indian Indentureship 1845-1917
providers.what: Catalogue description of the bound registers of Indian indentured immigrants (reference TT NATT IM 2), created by the Indian Immigration Office. The page says the volumes cover 1845 to 1917 in specific periods, entries are grouped by ship arrival with the ship name at the top of each page, and columns give ship number, registration number, name, father's name, age, sex, estate and a remarks column noting births, deaths, illness, return to India and land. Registers from the late 1800s and 1900 also record caste, native place and bodily marks. A companion research guide (node 274) gives 17 volumes, 298 ships and roughly 147,500 immigrants, notes that some registers are lost, and links a PDF list of the volumes to help find the year and ship. The page states no restriction on access; it does not say whether originals can be viewed on site or online.

providers.name: National Archives of Guyana (nationalarchives.gov.gy)
providers.what: Website of Guyana's national archive in Georgetown. It lists Court of Policy records, the Official Gazette, Colonial Office records, governors' dispatches, immigration records and colonial and modern newspapers, with holdings back to the Dutch period. A Family Research section links to research guidance and an Indian Immigration page; the Indian Immigration page lists 358 ship registers, immigrant certificates (1865-1917), birth registers and letter books. A featured project is the digitisation of immigration records, and the site links to a catalogue and an online immigrant search. The page does not state opening hours, fees or detailed access rules, and I did not test the catalogue.

providers.name: State Library of New South Wales: family history (eresources and guides)
providers.what: The State Library of NSW family history page points to its research guides (convicts before and after arrival, shipping and passenger records, births deaths and marriages, newspapers, a First Nations family history guide) and to a filterable list of family history eresources. The family history subject is split into groups such as convicts, directories, cemeteries, passengers and shipping, military, land and property and UK and Ireland. providers.name: State Library of NSW research guide: Convicts, life in the colony
providers.what: A research guide for tracing a convict after arrival in New South Wales: work assignments, gaol records, families, re-offending, illness and death, and settlements that were once part of NSW. It names the indexes the Library holds, with years: the index to colonial convict movements 1827-1853 (about 10,000 convicts, on CD-ROM and used at the Family history desk in the Library only), colonial secretary's correspondence 1826-1894, an index to the Female Factory at Parramatta 1826-1848, convict marriage banns 1826-1841, free passengers and crew on convict ships 1830-1840, orphan school records 1817-1833, applications to bring out families 1827-1873, NSW probate index 1800-1985, bench book and employer register indexes, and inquest reports. Each resource is marked on the guide with an icon for free online, Library member login or visit-only, but the page text did not say which icon belongs to which index. I did not open the individual index pages.

providers.name: State Library of NSW research guide: Convicts, bound for Australia
providers.what: A research guide to records made before a convict reached Australia: trials and courts, prisons and hulks, the voyage out, and the First and Second Fleets. It lists dated resource pages such as convict arrivals 1788-1842, probationary convicts to Sydney and Moreton Bay 1849-1850, assize courts 1775-1853, criminal entry books and registers (HO 13, HO 25, HO 27, HO 26) between 1786 and 1871, quarter sessions records 1723-1878, Old Bailey session records 1815-1849, petitions for mercy 1784-1830, prison commission books 1816-1866, hulk registers 1802-1849, transportation lists 1829-1840, musters 1790-1849 and surgeons' journals 1816-1856. Many are UK series seen through the Australian Joint Copying Project microfilm or online indexes. The page uses icons for free, member login or visit-only access, but the text did not map them to resources. I read only the guide's landing page.

providers.name: State Library of NSW research guide: Shipping and passenger records
providers.what: A guide to finding people who arrived in Australia, with sections for assisted passengers, unassisted passengers and crew, plus ships' logs and diaries, shipping movements and ship pictures. The guide marks each resource as free online, member login or visit-only, but the page text did not say which is which. I read the landing page, not the sub-pages.

providers.name: State Library of NSW: NSW First Nations family history research guide
providers.what: A guide written by First Nations staff for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people tracing family in NSW, starting with talking to family and a downloadable template. The page carries a cultural-safety note about family separation. I did not open the named resources.

Entries from the microfilm years are marked as not fully accurate and extra details such as maiden names are being added over time. providers.what: A guide to the surviving records of the Royal Derwent Hospital (formed in 1968 from Lachlan Park and Millbrook Rise, closed in 2000) and its predecessors. providers.name: Libraries Tasmania: schools and education records guide

providers.name: Libraries Tasmania: Tasmanian Aboriginal descent research guide

It says records generally begin in the early 1900s so a researcher must trace the family back to someone born around then, that early archival records identify people as Aboriginal mostly in the first decades of colonisation, and that later records usually do not state race except for those about the Bass Strait Islands. It points to the Names Index, Tasmanian Archives search, catalogue and a combined search. The State Archivist may issue a statement of lineage based on Library and Archives holdings through a research enquiry form. The page says it covers documented records and does not verify oral histories. I did not open the records.

providers.name: Library and Archives NT: search tools and family history

A third-party guide in search results says there is no searchable NT births, deaths and marriages index online; I did not verify that. I did not open the catalogue or Archives Navigator.

providers.name: Public Record Office Victoria (PROV)
providers.what: The Victorian state government archive, based at the Victorian Archives Centre in North Melbourne. Its Online collections page lists series that have been digitised, grouped by topic: inquest deposition files (1840-1985), assisted, unassisted, coastal and outwards passenger lists (1839-1923), prison registers and indexes (1847-1948), divorce files, rate books, Melbourne cemetery burial records (1866-1917), teacher and school records, ward-of-the-state registers, wills and probate. The page says that digitised items show as a thumbnail in catalogue results when filtered to online, and that records not digitised are ordered to the reading room. providers.name: PROV Wills and Probate index (Public Record Office Victoria)

providers.name: PROV Unassisted Passenger Lists index 1852-1923 (inward overseas arrivals to Victoria)

providers.name: NSW State Archives Collection (Museums of History NSW)
providers.what: The New South Wales government archive, now run by Museums of History NSW, with a reading room at Kingswood in western Sydney. The collection page says it documents NSW Government work from 1788 and lists popular subjects such as convicts, immigration and shipping, inquests, probate and wills, schools, land and the Colonial Secretary. Its Subjects A-Z pages list online indexes, guides and webinars, and an index search covers all indexes at once through the catalogue. Indexes featured on the front page are the Assisted Immigrants index (1839-1896), the Convicts index (1791-1873), the 1841 census index and a gaol inmates and prisoner photos index (c. 1870-1930). The older records.nsw.gov.au address now sits behind the Museums of History NSW site. I did not test the catalogue or the reading room booking.

Neighbouring indexes on the same site cover convict assignments (1821-1825), convict exiles (1849-1850), applications to marry (1825-1851), indent entries (1788-1801) and the Parramatta Female Factory (1819-1829). providers.name: Ryerson Index (Australian death notices)

The page says searching is free and the site is supported by advertising. I read the home page only and did not run a search.

providers.name: Convict Records (convictrecords.com.au)

A convict entry is structured into personal information (names, dates, occupation, aliases), the offence, court and sentence, and the voyage (ship and dates). A search box takes convict names, ship names or crimes. Contributing needs registration; photo and document uploads, messaging and Excel export are stated to need a paid supporter subscription. providers.name: Pacific Manuscripts Bureau (Australian National University)

That last series copied Catholic mission records for Fiji and Rotuma, New Caledonia, Wallis and Futuna, Tonga, Samoa and Tokelau, Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands onto 398 reels, with a published guide. providers.name: New Zealand Births, Deaths and Marriages Historical Records (Department of Internal Affairs)
providers.what: The New Zealand Government site for searching and ordering historical birth, death and marriage records. providers.name: Library and Archives Canada: Personnel Records of the First World War
providers.what: The guide describes the service-file database for 1914 to 1918. It lists about 622,000 Canadian Expeditionary Force files, about 8,800 Non-Permanent Active Militia files, about 6,700 Royal Newfoundland Regiment and Forestry Corps files, about 3,280 files of volunteers rejected at Valcartier, and about 16,800 Imperial War Service Gratuity case files. providers.name: Library and Archives Canada: Home Children records
providers.what: A research guide to the records of the more than 100,000 children sent from the British Isles to Canada from 1869 to the late 1930s. It explains how to search by surname, with wildcards, ship names written without 'S.S.', and the RG76 advanced search. Some records are digitised in Collection Search, microfilm images are on the partner site Heritage, and some issues of Ups and Downs for 1895 to 1903 are on Canadiana; other series need an on-site visit or a copy order and the Middlemore files need a donor-restriction access form. providers.name: Library and Archives Canada: Citizenship and naturalization records
providers.what: The guide describes three groups: naturalization records for Upper Canada and Canada West (1828 to 1850, 2,967 individuals in 188 registers, on microfilm reels), citizenship registration records of the Montreal Circuit Court (1851 to 1945, 8,437 files) and the naturalization lists of 1915 to 1951, which the page says are digitised and indexed by name. The lists give names and certificate numbers only; the full naturalization files are held by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada. A link to a Heritage microfilm reel is given for the early registers. The citizenship database address is not given on the page and the Collection Search site was gated, so no search was tested.
providers.triageNote: Read the Library and Archives Canada research-guide page on canada.ca on 2026-11-08. The linked Collection Search address (recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca) answered with a Cloudflare challenge page and was not opened or worked around, so search screens, result lists and image viewers were not tested.

providers.name: Library and Archives Canada: Birth, marriage and death records and indexes
providers.what: A guide stating that LAC holds only a small collection of birth, marriage and death material and that civil registration is a provincial or territorial matter. What it does hold, per the page: a few parish and synagogue registers, marriage bonds and licences for Upper and Lower Canada (1779 to 1858, some digitised), card indexes such as the Fabien collection and the Loiselle file, index cards for Red River (Kipling collection), Ontario and Quebec (Gravelle index) and Leeds County, and an index of about 15,000 Parliamentary divorces (1841 to 1968). It names a few other holders, for instance the Yukon Archives for Yukon marriage licence applications and the Centre du patrimoine in Saint-Boniface for Red River parish registers. Useful as a map of where to look; the databases were not opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the canada.ca guide page on 2026-11-08; no database opened.

providers.name: Library and Archives Canada: Metis Nation genealogy research guide
providers.what: A guide to Metis family history sources, mostly Red River (Manitoba) with some for Alberta and Saskatchewan. It covers censuses (including partial Red River censuses of 1831 to 1856 and the 1906, 1916 and 1926 prairie censuses), Metis scrip certificates issued from the 1870s (with Index Book I for North-West Territories applications), river-lot maps showing Red River owners, school files, and military service files. It advises searching 'dit' names, expecting spelling variation, and using terms such as 'M.R.R.' and the 1869-70 and 1885 resistances. Some items are digitised in Collection Search and some microfilm on Heritage; the page does not say which scrip records are digitised. Collection Search was bot-gated and not opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the Library and Archives Canada research-guide page on canada.ca on 2026-11-08. The linked Collection Search address (recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca) answered with a Cloudflare challenge page and was not opened or worked around, so search screens, result lists and image viewers were not tested.

providers.name: Library and Archives Canada: First Nations genealogy research guide
providers.what: A guide to First Nations family-history sources, centred on the Indian Affairs records (RG10). It describes census returns, band history cards (consulted by staff because they are restricted), pre-1951 membership lists, the 1951 posted lists and Indian Registers 1951 to 1984 (restricted), enfranchisement files, treaty annuity paylists (1850 to 1982) and interest distribution paylists (1856 to 1982) arranged by treaty, estates and wills, school records and annual reports (1864 to 1990). Finding aids are named for locating them. The page says records after 1909 in the paylists are restricted under the Privacy Act and that some items are digitised in Collection Search or on Heritage; other items need an on-site visit or a copy order. Collection Search was bot-gated and not opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the Library and Archives Canada research-guide page on canada.ca on 2026-11-08. The linked Collection Search address (recherche-collection-search.bac-lac.gc.ca) answered with a Cloudflare challenge page and was not opened or worked around, so search screens, result lists and image viewers were not tested.

providers.name: Heritage: digitised LAC microfilm (Canadiana)
providers.what: A ten-year digitisation project run with LAC and Canadiana to put popular archival microfilm online, about 37.5 million pages according to its home page. Material is grouped into Genealogy, Indigenous History, Government Documents, Military History and Landmark Papers (private papers), covering the 1600s to the mid-1900s. The home page offers a search box and a help page for search tips; LAC's guides link into it by reel number (for example Home Children inspection reports, Upper Canada naturalisation registers). The home page does not state pricing or licence terms, and no search or page viewer was tested.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 2026-11-08 only; did not test search or the viewer.

providers.name: Canadiana: Canadian Research Knowledge Network digital collection
providers.what: A digital collection run by the Canadian Research Knowledge Network. The home page lists monographs spanning about three and a half centuries, serials (dailies, weeklies, journals, city directories, annual reports of churches, schools and corporations), more than 1.7 million pages of pre-1920 colonial, provincial and federal government publications, and nearly 22,000 topographic maps (1905 to 2012). There is a search box with search tips, collection browsing and an English or French interface. It carries a warning that some historical content contains harmful language. Free or paid access is not stated on the home page and no search was run.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 2026-11-08 only; terms of service not read; search not tested.

providers.name: Archives Canada (Canadian Council of Archives portal)
providers.what: The national archival portal kept by the Canadian Council of Archives with the provincial and territorial councils, member archives and LAC. The home page calls it a gateway and links under several labels to an Access to Memory search at archivescanada.accesstomemory.ca for archival holdings and for finding archives across Canada. The home page does not describe the search features, and the search itself was not opened.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 2026-11-08; the AtoM search was not opened.

providers.name: BC Archives Genealogy Database (Royal BC Museum)
providers.what: The search page for BC Archives' indexes of vital records. It lists births 1854 to 1904, marriages 1871 to 1950, deaths 1872 to 2005, colonial marriages 1859 to 1872 and baptisms 1836 to 1888. You can filter by event type, names, gender, age at death, place, registration number and date range, with * wildcards and a keyword option; baptism searches add parents, denomination and church. Some entries show a BC Archives microfilm number for ordering copies; entries without one are directed to Vital Statistics. The page says indexes and images are for private archival and historical research, and that Vital Statistics sends new data to the Archives each year. I did not run a search or open an image.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page 2026-11-08; did not run a search or open an image, so image access is untested.

providers.name: BC Archives (Royal BC Museum)
providers.what: The provincial archive of British Columbia at 675 Belleville Street, Victoria. Its home page names three online databases: the BC Archives Collection (descriptions of records, with digital versions where available), the Archives Library Collection (books, directories, pamphlets, government reports) and the Genealogy Database of open birth, marriage and death registrations with many digitised images. It describes government, private, genealogical and Indigenous records and a library on British Columbia and the Pacific Northwest. The page says the archive is moving to a new campus in Colwood and closes for the move from 22 November 2026; visits are by appointment or open hours, with copies ordered by form. Only the home page was read.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 2026-11-08; the catalogue was not searched.

providers.name: Nova Scotia Archives
providers.what: The provincial archive of Nova Scotia, in Halifax. Its home page lists online Births, Marriages and Deaths, digitised newspapers, a Virtual Archives and Databases section, the MemoryNS catalogue, an archives search and a library catalogue; the reading room is at 6016 University Avenue. The Virtual Archives directory names searchable church records and cemetery records, census, assessment and poll tax records (1767 to 1838), divorce case files (1759 to 1960), land papers (1765 to 1800), Cape Breton petitions, Acadian deportation records and a Halifax Explosion list. The home page does not say whether the online databases are free. Several of these have their own rows.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the Virtual Archives directory 2026-11-08; the individual databases listed there were not each opened.

providers.name: Nova Scotia Archives: Nova Scotia Births, Marriages and Deaths
providers.what: A name search of historical Nova Scotia civil registration, about one million names. The page lists births 1864 to 1877 (with delayed registrations 1830 to 1924) and 1908 to 1924, marriage bonds 1763 to 1864 and registrations 1864 to 1949, and deaths 1864 to 1877, Halifax 1890 to 1908 and 1908 to 1974. It says births between 1877 and October 1908 were not recorded by the government. Search is by first name, last name and county with contains, starts-with, ends-with or exact matching and a year range, plus an advanced bride and groom search. The page states that each name links to a digitised original that can be viewed and downloaded at no charge; later records are held by Service Nova Scotia. I did not run a search or open an image.
providers.triageNote: Read the description page 2026-11-08; no search run and no image opened, so the no-charge statement is the page's, not tested.

providers.name: Nova Scotia Archives: digitised newspapers
providers.what: A set of digitised Nova Scotia newspapers, 175,000 pages in total according to the page. It lists about twenty titles from 1769 to 2002, including the Acadian Recorder (1813 to 1853), Liverpool Transcript (1854 to 1867), Eastern Chronicle (1867 to 1888), Gaelic papers of the 1920s and 1930s, Le Courrier de la Nouvelle-Ecosse (1937 to 2002) and several twentieth-century community papers. Issues are browsed title by title and by year and month, and the page says they can be viewed online at no cost. Microfilm for further years is held at the Archives, and some issues are held by other institutions. Some titles are only partly digitised. No issue was opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the listing page 2026-11-08; no issue opened and full-text search not tested.

providers.name: Nova Scotia Archives: Church Records
providers.what: A searchable finding aid to the Archives' microfilm of church registers, over 900 reels covering 512 parishes and congregations. The registers are mainly baptisms, marriages and burials, most between 1780 and 1920, with a very brief earliest entry from 1679. The database is for checking which churches are covered, whether the dates suit, and which reel numbers to request; the microfilm itself is consulted on site. The page does not say that register images are online. A guide with FAQs and a list of regional church archives are linked. I did not search the database.
providers.triageNote: Read the description page 2026-11-08; the database search was not run.

providers.name: Nova Scotia Archives: Cemetery Records
providers.what: A database of transcriptions of gravestone inscriptions held by the Archives, for more than 2,000 cemeteries and burial grounds. The lists are handwritten, typed or computer-made, sometimes with maps or plot plans, and nearly all have been microfilmed for use on site. The search is by community, county or cemetery or church name, and the page tells users that coverage is uneven and transcription quality varies, with many cemeteries surveyed more than once. It helps pick reel numbers to request. The page does not say that photographs or name-level entries are online. Not searched.
providers.triageNote: Read the description page 2026-11-08; search not run.

providers.name: Archives of Manitoba
providers.what: The provincial archive of Manitoba, which also houses the Hudson's Bay Company Archives. The page points to the Keystone descriptive database for archival descriptions, a research room with ordering of records from off-site storage, remote research, copying and a microfilm loan and purchase programme. Under genealogy-related records it lists Manitoba estate files, a Winnipeg divorce file index (1917 to 1984), a First World War index and extracts of Red River Settlement baptisms, marriages and burials. The page does not mention vital statistics. Only this overview page was read.
providers.triageNote: Read the overview page 2026-11-08; Keystone and the indexes were not opened.

providers.name: Hudson's Bay Company Archives (Archives of Manitoba)
providers.what: The archive of the Hudson's Bay Company and related fur-trade bodies, held within the Archives of Manitoba. The page says it holds company records and those of subsidiaries such as the North West Company, plus private papers, and that digitised microfilm covers over 10,000 volumes of pre-1870 records from nearly 500 posts. Finding aids include biographical sheets, name indexes (Indigenous names, servants' contracts, Northern Department engagement registers, proprietors' wills, North West Company account books and contracts, Red River Settlement baptism, marriage and burial extracts), post maps and ship histories. Searching is through the Keystone database. Staff do very limited research for inquiries, so the page suggests hiring a researcher for in-depth work. I did not open Keystone or an index.
providers.triageNote: Read the HBCA page 2026-11-08; indexes and Keystone not opened.

providers.name: Provincial Archives of Alberta
providers.what: The provincial archive of Alberta, reading room at 8555 Roper Road, Edmonton. Its home page offers genealogy help, birth, marriage, death and stillbirth indexes, homestead records, newspapers and faith-organisation records, with its holdings searchable in an Access to Memory catalogue at searchprovincialarchives.alberta.ca. The indexes page says each entry gives a registration number, place and year needed to request a record, and gives access ages (births 120 years or 50 years after death, marriages 75, deaths 50, stillbirths 75). Original vital statistics records are not viewable in the reading room. I read the home page and the indexes page only; year ranges of the indexes are not stated there.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and BMD indexes page 2026-11-08; did not search the indexes or the AtoM catalogue.

providers.name: Provincial Archives of Alberta: homestead records
providers.what: A guide to Alberta homestead application files held on microfilm. Each file typically gives the applicant's age, birthplace, former residence, entry date and marital status, and may include a naturalisation record. The method on the page: get the legal land description (using the LAC Western Land Grants database or the Alberta Genealogical Society index if only a name is known), find the file number in the reading-room indices, convert it to a reel number with the conversion lists, then view the reel; township maps name original homesteaders. Copies from reader-printers are priced per page. Canadian Pacific Railway land sales are said to be at the Glenbow in Calgary. No microfilm or index was opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the guide 2026-11-08; the reel and index are described as used in the reading room.

providers.name: Alberta Genealogical Society: Alberta Homestead Index
providers.what: A volunteer-transcribed index of Alberta homestead applications: land patents 1885 to 1897, homestead records 1870 to 1930 and homestead records after 1930. The search form takes surname and given name, or the legal land description (section, township, range, meridian) and place name, and returns the Provincial Archives of Alberta reference, microfilm and file numbers. The page states plainly that there are no images in the index. It does not say how many entries it holds or whether online use is free or for members only. Pair it with the Provincial Archives' reel guidance. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Read the index description page 2026-11-08; no search run; fee status not stated.

providers.name: Provincial Archives of Saskatchewan: homestead files (pre-1930 and post-1930)
providers.what: A page on the two homestead file series. The pre-1930 series (S 42) was created by the federal Dominion Lands Branch from 1871 to 1930 and is indexed by name and legal land description, covering applicants, patentees, heirs and people who received Metis or South African scrip; a search tool is linked and about 70,000 pages of files are online, with more being added. The post-1930 series (S 43) comes from the provincial Lands Branch, has an index open to staff only, and is access-restricted. The Archives' home page also says its online catalogue was unavailable at the time. I did not open the search tool.
providers.triageNote: Read the page and the Archives home page 2026-11-08; search tool and images not opened.

providers.name: The Rooms Provincial Archives: genealogy research (Newfoundland and Labrador)
providers.what: The provincial archive of Newfoundland and Labrador, in St. John's, describes its genealogical holdings. Pre-1892 church registers are held with a community index and are searched by archive staff on request, page by page, within five years of a stated date. Civil registration on microfilm covers births 1891 to 1899, marriages 1891 to 1922 and deaths 1891 to 1949; later records come from the provincial Vital Statistics Division. Other sources named include nominal censuses of 1921, 1935 and 1945, All Newfoundland Births (1840 to 1915, finding aid on site only), newspaper notices, voters' lists, Crown land grants and probated wills. The Rooms does not make prints of vital records. The site also lists a deaths database for 1950 to 1968, died-in-service and Royal Naval Reserve databases for the First World War; those were not opened.

at.place: St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada

providers.triageNote: Read the genealogy page and the home page 2026-11-08; the databases were not searched.

providers.name: Northwest Territories Archives
providers.what: The territorial archive of the Northwest Territories at the Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre, Yellowknife. The page says it holds Government of the Northwest Territories records and material from private people and organisations, and points to an online catalogue at gnwt.accesstomemory.org for photos and other records, with ordering of copies. It does not mention genealogy resources or how much is digitised. Only this page was read.
providers.triageNote: Read the page 2026-11-08 (the old address redirects to the territorial education department site); catalogue not opened.

providers.name: Canadian Virtual War Memorial (Veterans Affairs Canada)
providers.what: An online register of more than 118,000 Canadians and Newfoundlanders who died in service since Confederation, tied to the Books of Remembrance (South African War, First and Second World Wars, Newfoundland, Korean War, Merchant Navy, in the service of Canada, and the RCMP). There is a basic search and an advanced search by surname, alternate spelling, given names, force, unit, date of death, service number, age, cemetery and book. A profile typically shows age, service number, dates and force, and some have a photo, headstone image or clipping. The page does not state any fee. I did not search or open a profile.
providers.triageNote: Read the landing page 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: Dictionary of Canadian Biography / Dictionnaire biographique du Canada
providers.what: A bilingual scholarly reference of more than 9,000 biographies of people from across Canada, with a new biography added each week and corrections to earlier ones. It has its own Advanced Search page with Boolean operators and limiters, and entries can also be browsed by category. Entries draw on primary sources, so they are useful to link a family to context, sources and places rather than as a record index. The home page does not state the period covered or whether use is free. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 2026-11-08; search not run.

providers.name: Alex Dworkin Canadian Jewish Archives (Montreal)
providers.what: An archive of the Jewish presence in Quebec and Canada, run as a programme of UIA-Canada and located in uptown Montreal. Collections cover immigration, community organisations, Zionism, human rights, education, literature and genealogy; the major-collections page lists Canadian Jewish Congress records, records of immigrant-aid and colonisation bodies, family and personal papers, over 10,000 personalia clipping files, tens of thousands of photographs and over 4,000 hours of recordings. Series descriptions are searchable in an Access to Memory interface at archivesjuivescanadiennes.ca, and many digitised items are on the Canadian Jewish Heritage Network. Visits are by appointment. The casualties database has moved to the Heritage Network. The Heritage Network site itself could not be read.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and major-collections page 2026-11-08; AtoM interface not opened; cjhn.ca returned 403 to scripted access and was not used.

providers.name: Ontario Genealogical Society (OGS)
providers.what: A member-supported charity for Ontario family history, with 22 branches and special interest groups including British Home Children, Eastern European, Scottish, Irish and Irish-Palatine. Its home page lists TONI (The Ontario Name Index), a cemetery records collection, an Ontario place locator, a master library catalogue, a research request form, a journal and webinars. Members get extra material such as journal back issues and a MyHeritage library edition. The page does not say whether TONI or the cemetery collection need membership, and neither was searched.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 2026-11-08; the TONI host answered with a server error, so TONI was not opened.

providers.name: Peel's Prairie Provinces (University of Alberta)
providers.what: A University of Alberta digital collection about the Canadian Prairies. The home page shows newspapers, postcards, maps, books and pamphlets, and featured sets such as Henderson's Directories, a photograph collection and programmes, with items from the 1910s to the 1990s. It has a searchable list of newspaper titles, searchable flip books and a how-to-use guide, and items can also be viewed on the Internet Archive. Terms of use are posted. The home page does not give the full date range or title list, and I did not search it.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21: immigration research resources
providers.what: The museum's research page in Halifax lists a Ship Arrival Database, a Passenger List Database, ordering of ship images, a family history centre, immigration-records FAQ, oral histories and articles on topics such as Home Children and Irish famine migration. The page does not describe what the databases contain, their years or whether they are free, and the individual database pages were not opened. A collection search portal is linked. Treat as a lead to follow rather than a description of a database.
providers.triageNote: Read the research landing page 2026-11-08 only; the databases it names were not opened.

providers.name: City of Toronto Archives
providers.what: The municipal archive of Toronto. Its page links to a searchable database of records, a What's in the Archives section, a What's Online section of exhibits, maps and other records, appointments, copy services, and a donation page. The page does not list particular collections or say how much is digitised. Only this page was read; the database and the online section were not opened.
providers.triageNote: Read the landing page 2026-11-08; nothing deeper opened.

providers.name: BaSIA - Baza Systemu Indeksacji Archiwalnej (Archival Indexing System database, Greater Poland)
providers.what: Volunteer-built search engine for indexed archival records from western Poland (Greater Poland). The home page reports about 7 million entries from over 700 places, drawn from the State Archive in Poznan, the Poznan Archdiocesan Archive and the National Digital Archives, covering Catholic and Protestant parishes and civil registry offices, mostly 18th to 20th century. Entries are births/baptisms, marriages, deaths and banns, and some link to scans on szukajwarchiwach.gov.pl. Search takes a name with an adjustable similarity percentage, year ranges and a place with a radius; an advanced form filters by role, document type and date added. The site states the search engine is and will remain free; a free account adds e-mail alerts for chosen surnames and a clipboard. I did not run a search or open any linked scan.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English home page on 2026-11-08 and read the description of coverage, search options and account benefits. Did not run a search or test scan links.

providers.name: Skanoteka - baza skanow dokumentow o wartosci genealogicznej (Polish Genealogical Society scan database)
providers.what: Database of scanned documents of genealogical value run by the Polish Genealogical Society (PTG). The home page quotes about 18.5 million images and sorts them into church registers, court books, registration (meldunkowe) records, notarial records and other documents, drawn from archives, parish offices and civil registry offices; recent additions include land registry and cadastral files and some school and military records. You can use a search box, optionally reaching into individual units, browse by archive, or search the tags that volunteers add, and there is a how-to-search page. The page does not say whether viewing needs an account, and I did not open a scan.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the collection categories and search options. Did not search, log in or open scans, so account requirements are unknown.

providers.name: Katalog Zasobow Metrykalnych (PTG catalogue of parish record holdings, Poland)
providers.what: Polish Genealogical Society catalogue of parish record holdings, copyright shown 2010-2026. The page is a navigation shell: you can look up a parish by name (with an exact-match option) or browse a map by voivodeship or by Catholic diocese, and there is an information section about the catalogue. The home page does not itself describe which registers, years or archives a parish entry lists, nor whether use is free, so it is best treated as a finding aid for locating where a parish's books are kept. I did not open a parish entry.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. It is a thin shell; did not open any parish record or the information page.

providers.name: Geneszukacz (surname search across Polish Genealogical Society indexes)
providers.what: Single surname search form that fans out to several Polish Genealogical Society indexes. The page lists Geneteka (birth, marriage and death index entries, with region links including Ukraine and Lithuania), the 1941 Polish Declaration of Admiration and Friendship for the United States, losses of soldiers 1918-1920 and an index of Polish Army soldiers 1918-1920; the combined total shown is about 68.5 million entries. You type a surname, optionally a from/to year and an exact-search tick, and the form passes you to the relevant database. It is a gateway rather than a record source; the existing Atlas row for Geneteka covers the main index. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page on 2026-11-08 and read the list of indexes and counts. Did not submit a search, so how results display and any limits are untested.

providers.name: Poznan Project (19th-century marriage index of historical Greater Poland)
providers.what: Volunteer indexing project, running since 2000, for marriages in historical Wielkopolska (Greater Poland) between 1800 and 1899. The site says it holds over a million records, roughly three quarters of the marriages of the period, and you can filter by Catholic, Evangelical or civil registry records. Simple search uses a surname with a similarity setting; the extended search takes one or both spouses, given names, mothers' surnames, a date range and record type, and results can be saved to a cart and exported as a GEDCOM file. A map can limit the search area. The page mentions a login but gives no price, and I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the scope, search and GEDCOM options. Did not search or log in; cost and account requirements are not stated on the page.

providers.name: JRI-Poland - Jewish Records Indexing Poland (Preserving Jewish Records of Poland)
providers.what: Volunteer-run US non-profit that indexes surviving Jewish vital and other records from Poland. The home page quotes about 6.4 million records, 2.5 million images and 1,902 towns and settlements, and describes more than 250 years of coverage without giving a firm year range. Two search versions are linked, a legacy one described as fully functional and a NextGen one with a limited test data set; results are grouped by town, and the site also offers a Town Explorer, Project Explorer and a community forum. Search results ask the visitor to log in or create a free account to continue, and some extra tools are for paying members. I did not log in or run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. The page says a free account is needed to continue past the search results; membership prices were not shown. Did not create an account or search.

providers.name: Indeks Represjonowanych (Index of Repressed Persons, IPN / Osrodek KARTA)
providers.what: Research programme and public online database of people repressed by the Soviet authorities after the occupation of eastern Poland on 17 September 1939 (imprisoned, sent to labour camps or exiled inside the USSR). Begun by the Archiwum Wschodnie and Fundacja Osrodka KARTA and run since 2013 by the Institute of National Remembrance (IPN). The page says the public database has over 316,000 records, including entries from published volumes, lists such as the 1940 executions in Ukraine and NKVD investigation records for western Ukraine and Belarus 1939-1941; an internal database is larger. Data comes from questionnaires filled in by victims or families, Polish archives and the Moscow Memorial society. I read the history and scope on the home page but did not run a search or open a record.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the description of the programme and database size. Did not run a search; the page points enquiries to the IPN by e-mail and phone.

providers.name: Polish Genealogical Society of America (PGSA)
providers.what: US society for Polish family history. The home page links surname databases for the USA, Poland, Lithuania, Ukraine, Russia and Belarus, plus sections on research sources, education, research services and downloads of the Rodziny journal. There is a members area, a shop for books and CDs, an events calendar and a free monthly e-newsletter; a Massachusetts chapter is listed. I did not open the individual databases, so I cannot say what each holds or what is free to non-members.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 only; did not open any database or the members area.

providers.name: Gesher Galicia (Jewish research on Galicia, Poland and Ukraine)
providers.what: Non-profit for Jewish genealogical and historical research on Galicia, the former Austro-Hungarian province now split between south-east Poland and western Ukraine. The home page lists the All Galicia Database (over 500,000 records), searchable record inventories from Polish, Ukrainian and other archives, a map room with zoomable cadastral and regional maps, and a knowledge base with guides to archives such as AGAD in Warsaw and the Przemysl State Archive. Projects named include 1940-1941 vital records and a Holocaust project, and the society publishes a quarterly journal. Membership is shown from 50 US dollars a year and the site says some content is for logged-in members only, without saying which databases are free. I did not open the databases.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open databases or log in, so the free/member split is unknown.

providers.name: Archiwum Panstwowe w Katowicach (State Archive in Katowice, with branches)
providers.what: Silesian state archive with reading rooms at Katowice and branches at Bielsko-Biala, Cieszyn, Gliwice and Raciborz. The site has menus for online collections, a link to the national Szukaj w Archiwach portal, its own advanced search, rules for access to holdings, certified copies and extracts, and personnel and payroll records. An online exhibition on passports from the Olkusz county office was featured. The home page does not describe parish or civil registers, so the specific series held need to be checked on the archive's holdings pages. I read the home page only, including notices about reading-room closures dated autumn 2026.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the online collections or holdings pages, so register series and years are unverified.

providers.name: Archiwum Panstwowe w Poznaniu (State Archive in Poznan)
providers.what: State archive for Greater Poland. The home page reports 66,761 new scans in the third quarter of 2026 published through the Szukaj w Archiwach service, including a landed-estate collection and civil status office files from Nekla and Nowe Miasto nad Warta. It has a reading-room section with a note that some holdings are stored in Bydgoszcz and are fetched in monthly batches when requested by the end of the previous month, a family archives section and personnel/payroll records pages with a databases page. Parish registers are not mentioned on the home page. I read the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the reading-room, databases or scan pages.

providers.name: Archiwum Panstwowe w Gdansku (State Archive in Gdansk)
providers.what: State archive for the Gdansk area, with a reading room in Gdansk, a Gdynia branch under construction and, since March 2024, the former Malbork archive, whose reading room still operates by booking. The home page says over a million documents are online on Szukaj w Archiwach, including metrical and civil-status records, plus more than 85,000 scans of Gdansk city records from the 15th to 18th centuries. It also runs a youth genealogy contest with a consultation line. The Gdansk reading room had temporary reduced opening hours in 2026. I read the home page only and did not check which parishes or years the metrical records cover.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the scans on Szukaj w Archiwach, so coverage of the metrical records is unverified.

providers.name: Zydowski Instytut Historyczny (Jewish Historical Institute, Warsaw)
providers.what: Warsaw institute for the history of Polish Jews with an archive, library, online collection and a genealogy department. The English home page lists exhibitions, the Ringelblum Archive and an education programme; its genealogy page describes help with finding ancestors, a guide to the history of Jewish surnames, confirmation of Polish citizenship and a contact route to the Genealogy Department. The page does not say what databases the institute offers, how a request is submitted or what it costs. I read the home page and the genealogy page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English home page and genealogy page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the subpages on searching for roots or the online collection.

providers.name: Narodowe Archiwum Cyfrowe (National Digital Archives, Poland)
providers.what: Polish national archive for photographs, film and sound, and a major source of scans behind the national Szukaj w Archiwach portal, which the home page advertises as millions of scans in one service. The site has a holdings section with access rules and a footer link to a register of places that keep employers' personnel and payroll records. The home page does not describe genealogy services or give holdings details, so I cannot say what family-relevant series exist. I read the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the holdings or access-rules pages.

providers.name: Archiwum Akt Nowych (Central Archives of Modern Records, Warsaw)
providers.what: Warsaw archive for modern Polish state, party and private records. The home page has a holdings section with a list of record groups, a users section covering access rules, price list, ordering scans and loans, online exhibitions, and links to the Szukaj w Archiwach portal and thematic projects on independence, the Riga Treaty and wartime Warsaw. A notice from May 2026 reports customer service at the front office temporarily suspended. I read the home page only and did not check what person-level series exist.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the record group list or user pages.

providers.name: Slaska Biblioteka Cyfrowa (Silesian Digital Library)
providers.what: Regional digital library built on dLibra, with Polish, German and English interfaces. Collections named on the page are Lower Silesia, Upper Silesia, a maritime collection, the Eastern Borderlands (Kresy) and Lusatia, with browse lists by title, author, subject and publisher and separate lists of periodicals, bibliographies and official publications. The project is co-financed by the EU under the Silesian regional programme. The page does not mention genealogy or state whether access is free, and I did not open any item.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open any periodical or test full-text access.

providers.name: Malopolska Biblioteka Cyfrowa (Malopolska Digital Library, Krakow)
providers.what: Digital library run by the provincial public library in Krakow. The page lists cultural heritage, science and education, regional materials, periodicals and special collections, and says the collection is moving to a new platform at this address while the complete collection stays on the current site. A news item notes digitised cemetery books of the Krakow municipal cemetery administration, with records of the deceased and indexes of personal data, and a Podhale library with literature, periodicals and photographs. The page does not state whether access is free and I did not open the cemetery books.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the cemetery books or confirm years covered.

providers.name: Grobonet (search engine for people buried in Poland)
providers.what: Commercial search engine for graves in Polish cemeteries, claiming the largest database of people buried in Poland (7.6 million people on the day read). It draws on local cemetery systems and shows cemetery, sector, row and grave number, birth and death years and sometimes a headstone photo. You search by first and last name, or by surname plus a voivodeship or city; there are minimum letter counts, and a cemetery map, recent burials, obituaries and links to cemetery sites are offered. The page mentions a fee regulation and paid extras, but does not say whether the grave search itself is free. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not search or open the fee regulation, so whether searching is free is unknown.

providers.name: Narodni archiv (National Archives of the Czech Republic)
providers.what: Czech national archive in Prague with research rooms at Chodovec (collections from 1850 onward) and Dejvice (mainly up to 1850). The English page lists online resources including military conscriptions 1850-1918, registers of Jewish religious communities from 1784 to 1949, books of Jewish familiants, land files and political trials of the 1950s, plus application forms for census and citizenship data and Jewish settlement plans. It points to a national archives portal (portal.nacr.cz) and a national digital reading room, and says inventories of processed fonds are at digitalnibadatelna.nacr.cz. The page does not explain how each search works and I did not open them.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English page on 2026-11-08 and read the list of online resources. Did not open the portals or test any search.

providers.name: Moravsky zemsky archiv v Brne (Moravian Land Archive, Brno)
providers.what: Moravian archive in Brno.
