The home page has an online archive area with the ARON catalogue, a portal of archival fonds and collections, and digital collections including ActaPublica, census enumeration sheets (scitaci operaty), cadastral sketches (indikacni skici), urbaria and Monasterium. A reading room has study rules, a fee schedule and online booking. The page also lists digitised finding aids for the Brno-venkov district archive, among them parish and deanery office fonds, but does not say they are digitised registers. The existing Atlas row for Acta Publica covers the parish-register viewer; this row is for the institution and its other catalogues.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open ARON or the census sheets, so coverage and access are unverified.

providers.name: Zidovske muzeum v Praze - archiv a online sbirky (Jewish Museum in Prague, archive and online collections)
providers.what: Prague museum with an archive, library, photo archive and online catalogue at collections.jewishmuseum.cz. The Czech-language home page lists archival fonds including Holocaust documentation, witness testimonies, documentation of Jewish communities, rare prints and manuscripts, plus research projects and a provenance programme. The page does not mention genealogy services, opening times for the archive or how to request material, so it is a lead rather than a confirmed family-history source. I read the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the online catalogue or the archive pages.

providers.name: CEMETERY.sk - Virtualne cintoriny Slovenska (Virtual Cemeteries of Slovakia)
providers.what: Company-run website of Slovak cemetery records, with 162,758 entries and a last-updated date of 9 February 2018 on the day read. You can search for a grave by last name with an extended search option, browse a list of cemeteries and famous persons, and users can add graves through a form. The site also carries funeral-service, stonecutter and genealogy listings. The age of the last update suggests it may be incomplete or stale; I did not run a search or check which cemeteries are covered.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English home page on 2026-11-08. Did not run a search. Last update date shown was 2018.

providers.name: Statne archivy Slovenskej republiky (state archives of Slovakia, Ministry of the Interior list)
providers.what: Ministry of the Interior page listing the Slovak archive network: the Slovak National Archive (with the Slovak Mining Archive), and state archives at Banska Bystrica, Bratislava, Zilina (seat Bytca), Kosice, Nitra, Trencin, Trnava and Presov (including the Spis archive in Levoca), each with named workplaces in smaller towns, plus the Kosice city archive and specialised archives. Online items named are the Elektronicky archiv Slovenska, a list of fonds and collections in the state archives, archival standards and the heraldic register. The page does not mention church registers or digitised holdings, so use it to find the right archive rather than for records.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08 and read the list of archives and online links. Did not open the Elektronicky archiv or the fonds list.

providers.name: JewishGen Hungary Database
providers.what: JewishGen database of more than 1.7 million records for present and former Hungarian territory, including Hungary, Slovakia, Croatia, northern Serbia, north-western Romania and Subcarpathian Ukraine, supplied by the Hungarian Special Interest Group and individual donors. Search by surname, given name, town or any field, with phonetic, exact, starts-with and several fuzzy-match options. The page says multi-field searches need a donation of 180 US dollars or more to the JewishGen General Fund. The list of individual databases failed to load when I read the page. The Atlas already has a general JewishGen row; this one is the Hungary index.
providers.triageNote: Opened the page on 2026-11-08. The individual-database list did not load, so the contents are described only from the introduction. Did not search.

providers.name: Budapest Fovaros Leveltara (Budapest City Archives)
providers.what: City archive of Budapest. Its online section lists a holdings registry on eleveltar.hu with the archive pre-selected, its own searchable databases on a separate page, the Budapest Time Machine project on Hungaricana, an archival glossary and thematic pages including the siege of Budapest. The page names parish and civil registers and family-tree research among its general topics and gives research-desk telephone lines and opening days. How the databases search and what they contain was not visible on the home page, and I did not open them.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. The www host has a certificate mismatch, so I used the bare domain. Did not open the databases page.

providers.name: Siebenbuergen-Institut (Transylvanian Saxon library, archive and genealogy section)
providers.what: Institute for Transylvanian Saxon studies, shown on its page as part of Heidelberg University. It runs the Siebenbuergische Bibliothek with an online catalogue, an archive including a picture and sound archive and literary estates, and the genealogy section of the Transylvanian Saxon regional studies working group, with a catalogue of its genealogical archive, the journal Siebenbuerger Familienforschung, obituaries and working files. Full-text publications and an image archive are hosted on subsites. The library and archive have usage and fee regulations that I did not read. I opened the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the genealogy catalogue or the regulations. Location taken from general knowledge of the institute's seat, not from the page.

providers.name: Germans from Russia Heritage Collection (North Dakota State University)
providers.what: University library collection on Germans from Russia, in Fargo. The page lists photograph collections, oral histories and exhibits, search tools (finding aids, library catalogue, Digital Horizons) and research areas for genealogy, the history of Germans from Russia including villages, maps and Volga German history, and translation resources. Visits are by appointment through an online form. The page does not describe each search tool or any indexes in detail, and I did not open them.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the finding aids or genealogy pages.

providers.name: Ex-Yu Genealogy (sources for post-Yugoslav family history)
providers.what: Blog-style guide, begun in 2012 in Serbo-Croatian and now with more English, to genealogical research in the former Yugoslavia: Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro, Kosovo and North Macedonia. Sections are getting started, family names and lineages, church records and archives, census lists and war records, and research tools and links. The Croatian archives page I read lists the Croatian State Archives, the ARHiNET parish-register search, a FamilySearch collection of microfilmed registers and the website addresses of each regional state archive, with advice on preparing a visit. I did not open the pages for other countries.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the Croatia archives page on 2026-11-08. Did not open pages for the other countries.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv u Osijeku (State Archives in Osijek)
providers.what: State archive for the Osijek area of Slavonia. The home page has a digitised-materials section listing photographs and postcards and a digitised 1905 estate file, plus digitised publications; a guide to fonds and collections and finding aids are linked, and a use-of-holdings section has reading-room rules, a fee schedule of 2022 and request forms. The page does not mention parish or civil registers or genealogy and shows no search tool, so what registers exist and how to ask for them must be taken up with the archive. I read the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the guide to fonds, so register holdings are unverified.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv u Splitu (State Archives in Split)
providers.what: State archive for the Split area of Dalmatia. The home page offers request forms for extracts of birth, marriage and death register data, cadastral data, school records and work-history records, a registry of fonds and collections with finding aids, a digitised-holdings section and a link to HAiS, the Croatian archival information system. The reading room is open on weekdays and records must be ordered a day ahead, with an urgent surcharge. The page does not give years or parishes for the registers, and I did not open the digitised material or HAiS.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the digitised holdings or HAiS.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv u Bjelovaru (State Archives in Bjelovar)
providers.what: State archive for the Bjelovar area. The holdings page says the archive keeps parish registers of Roman Catholic, Greek Catholic, Orthodox, Jewish and Evangelical communities, mostly baptisms, marriages and deaths, plus Orthodox duplicate registers from 1858 to 1946. State civil registers after 1946 are kept by the registry offices, not the archive. PDFs updated 10 June 2024 list the registers in its area and where each one now is, one per denomination, and the whole collection is said to be microfilmed at the Croatian State Archives and partly digitised. The page points to the national eArhiv catalogue of over 20,000 fonds. I read this page only and did not open the PDFs.
providers.triageNote: Opened the fonds and collections page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the register-list PDFs or the eArhiv catalogue.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv u Sisku (State Archives in Sisak)
providers.what: State archive for the Sisak area, with a branch at Petrinja. The home page has sections on the registry books it holds, their availability and use, and an e-database of registry books from the Sisak archival area that reports 1,631 books. A family-tree research service is listed under services, a register of fonds and collections is available, and digital collections and a virtual exhibition on early Sisak photographers are linked, as is HAiS. The page did not show the database fields or the years it covers, and I did not open the database.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 and read the section headings and database size. Did not open the registry book database, so its years and fields are unverified.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv u Varazdinu (State Archives in Varazdin)
providers.what: State archive for Varazdin county with collection centres in Koprivnica and Krapina. The site's registers section lists Roman Catholic parish registers, Serbian Orthodox registers, Jewish community registers, Evangelical registers and civil registers, and a digitised-holdings section is linked. Further pages cover use of holdings, how to submit a request and the fee schedule. A 2026 news item reports a renovated archive building opened in May. Parish-level coverage, date ranges and search tools were not shown on the pages I read, and I did not open the digitised holdings.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08 (two reads, one returned only the news). Did not open the registers section itself or digitised holdings.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv u Slavonskom Brodu (State Archives in Slavonski Brod) and its Digitalni arhiv
providers.what: State archive for Slavonski Brod, with a registry-books section, an overview of fonds and collections, finding aids, request forms and a fee schedule. It runs a Digital Archive at arhiv.dasb.hr, an online repository of scanned or photographed items browsable by fonds, collections and other, with a search over all items. The digital archive page says the archive holds 1,030 fonds, the oldest from 1725, and that only a small part is online; it does not say whether registry-book scans are included. Reuse needs the archive's approval and citations must name the fonds and unit. I read the home page and the digital archive page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the digital archive page on 2026-11-08. The registry-books subpage returned a rate limit and was not read.

providers.name: Historijski arhiv Sarajevo (Historical Archives of Sarajevo)
providers.what: Archive for Sarajevo and its region. The site has a guide to holdings and collections (new edition promoted April 2026), family and personal fonds, Ottoman-period collections in Arabic, Turkish and Persian and in Bosnian written in Arabic script, land registry records, and registers of record creators. A How to research page and forms for data-research requests, library requests and transcription requests are available, and virtual exhibitions are listed. In-person hours are weekday mornings. The page does not describe birth, marriage or death registers, and I did not open the guide or request forms.
providers.triageNote: Opened the site (redirecting to a WordPress home page) on 2026-11-08. Did not open the holdings guide.

providers.name: Drzavni arhiv Crne Gore (State Archives of Montenegro, Cetinje)
providers.what: National archive of Montenegro in Cetinje. The site has counters for fonds, collections and linear metres, public visiting hours each working day, a free-access-to-information section, internet exhibitions (for example on Niksic, Budva and Ulcinj archives), publication series such as Arhivski zapisi, and annual work plans and reports. A login area exists but new registration was not allowed when I read it. The page says nothing about parish or civil registers or a researcher search, so what family records are held remains unconfirmed.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the exhibitions or reports.

providers.name: Digitalna NBS (Digital National Library of Serbia)
providers.what: Digital portal of the National Library of Serbia, in Cyrillic, Latin and English. It offers medieval manuscripts and old printed books, Serbian works up to the mid 20th century, newspapers and magazines from the 19th to mid 20th century, music and sound, images and maps, and thematic features including a First World War portal from the Europeana 1914-1918 project. An advanced search and terms of use are provided, but the page does not state that access is free, and I did not open a periodical or test full-text search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open any periodical title.

providers.name: Zgodovinski arhiv Ljubljana (Historical Archives Ljubljana)
providers.what: Regional archive for the Ljubljana area. The home page links a search for materials, a virtual archive reading room (vac.sjas.gov.si), a service for issuing documents, a Digiteka, online publications and exhibitions, a register of creators and a list of private holders. The reading room is open on weekdays with a longer day on Wednesday. The page does not mention parish registers or genealogy, so which person-level series exist must be checked in the search or with the archive. I read the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the virtual reading room or Digiteka.

providers.name: Pokrajinski arhiv Maribor (Regional Archives Maribor)
providers.what: Regional archive for north-eastern Slovenia with a research reading room at Ravne na Koroskem. The home page has a search of archival material, a virtual archive reading room for browsing data on holdings, a section of digitised archival material, a register of creators and a library catalogue search. Separate desks handle the reading room and the issue of documents, with posted hours. The page does not mention genealogy or registers and I did not open the digitised section.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the digitised material or the search.

providers.name: Departament po arkhivam i deloproizvodstvu Ministerstva yustitsii Respubliki Belarus (Department for Archives and Records Management, Belarus)
providers.what: Portal of the Belarusian state archive service under the Ministry of Justice, in Russian. The menu has a Genealogy section, thematic databases, archival reference guides, services and administrative procedures, an electronic enquiry form, and a map of archive locations. The home page links the Documentary Chronicle of Belarus (letopis.by), the open-access system for National Archival Fund documents (sodd.by), the state archives' fonds catalogue (fk.archives.gov.by) and a coat-of-arms portal. The page does not explain what the genealogy section contains or any fees. I could not open the genealogy page, which returned not found at the address I tried.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. My guess at the genealogy page address returned 404; the fonds catalogue timed out.

providers.name: SODD NAF - Sistema otkrytogo dostupa k dokumentam Natsionalnogo arkhivnogo fonda Belarusi (open access system for National Archival Fund documents)
providers.what: Online portal operated by the Belarusian Centre for Digitalisation of Archival Activity. The page says it gives information on the composition of the fonds of all state archival institutions, and names the National Archive of Belarus, the National Historical Archive in Minsk and the State Archive-Museum of Literature and Art. It has a search by archive, an advanced search and a how-to-search guide, plus a login link and price lists. The page does not state document types or years, nor what is free, and I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not log in or search.

providers.name: Rossiyskiy gosudarstvennyy istoricheskiy arkhiv (Russian State Historical Archive, RGIA)
providers.what: St Petersburg archive of Russian Empire central institutions. The site has a searchable catalogue of fonds, inventories, files and sheets with a filter for files that have scanned sheets, and indexes by personal name, geography, subject and topography, plus a reference library catalogue, virtual exhibitions and video tours. The page describes personal and family fonds of noble and official families, with member names and dates. A personal account must be registered before files are requested for issue; copy orders use an official form and there is a price list, effective May 2026, and self-scanning is offered. The page does not mention metric books, and I did not run a catalogue search.
providers.triageNote: Opened fgurgia.ru (rgia.su redirects there) on 2026-11-08 and read the catalogue, request and account notes. Did not register or search.

providers.name: Rid (pra.in.ua) - Baza danykh meshkantsiv Ukrainy 1650-1920 (database of Ukrainian residents, genealogical society Ridni)
providers.what: Volunteer genealogy database from the society Ridni, running since 2016, listing about 3.9 million people born between 1650 and 1920 and about 446,000 family trees on the day read. Volunteers index scans and photocopies of documents posted on the site and add the people they find. Records are grouped into 1650-1799, 1800-1849, 1850-1899 and 1900 onward, and can be browsed by top surnames, districts, settlements or a map; there is also a database search page. The site states that access is free and has login and registration links, but I could not tell whether an account is needed to search. The source archives are not named on the home page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not run a search or register; sources behind the index are not stated.

providers.name: Sakartvelos erovnuli sagarcho biblioteka (National Library of Georgia / NPLG)
providers.what: National library of Georgia in Tbilisi. The site links digital libraries including Iverieli and Mamardashvili collections and an online archive of Georgian music, a project inviting families to share old photographs and postcards, and a catalogue that describes newspaper and journal articles. Related resources include a Georgian biographical dictionary and biographies of Georgians living abroad. Reading halls are open daily and reader registration, reference, interlibrary loan and internet services are listed. The page does not mention genealogy or say whether newspapers are digitised in full, and I did not open the digital libraries.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open the digital libraries or the biographical dictionary.

providers.name: Biblioteca Digitala BCU Cluj (Lucian Blaga Central University Library digital collection)
providers.what: Digital library of the Lucian Blaga Central University Library in Cluj-Napoca. It holds books, manuscripts, serial publications and pictures chosen for their relevance to the history of Cluj and Transylvania or because readers asked for them, with about 276,900 items in the periodicals category and subject groups such as political and economic press. Search covers metadata and full text and can be sorted by relevance, title or date. The page does not mention genealogy or state whether access is free, and I did not open a periodical.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page on 2026-11-08. Did not open any periodical or test download.

providers.name: The National Archives (Kew, London)
providers.what: The national archive for England and Wales and the UK central government, at Kew. Its Help with your research page points to the Discovery catalogue, a set of research guides, a live-chat and email enquiry service, a paid-research option and a request route for armed-forces service records. Visiting Kew to see original documents is stated to be free with no need to book, and its guides say online records can be viewed free at Kew. Some record sets are only online through partner sites at a charge: the 1939 Register guide names Findmypast and Ancestry as the places to search it. The Discovery catalogue is already a separate row in the Atlas; this row is for the institution and its guidance.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the Help with your research page, 8 Nov 2026. Did not test Discovery downloads, ordering copies or the reader's-ticket process.

providers.name: The National Archives - research guides (family history and military)
providers.what: A listing of 377 research guides (the page says so) that explain which records exist for a topic, where they are held and how to use them. The guides can be filtered by subject, among them family history, First World War, Second World War, military and maritime, immigrants and emigrants, religious groups and wills; there is an A-Z index, keyword tags and a filter for guides whose records are all online. The family-history filter lists 157 guides (I read the first 60 titles), which include census records, births, marriages and deaths for England and Wales, for Scotland and Ireland, and for the Channel Islands and Isle of Man, army, navy and merchant records, criminal transportation, coroners' inquests and the 1939 Register. A guide's header shows how many of its records are online. I read the listing and the 1939 Register guide only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the guide index, the family-history filtered list (first 60 titles) and the 1939 Register guide, 8 Nov 2026. Free to read; did not open the other guides.

providers.name: British Library
providers.what: The national library of the United Kingdom. Its Explore the collection page describes printed and manuscript holdings from antiquity to the present, including the Burney collection of 17th and 18th century newspapers, UK publishing, the East India Company records (1600-1858) and the India Office records (1858-1947) with a large India Office photograph collection. The page says the Library is still recovering from a cyber-attack and that the guides explain how to reach different parts of the collection. Its Asia and Africa reading room and a print room are stated to need an appointment. I did not find a family-history guide at the addresses I tried.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home-level Explore the collection page and the India Office subject page, 8 Nov 2026. The specific India Office family-history guides were not found at the addresses tried; the catalogue itself was not searched.

providers.name: National Library of Scotland - family history guide and collections
providers.what: The Library's family-history pages point to births, deaths and marriages, census records, lists and directories, emigration records, maps, valuation rolls, voters' rolls, films and newspapers. It says it is unlikely to hold everything and signposts other organisations, and it offers a limited research service. Its eResources include newspaper and index databases, and the pages say library members with a Scottish address can use the online newspaper databases. The collections page lists map images (over 400,000 maps), an archives and manuscripts catalogue, a moving-image archive, a digital gallery and a data foundry. The map and directory sites (maps.nls.uk, digital.nls.uk) showed a human-verification page to my browser, so I did not read them.
providers.triageNote: Opened the family-history guide and the collections page by script, 8 Nov 2026. maps.nls.uk answered a script with HTTP 405 and a browser with a Human Verification page; not bypassed.

providers.name: Scottish Indexes
providers.what: A name-search site for Scottish records, with a global search box and separate record sets. The record-set page lists a criminal database, a paternity index, mental-health records, a Court of Session index, poor-relief records, deeds, the registers of sasines, a dispensary's patient registers, births/baptisms, banns/marriages and deaths/burials indexes, pre-1841 censuses and population lists, and 1841-1861 census coverage. The home page says an update on 10 March 2026 added over 100,000 prison-register entries from across Scotland, and it advises wildcards for variant spellings. There is a shopping cart and a bookshop, so some items are sold; I did not test what the searches show without paying.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the record-sets page, 8 Nov 2026. Did not run a search, so I do not know what results are free.

providers.name: Glasgow City Archives (Glasgow Life)
providers.what: The archive of Glasgow City Council and a range of private and business collections, run by Glasgow Life. The page says it holds databases for family historians, including poor law records and church registers, most of which can only be used in the search room, and a card catalogue of names, places and subjects. An online catalogue exists at cityarchives.glasgowlife.org.uk; descriptions for core local-authority collections (refs A-H) are online and others are not yet. Visits are by appointment, up to six items can be requested in advance, and staff can do a search by email. The page also lists closure periods for school records (30 to 75 years), poor law applications and some police records.
providers.triageNote: Read the city-archives page 8 Nov 2026. The separate online catalogue site was not opened.

providers.name: Royal Berkshire Archives
providers.what: The archive of the Royal County of Berkshire. Its family-history pages say it holds registers for all but one of the roughly 200 ancient parishes plus about 100 later ones, with some surviving from 1538, and non-Anglican registers. In association with Ancestry, parish registers have been digitised (over 4 million entries, per the page), as three Ancestry collections: Church of England baptisms, marriages and burials 1538-1812, baptisms 1813-1925, and marriages and banns 1813-1941. Visitors can use Ancestry, Findmypast and the British Newspaper Archive free on site. The site also has a wills index, voting records and a page on national resources.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home, family-history, parish-registers and wills-index pages, 8 Nov 2026. Did not follow the Ancestry links, so online access outside the building is as the page states.

providers.name: Royal Berkshire Archives - Wills Index
providers.what: A name index to wills held by the Berkshire record office, on the archive's own site. The page offers an all-fields search, a names-only search, an A-Z letter filter and sorting by name, place, occupation, year or reference. Each entry I saw gives a name, the place, an occupation where known, a year (the first entries I saw were from the 1540s to 1600s), a document reference in the D/A1 series and the microfilm copy number. The page the index sits under is titled Wills and Probate 1480 to 1857. It is an index to wills; I did not see images.
providers.triageNote: Opened the index page 8 Nov 2026 and read the first screen of entries; did not run searches or open any will.

providers.name: Cheshire Archives and Local Studies
providers.what: The record office and local studies service for Cheshire (its web forms are hosted by Cheshire East Council). Its home page says Cheshire ancestors can be found online in The Cheshire Collection on Findmypast and on Ancestry, and has sections for family history, house history, parish registers, baptism certificates, electoral registers, wills, newspapers, maps, asylum, court and school records. The wills page says the office holds over 70,000 original wills proved in the Archdeaconry of Chester 1487-1857 and 60,000 microfilm copies of Chester wills 1858-1940, and that indexes can be searched and downloaded on Findmypast. A tithe-maps viewer is linked from the family-history menu. I did not search the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home, family-history and wills pages, 8 Nov 2026. Findmypast and Ancestry sections are subscription sites; not opened.

providers.name: Bedfordshire Archives
providers.what: The county record office for Bedfordshire, hosted by Bedford Borough Council and based at Borough Hall, Bedford. The home page offers an enquiry and research service, a copies request form, catalogue searching, project and event pages and a Community Histories section. It states that anyone may use the archives in person or remotely and asks users to check the catalogue before sending an enquiry. I did not open the catalogue or the fees page, and I did not see which record series are digitised.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; catalogue not searched.

providers.name: Bedfordshire Archives - Community Histories
providers.what: A set of place histories for Bedfordshire settlements, indexed A-B to T-Z by clickable map. For each place the archive aims to give an introduction, extracts from historic maps, photographs, details of public houses and beerhouses, places of worship, schools, buildings and notable local people. Where no history is written yet, the page lists the resources and collections for researching that area. The archive invites members of the public to contribute. Pages are open web pages; I read the index page only, not individual parish histories.
providers.triageNote: Opened the index page 8 Nov 2026 only.

providers.name: Essex Archives Online (Essex Record Office)
providers.what: The digital catalogue of the Essex Record Office, Chelmsford. It describes every item in the archive and carries over 780,000 digital images, including 590,000 images of Church of England parish registers from Essex and north-east London, 175,000 images of original wills from Essex and eastern Hertfordshire (1400-1858), 21,000 electoral register images (an incomplete set 1833-1883, plus 1918 and 1929, not indexed by name) and Industrial School admission registers. The catalogue is free to search from home; some images and recordings are free after registering, while the parish register images need a paid subscription (1 day to 1 year) at home. All images can be viewed in the Searchroom and at three archive access points. Certificate copies for Essex events can be ordered from the office.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the Essex Archives Online page 8 Nov 2026. The catalogue and subscription pages were not opened.

providers.name: Kresen Kernow (Cornwall's archive centre)
providers.what: The home for Cornwall's archives at Redruth, which the site describes as holding the world's largest collection of documents, books, maps and photographs about Cornwall's history. The site has collections guides, a browse-images section, mapping, a Historic Environment Record, a copies and search service and a Cornish Archives Network page. Its catalogue runs on Calm, and the visit information says the archive is open on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays with pre-booking required. I did not open the collections guides, so I cannot say which parish registers or wills are digitised.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the collections FAQ page 8 Nov 2026. Catalogue not searched.

providers.name: The Keep (East Sussex Record Office, Brighton)
providers.what: A joint archive centre in Brighton whose partners are East Sussex Record Office, Brighton and Hove Museums, the East Sussex Historic Environment Record and the University of Sussex. Its home page is a single catalogue search with all-words, any-words, exact-phrase and proximity modes, partner filters, and fields for title, creator or related person or organisation, place, keywords, formats and date range. Readers can register an account and keep a wishlist, and the site has research-room, services and visit pages. I did not open the collections pages, so which registers and indexes are held or imaged is unchecked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026. Did not register or search.

providers.name: Staffordshire Name Indexes (Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Archive Service)
providers.what: A set of free name indexes put online by the Staffordshire and Stoke-on-Trent Archive Service. The home page lists an apprentices index (1600-1900), an asylum patient database (1818-1920), calendars of prisoners at Staffordshire Quarter Sessions (1779-1921), Lichfield and Coventry diocese wills (1550-1810), an extended illegitimacy index (1559-1923), Newcastle-under-Lyme manor tenants, military tribunals (1916-1918), parish clerks of Lichfield diocese (1691-1916), police registers, quarter-sessions jurors and indictments, a Great War newspaper index (1914-1919), gaol photograph albums and Stoke-on-Trent police and welfare indexes. The page says the site allows free access to these indexes. I did not run a search or open a record.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; the list of indexes is read from it.

providers.name: Hull History Centre
providers.what: An archive and local studies centre in Hull. The home page names an online catalogue as the starting point, research guides by theme and an A-Z list, a research service, a family-history helpdesk, microfilm readers and a searchroom, and states that copies and digital images are charged. It gives the address as Worship Street, Hull. The page does not say which family-history record types are held, and I did not open the catalogue or the guides.

at.place: Hull, East Riding of Yorkshire, England

providers.triageNote: Read the home page 8 Nov 2026 via WebFetch; no deeper pages opened.

providers.name: Tyne & Wear Archives
providers.what: The archive service for Tyne and Wear, based at Discovery Museum in Newcastle and run by North East Museums. The page says it is essential to book to use the searchroom, which is open Tuesday to Thursday, and links to an online catalogue, services pages and a Flickr gallery. The building was under roof restoration but the archives were operating. I did not open the catalogue or see which family-history series are held, so the access class reflects only the booked-searchroom use stated on the page.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 8 Nov 2026; catalogue not opened.

providers.name: Dorset Online Parish Clerks (OPC)
providers.what: A volunteer site of parish-by-parish transcriptions for Dorset. The home page claims over 2.2 million individual records and a latest update on 5 November 2026, lists the parishes alphabetically, and has search, updates, maps, links and windmills pages. It states that the transcripts are made freely available for personal research, are not always validated, and should be checked against originals, usually at Dorset History Centre. The Dorset OPC project is described elsewhere as the model for several other county OPC sites. I read the home page only, not individual parish pages.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; did not run a search.

providers.name: Cornwall Online Parish Clerks - Cornwall OPC Database
providers.what: A searchable database of Cornish parish records donated by volunteer transcribers. The menu lists searches for banns, baptisms, burials, marriages, marriage allegations and certificate transcriptions, plus extra searches for bastardy, civil and criminal courts, emigrants, hearth tax, institution inmates, land records, memorial inscriptions, muster rolls, newspaper reports, apprenticeship indentures, parish settlements, Protestation returns, school admissions, voters' lists and wills. There are coverage pages by parish and for non-conformist records. The site warns users to consult originals, and asks for donations towards hosting. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; no search run, so whether results are fully shown is not tested.

providers.name: Wiltshire Online Parish Clerks (Wiltshire OPC)
providers.what: A volunteer-run project that publishes genealogical and local-history material for Wiltshire, organised by the historic Church of England parishes. Begun in 2006, it holds parish pages, county-wide pages and military pages, a newsletter and a statistics page that lists what has been published. The site says it intends to remain a free facility and invites small donations towards running costs. It recommends cross-checking transcripts with originals. I read the home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; individual parish pages not opened.

providers.name: Sussex Online Parish Clerks (Sussex OPC)
providers.what: A volunteer site for East and West Sussex organised by parish. The menu lists documents (baptisms, burials, marriages, monumental inscriptions, census returns, enumeration districts, wills), other resources (postal directories, poll registers, Protestation returns, a Gazette index, a name index, postcards and images) and a 1841 census project that asks for volunteers. It has a login and registration area. I did not log in or search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; registration not tried.

providers.name: Archives Wales (Archifau Cymru)
providers.what: The public face of the Archives and Records Council Wales. The site introduces archives, how to use them and how to get involved, and has a members page with a map of archive services across Wales, news and project pages, and a Welsh-language twin site. The home page did not show a combined catalogue search, so I cannot say whether one exists here. It is a way to find the right county or university archive rather than a records database.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 8 Nov 2026; the members list and map not opened.

providers.name: Glamorgan Archives (Archifau Morgannwg)
providers.what: The joint record office for Bridgend, Caerphilly, Cardiff, Merthyr Tydfil, Rhondda Cynon Taf and the Vale of Glamorgan, at Leckwith, Cardiff. Its online catalogue, Canfod, is stated to describe over 180,000 items. The site has research guides on record series and an Indexes and Transcriptions section, but I did not open them, so the indexes are unchecked. Enquiries go through a form and the page asks for a clear question.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 8 Nov 2026 via WebFetch; Canfod and indexes not opened.

providers.name: People's Collection Wales (Casgliad y Werin Cymru)
providers.what: A Welsh heritage platform where archives, museums and individuals share photographs, memories and stories. The home page shows themed collections, a search box, a map section, learning resources and digitising guides, and it asks visitors to contribute and offers account registration. It features material from archives such as Anglesey and Glamorgan. It is a community and local-history resource more than a records database; I did not search it.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 8 Nov 2026 via WebFetch; no search tried.

providers.name: Dictionary of Welsh Biography (Y Bywgraffiadur Cymreig)
providers.what: A reference work with over five thousand concise biographies of people who made a notable contribution to Welsh life. It can be browsed by letter or searched by name. The home page says that for cyber-security reasons the site is now static, with new articles published provisionally on a University of Wales Centre for Advanced Welsh and Celtic Studies page. It is a biographical reference for notable people, not a record index of ordinary families.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; articles not read.

providers.name: Military Archives (Cartlann Mhíleata), Ireland
providers.what: The archive of Ireland's Defence Forces. Its family-research page says it may hold a personnel record if a relative served in the Defence Forces from 1922, and that individual Irish Volunteer, IRA, Cumann na mBan and Fianna records were not kept as service files. It states that it has no records of military service before 1922 and points to the National Archives in London for British Army service. Online collections include the Military Service Pensions Collection, the Bureau of Military History, an Irish Army census of 1922, the Collins Papers, magazines and maps; 27 more collections are described for the reading room (open Tuesday to Thursday by appointment). Deceased soldiers' service records from 1922 are available to next of kin on request.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and the family-research page 8 Nov 2026. A cookie-accept prompt hid some page text; I did not click it.

providers.name: Military Service Pensions Collection 1916-1923 (Military Archives, Ireland)
providers.what: The digitised files of applications for military service pensions and medals from people who took part in Ireland's revolutionary period, 1916-1923, held by the Military Archives. The collection page offers a search of the full database, sections on the 1916 Rising, the War of Independence, the Truce and the Civil War, brigade activity reports, nominal rolls and file-release lists. The family-research page warns that not all pension applications are online yet. The page also records that files exist for 72 people executed in the Civil War. I did not run a search or open a file.
providers.triageNote: Opened the collection page 8 Nov 2026; the search form and files were not tested.

providers.name: Irish Army Census Collection, November 1922 (Military Archives)
providers.what: A digitised census of the Irish National Army taken on 12-13 November 1922 after the split in the army and the rapid recruitment of the Civil War. The page says the ten bound volumes are arranged by military post, so before digitising a soldier could only be found if the post was known. It offers a search of the collection plus history, project and map sections. The page describes the returns as a source for personnel serving in November 1922. I did not search it.
providers.triageNote: Opened the collection page 8 Nov 2026; search not run.

providers.name: Bureau of Military History 1913-1921 (Military Archives, Ireland)
providers.what: The Bureau collected witness statements about the Irish revolutionary period between 1947 and 1957: 1,773 witness statements, 334 sets of contemporary documents, 42 sets of photographs and 13 voice recordings, according to the Military Archives guide. The collection was transferred to the Military Archives in 2001 and launched online in March 2003, and the site has sections for contemporary documents, an index, witnesses, an image gallery, press cuttings and voice recordings. A duplicate set of statements went to the National Archives. Note that the older bureauofmilitaryhistory.ie address now shows an unrelated gambling page, so use the Military Archives address.
providers.triageNote: Opened the collection guide 8 Nov 2026. Also opened bureauofmilitaryhistory.ie and found it serving a casino-review page.

providers.name: National Archives of Ireland - Census of Ireland 1901 and 1911
providers.what: The search form for the 1901 and 1911 censuses of Ireland, which the National Archives says are the only surviving full censuses open to the public; they cover the whole island, were opened for inspection in 1961 and went online in 2009. The form searches by census year, surname, forename, county (including the six Northern Ireland counties), townland or street, district electoral division, age plus or minus five years, sex and relation to head of household. A county browse and a step-by-step guide are linked, and the page says earlier census material is searched through a separate link. I did not run a search or view a household return.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search form and the About the census collections page 8 Nov 2026. The older census.nationalarchives.ie address timed out; the National Archives collections page says its genealogy microsites are offline for a rebuild.

providers.name: National Archives of Ireland - Census of Ireland 1926
providers.what: The search form for the 1926 census, the first taken after the Irish Free State was established, on 18 April 1926; the National Archives says returns are closed for 100 years under the Statistics Act 1993, and the page now carries a search form for it. The form takes surname, forename, county (the 26 counties), townland or street, district electoral division and an exact-match option, and there is a Census 1926 map for geographical searching and a public-programme page. Records from 1901 and 1911 are searched on a separate form. I did not run a search or view a return.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search form 8 Nov 2026 and the collections page that introduces the census; no search run.

providers.name: Cork City and County Archives
providers.what: The archive for Cork City and County. Its holdings, as described, include Cork City and County Council records, Cork Harbour Commissioners (1814-1985), Cork Poor Law Unions (1838-1923), photographs, maps, cemetery and burial records, directories and almanacs, business and school records, religious institutions and oral histories. There is an online catalogue with a user guide and a family history and genealogy section that lists digital collections such as workhouse inmate registers (1840-1923) and a cemetery's burial records. Research-room access is by appointment and readers register first. I did not open the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page 8 Nov 2026 via WebFetch; catalogue and genealogy pages not opened.

providers.name: Irish Newspaper Archives
providers.what: A commercial searchable archive of Irish newspapers, national and local, from both sides of the border. The home page claims over 19.5 million pages, offers search, browse by newspaper or by directory, clippings and gift subscriptions, and has Subscribe and Sign in buttons. Titles shown as recently updated include the Belfast News Letter (1738-2026), the Derry Journal (from 1772), the Anglo-Celt (1846-2026) and several county papers. I did not search, so the extent of free results is untested.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; no search and no subscription page read.

providers.name: Jersey Heritage - family history research and online catalogue
providers.what: Jersey Heritage runs the Jersey Archive and its online catalogue, which its family-history page names as the main starting point. Records described include German Occupation registration cards (1940-1945), Church of England baptisms 1842-1923 and marriages 1842-1945 with downloadable images, non-conformist records, civil registration indexes from 1842, wills 1660-1999 (digital images to the 1960s), funeral directors' records, alien registration cards from 1920, Royal Court, militia, hospital, prison (1814-1939) and school records. The page says some downloads are pay-per-view and an annual catalogue subscription starts at 30 pounds. Censuses are on Ancestry and Findmypast, according to the page.
providers.triageNote: Read the family-history page 8 Nov 2026 via WebFetch; did not open the catalogue or test downloads.

providers.name: Priaulx Library (Guernsey)
providers.what: Guernsey's local-history library. Its family-history page lists civil and parish microfilm records, selected Alderney records, Guernsey and Jersey census returns 1841-1901, local newspapers from 1791, almanacs and directories, army lists, Elizabeth College registers, photographs and research files on local families. Paper and microfilm can be browsed in the library free of charge, a paid research service is offered for overseas researchers, and visitors get free use of Ancestry, Findmypast and the British Newspaper Archive. A digitisation programme is building a database of images, newspapers and documents. The Library is also the repository for Guernsey French material. I did not search its catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and the family-history page 8 Nov 2026; catalogue and family-name list not opened.

providers.name: Bailiwick of Guernsey Digitisation Partnership (familyhistory.gg)
providers.what: A partnership set up in 2023 between the Greffe, the Island Archives and the Priaulx Library to put Guernsey's family-history records online through Findmypast. The page says about 210,000 pages are digitised: civil births, deaths and marriages, church baptisms, marriages and burials (earliest from the late 1500s), German Occupation identity records, wills and partage, crime and conveyancing records, cemetery and Town Hospital records, and the 1827 census. Privacy cut-offs apply (births and baptisms over 100 years, marriages over 85, deaths and burials over 25). Findmypast is free to use at the Priaulx Library, Island Archives and the Greffe; from home it needs a subscription. I did not test the Findmypast search.
providers.triageNote: Read the page 8 Nov 2026 via WebFetch; Findmypast side not opened.

providers.name: Find a will or probate record (England and Wales) - GOV.UK
providers.what: The government service for finding a probate record, also called a grant of representation, for someone who died after 1857 in England and Wales. The guide says a new probate record is online about 14 days after it is issued, that records for 1858 to 1996 are stored by the year the grant was issued (so check later years), and that not every grant includes a will. Copies ordered online cost 16 pounds each, a postal search with form PA1S also costs 16 pounds and a standing search for recent deaths costs 4 pounds. It separates Scotland and Northern Ireland, which follow different processes. I read the guidance page only and did not use the search service.
providers.triageNote: Read the guidance page 8 Nov 2026; the probatesearch.service.gov.uk search service itself was not used.

providers.name: The Digital Panopticon (London convicts, Britain and Australia 1780-1925)
providers.what: A research site linking about fifty datasets to follow the lives of some 90,000 convicts tried at the Old Bailey, 1780-1925. The home page offers search of individual convict life archives, visualisations and background essays on crime, policing, trial, sentencing and punishment, with London and Australian sections. It notes a December 2019 update adding convict tattoo datasets and an occupation search. It is a research project site rather than an archive; I did not run a search or check how much is open.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; search not run.

providers.name: Charles Booth's London (LSE)
providers.what: The London School of Economics site for the Inquiry into Life and Labour in London (1886-1903). It offers the Maps Descriptive of London Poverty and the inquiry's notebooks, which the page says can be searched, browsed and downloaded. There are also pages on the inquiry's history, a Minecraft world and a link to the LSE Digital Library. The maps cover London districts street by street; I did not check whether the notebooks name residents. I did not open a map or notebook.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; maps and notebooks not opened.

providers.name: The Workhouse - history of the Poor Law and workhouses (workhouses.org.uk)
providers.what: A single-author history site on the Poor Law, with an introduction, the Old and New Poor Law, full text of Poor Law Acts, and a Poor Law Union list for England, Wales, Scotland and Ireland. Workhouse locations are arranged by region and county, with maps and a section on workhouses outside Britain; it links a companion site on former children's homes. Pages are open web pages. It is a history and location guide, not a name index; I read the contents menu and home page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; no county page read.

providers.name: UKBMD - links to local BMD indexes and census transcriptions
providers.what: A directory of links to websites that offer transcriptions of UK births, marriages, deaths and censuses; the page says it provides 2,795 links, with other indexes such as parish records, wills and monumental inscriptions for most counties. The Local BMD websites it points to are run by volunteers from local family history societies, and tutorials on them are offered. The page carries affiliate links to commercial sites. It is a finding aid rather than a database; I did not follow the county links.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026 only.

providers.name: Deceased Online
providers.what: A commercial database of UK burial and cremation registers from participating cemeteries and crematoria. The home page offers a free search by last name (with optional first name and year range) and a free sign-up; the coverage page lists authorities and the number of names recorded for each, for example Aberdeen City Council 192,000 and Bolton Council 415,000. The FAQ says new areas are added and that records may be missing when an authority is not yet loaded. I did not read what viewing a record costs.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page, coverage page (first screen of five) and FAQ 8 Nov 2026; did not search or read pricing.

providers.name: Gravestone Photographic Resource (GPR)
providers.what: An international directory of grave, tomb and war memorials, built from photographs, with an index of names taken from the monuments. The home page says it holds over 1.29 million names from English grave monuments and about 1.97 million worldwide, lists burial grounds by country and notes the newest addition (a Cheshire churchyard, May 2024). The site describes itself as running free of charge since 1998. I did not search or open a cemetery page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026 only.

providers.name: Lloyd's Register Foundation Heritage Centre (Lloyd's Register of Ships online)
providers.what: A free maritime archive with over 1.1 million documents, ship plans and survey reports, according to the home page. Its popular resources include Lloyd's Register of Ships online (1764-2000, searchable by ship name, master, owner and build location), the Casualty or Wreck Returns of total vessel losses, and Lloyd's Register of Yachts (1878-2001, 110+ volumes). Information guides cover shipwreck sources, classification societies and passenger lists. I did not open the registers or run a search.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026 (it asks for JavaScript); registers not opened.

providers.name: Royal Museums Greenwich - archive catalogue
providers.what: The catalogue of archives at the National Maritime Museum, Greenwich. Its filter lists catalogue sections for public records of the Royal Navy and the Merchant Navy (both local records and central administration), personal collections, records of semi-governmental and non-governmental organisations and uncatalogued material, with a long creator list including shipping companies and naval officers. Results can be filtered by level (collection, file, item). I did not run a search or open any item.
providers.triageNote: Opened the archive search page 8 Nov 2026; no search run.

providers.name: Family History Federation (Federation of Family History Societies)
providers.what: The charity that represents family history societies; the home page says it has over 160 member organisations. It offers a find-a-society A-Z, a speaker finder, a society sign-in and a joining page, and links to sibling sites: Explore Your Genealogy, Parish Chest, Family History Books Online and the Really Useful bulletins. Surname interests, once on this site, are now on Explore Your Genealogy. It does not itself host records; it is a route to the local societies that produce indexes.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026; the society list was not opened.

providers.name: Explore Your Genealogy (Family History Federation)
providers.what: A guide site from the Family History Federation, with topic pages on civil registration, parish registers, wills, graveyards, military and naval records, Poor Law records, census records, non-conformist records, occupations, old handwriting, names, maps and gazetteers, newspapers, and Scottish and Irish records. It has a find-a-society tool, a free online resources section, a video library and a surname-interests search. Contributions are invited from members. I read the front page only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026 only.

providers.name: Guild of One-Name Studies - indexes and surname lists
providers.what: The Guild of One-Name Studies lists surnames registered for one-name studies at one-name.org/surnames_a-z/ and offers a surname search that shows where a name occurs in its resources. The indexes page says the Global Marriages Index, Inscriptions Index and Modern Newspaper Index are open to all, while members reach the others, and a Marriage Locator helps place a GRO index marriage in a church. The site also has a wiki, library, forums and a members' profile service. Whether a given study is searchable beyond its listing varies and I did not test a study.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page, the indexes page and the A-Z surname page 8 Nov 2026; no study opened.

providers.name: GENUKI - UK and Ireland genealogical information service
providers.what: A non-commercial reference library for UK and Ireland family history, maintained by a charitable trust and volunteers. The site is organised by England, Scotland, Wales, Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands, with county pages, a gazetteer, a churches directory, a societies directory and guidance for newcomers. It is a link and information hub, not a record database. I read the home page and the UK and Ireland overview only.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page and /big/ page 8 Nov 2026; county pages not opened.

providers.name: Society of Genealogists (London)
providers.what: A family-history society with a library and archive at Wharf Road, London. Its research page says the library holds research and record guides, local history and extensive indexes, and the archive holds thousands of original documents and over 700 family-history research collections. Digital collections are available to members through SoG Explore, and onsite computers carry subscription sites for visitors. The page does not say what online material non-members can open. I did not search its catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and research page 8 Nov 2026; SoG Explore not accessed.

providers.name: The Peerage - genealogical survey of the British peerage
providers.what: A private site that collects the interconnected families of the British peerage and some European royal families. The home page describes it as a work in progress from the work of one person, warns that conflicting information may remain and urges users to weigh the citation given for each entry. It has an FAQ, custom indexes, abbreviations and a site map. It lists many persons, so use the cited sources to verify; I did not open any person page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page 8 Nov 2026 only.

providers.name: FamilySearch Research Wiki
providers.what: A wiki of research guidance run by FamilySearch. The home page says it holds about 156,000 articles and is browsed by choosing a region and then a country, with a world map and an all-localities list, or by a search box. Pages are meant to tell a researcher which birth, death, marriage, census and other records exist for a place and how to find them. The same page is offered in eight languages. Text is shared under a Creative Commons share-alike licence. The page does not say whether an account is needed, and I did not open any country page.
providers.triageNote: Opened the wiki home page on 2026-11-08 and read its structure; did not open a country or locality article.

providers.name: FamilySearch Library Catalog
providers.what: The catalogue of the FamilySearch Library in Salt Lake City and of material in the FamilySearch digital library. The search page offers search by place, keywords, titles, author, subjects and surnames, plus call number or film, fiche and image-group number, with a filter for items available online. It lists books, microfilms, microfiche and maps, and curated lists. The page does not state whether signing in is required, and I ran no search, so what any particular place or film shows was not checked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the catalogue start page on 2026-11-08; ran no search and did not test sign-in or image access.

providers.name: Fold3
providers.what: A military-records site that belongs to Ancestry. The home page claims over 900 million records and lists collections for the American Revolutionary War, War of 1812, Mexican-American and Indian wars, the Civil War (Union and Confederate), the Spanish-American War, both world wars, Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan, plus Black history, Native American and non-military sets. Australian, Canadian, New Zealand and British collections are also listed. Entry points are search, browse, list-all and search by state. A seven-day trial and a free-membership link are shown; what the free tier includes and the prices are not stated, and I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not search or test what is free.

providers.name: American Ancestors (New England Historic Genealogical Society)
providers.what: The website of the New England Historic Genealogical Society, based in Boston. The home page lists an advanced search, a list of all databases, partner databases, search by project and by topic, a library catalogue, newspaper archives and a digital library. Emphasis areas named are colonial New England and the Great Migration, Revolutionary War, Massachusetts, Irish, Quaker, Catholic and African American research, and a project on enslaved people. Membership is sold and some content is member-only, while some guides and a chat service are free. The page does not say which databases need membership or give date ranges, and I opened no database.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open individual databases or test membership walls.

providers.name: Archives.com
providers.what: A subscription records site, owned by Ancestry. The home page claims over 11 billion items across more than 680 collections, including census, military, yearbook and newspaper sets, and names recent additions such as a whaling crew lists index (1809-1927), high-school indexes and a blacksmith and related trades index (1720-1940). A free seven-day trial is offered and the 1950 US census is stated to be free to explore; there is also a free resources section. Prices are not shown. I did not run a search, so the depth of any one collection was not checked.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not search.

providers.name: GenealogyBank
providers.what: A commercial newspaper-led archive for the United States. The home page claims over 16,000 American newspapers, with newspaper coverage from 1690 to today, obituaries from 1690 with a recent-obituary set from 1977, US census records 1790-1940, government publications 1789-1994 and historical books 1749-1900. The Social Security Death Index is described as free access; the trial and sign-up route to the rest is shown but prices are not on the page I read. I ran no search, and the claim that most of its papers are exclusive is the site's own.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not search or test paywalls.

providers.name: Interment.net
providers.what: A free site of cemetery transcriptions. The home page counts about 16.2 million burial records from some 2,400 cemetery transcriptions, each published as its own transcription so that several versions of one cemetery stay separate. Cemeteries are browsed by country and then state or region. The search takes a surname or given name of at least two characters with starts-with, contains or exact matching, optional birth or death year, and a place filter. The countries named on the page include the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand and Germany. I ran no search and did not check how complete any one cemetery is.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; page footer calls the site free; no search run.

providers.name: JewishGen Holocaust Database
providers.what: A search over well over 200 named sub-databases of Holocaust victims and survivors, with more than six million records stated. Examples listed with counts include camp records for Dachau, Mauthausen-Gusen and Bergen-Belsen, ghetto lists such as Lodz, transport and deportation lists, survivor registers, Claims Conference lists for Romania and Hungary, and a database drawn from the Arolsen Archives. The search form takes surname, given name, town or any field, with phonetic, sounds-like, starts-with, exact and three fuzzy levels, and AND or OR across terms. The page calls the collection a free public resource and asks for donations. I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the page on 2026-11-08; no search run; no login prompt mentioned on the page.

providers.name: JewishGen Online Worldwide Burial Registry (JOWBR)
providers.what: A registry of Jewish burial records from cemeteries around the world. The page states more than seven million burial records, over two million headstone photographs, and 12,114 cemeteries in 144 countries. The search takes surname, given name, town or any field with phonetic, exact, starts-with, sounds-like and fuzzy options, wildcards, AND or OR, and an optional country limit. A cemetery inventory can be browsed, and contributors can add data. Whether an account is needed for results was not stated on the page, and I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the page on 2026-11-08; no search run, access terms not tested.

providers.name: JewishGen Yizkor Book Project
providers.what: Translations of memorial books written by survivors and former residents about Jewish communities of Eastern and Central Europe lost in the Holocaust. The collection is browsed by town or region and the translated books can be read on the site. Two name tools are described: a Necrology Index of martyrs lists in the translated books and a Master Name Index of people named in translated portions. Print copies of completed translations can be ordered, and the page lists libraries and retailers that hold the originals. Translation is funded by donations. I did not open a book or run a name search.
providers.triageNote: Read the page on 2026-11-08; no book opened, access terms not tested.

providers.name: JewishGen Family Finder (JGFF)
providers.what: A registry in which Jewish genealogists list the surnames and towns they research, so that researchers of the same name or place can contact each other. The page states about 585,000 entries covering roughly 140,000 surnames and 18,000 towns, cross-referenced both ways. Searching and listing entries cost nothing, and a log-in is needed to add or edit your own entries. Use is limited to personal family research, and the page says the data may not be used for paid research, publication or school projects without written permission. I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the page on 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: JewishGen Communities Database and Gazetteer
providers.what: A place-name tool for Jewish genealogy. The Communities Database describes about 6,000 Jewish communities in Europe, North Africa and the Middle East with historical town names and jurisdictions, population figures and maps, searched by community name. A separate Gazetteer is described as covering about 2.4 million localities in 54 countries, with distance and radius searches. The page calls JewishGen a free public resource but carries a 2011 update date, so counts may be out of date. I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the page on 2026-11-08; page shows an old update date (2011); no search run.

providers.name: International Association of Jewish Genealogical Societies (IAJGS)
providers.what: The umbrella body for more than 90 Jewish genealogical societies worldwide. The site has a member-society list with a locator map, a cemetery project, a memorial-plaque indexing challenge, North American Jewish community books, publications and library material. It runs an annual conference (the page names a virtual event in April 2027 and an in-person one in 2028) and a records-access advocacy section. Useful as a way to find the society for a given country or town. I did not open the member list.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open the society list.

providers.name: Avotaynu
providers.what: A publisher of Jewish genealogy books and the journal AVOTAYNU, with more than 75 titles since 1991. The home page says the Anthology of Jewish Genealogy puts over 2,900 journal articles from 1985 to 2011 online. A link to a name-search section is present but is not explained on the page I read. The page does not say which content is free and which is paid, and I opened no article or search.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open the anthology or the search link.

providers.name: Centropa
providers.what: An archive of Jewish family memory from Central and Eastern Europe. The home page states 1,230 interviews conducted in 15 European countries and about 25,000 family photographs, with a further Sephardic set for the Balkans and Turkey. It can be searched by biography, by photograph and by map, and the page lists 21 countries. The page says the archive has passed to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, with a special-collections page promised. Access terms are not stated. I opened no individual interview.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open interviews or test access.

providers.name: Immigrant Ships Transcribers Guild (ISTG)
providers.what: A volunteer group that transcribes ship passenger manifests and posts them as web pages. The home page says there are over 30,000 manifests in volumes indexed 1 to 28, a latest-uploads list, and special projects such as lists of deaths on ships and rescued passengers. Examples named include Halifax arrivals and departures, departures from Bremen and Hawaii arrivals in 1898-99. A site search box is provided. The site states it forbids copying for profit and retrieval by spiders or robots, so only the home page was read. Years, ports and cost are not summarised on that page.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open volumes; site terms bar robots so no further automated reading.

providers.name: Steve Morse One-Step Web Pages
providers.what: A collection of search helpers that reach other sites' data in more flexible ways. The home page groups tools for the Port of New York and Ellis Island, other US ports and Hamburg outbound lists, US censuses 1790-1950, Canadian and British censuses, New York state censuses, vital-record indexes, Soundex and phonetic matching, calendar conversions, gazetteer and map tools, foreign-alphabet tools, and some Holocaust-era databases. Each tool names its source; some use free FamilySearch data and others depend on Ancestry or are marked as pay. I used none of the tools.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; ran no tool.

providers.name: RootsWeb
providers.what: A community genealogy site funded by Ancestry. The home page links hosted personal and society web sites, family trees, mailing lists, message boards, a family history wiki and the Obituary Daily Times, with quick links to the US GenWeb and World GenWeb projects. The footer links point to a mailing-list archive held on the Internet Archive and forms to restore or download a hosted site. Cost and registration terms were not stated on the page. I did not search any board or tree.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home page in the browser on 2026-11-08; did not search.

providers.name: Genealogy Trails History Group
providers.what: A volunteer project that transcribes records and posts them by US state and county, with state sites linking to county pages. Record types named on the home page include military records such as Civil War headstone lists and pensioner lists, obituaries, census and gazetteer data, mortality schedules, slavery and African American records, Native American records, maps and transportation records. The page says the data is free, carries no advertising, and may be used for personal research but not copied to other sites. Only US areas are described. I did not open a county site.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open county pages.

providers.name: WorldGenWeb Project
providers.what: A volunteer project that offers a web presence for each country, listed alphabetically from Afghanistan to Zimbabwe. Some countries link to their own pages and others to regional sites such as AfricaGenWeb, CaribbeanGenWeb, OceaniaGenWeb, SouthAmericaGenWeb, FranceGenWeb and EastEuropeGenWeb. The page also offers a volunteer page, a country-partner application, a newsletter, a getting-started guide and an FAQ. It does not describe what an individual country site holds, and some countries have no link. Fees and registration are not mentioned. I opened no country site.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open country sites.

providers.name: Cyndi's List
providers.what: A free, categorised index of links to online genealogy resources, described as a card catalogue for the web. The home page counts about 318,000 links in 231 categories, browsed A to Z or by the full category list, and says it has run for more than 25 years. It points to other sites rather than holding records itself. I did not open a category or test links for age.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open categories or check links.

providers.name: GeneAll.net
providers.what: A genealogy portal running since 2000 with an interface in Portuguese, English, Spanish, French, German and Italian. The home page counts about 5.17 million people and 178,000 families, of whom some 648,000 are listed as descendants of a medieval Portuguese king, and offers people, families, titles, offices and professions, coats of arms, royal houses, historical sources, a dictionary and a forum. A paid Premium tier adds kinship tools and alerts; the page does not say what is open without an account. I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not search or test login.

providers.name: ICRC First World War Prisoners Archive (1914-1918)
providers.what: The digitised archive of the International Prisoners of War Agency of the Red Cross for the First World War. The site says index cards were made for about ten million captured servicemen and civilians and that around five million cards can be searched. The Search for a person page filters by nationality (for example British and Commonwealth, French or Belgian, German, Austro-Hungarian) and by military or civilian status. The site is in English and French and is not tuned for phones; it warns of some indexing errors in civilian internee registers and says requests are not currently being answered. I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the site start page on 2026-11-08; no search run and image access not tested. Separate from the existing ICRC Second World War rows.

providers.name: Aircrew Remembered
providers.what: A web site of Second World War aircrew research that says it is used in 153 countries. The home page lists Allied databases (Allied Losses and Incidents for all commands, and the Paradie-Dutil RCAF archive) and Axis ones (the Kracker Luftwaffe archive), with a search page and search tips. Contents of each database are not described on the page I read, and cost is not stated although donate and sponsor pages exist. I opened none of the databases.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not open the databases.

providers.name: The War Graves Photographic Project (TWGPP)
providers.what: A volunteer project that photographs war graves and memorials. The home page states photographs of about 1.9 million graves, with a start in the First World War era and now all nationalities and conflicts, and says it worked jointly with the Commonwealth War Graves Commission until June 2016. The database search takes a surname and initial or forename, with an advanced search. The page does not say whether use is free. I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: David Rumsey Map Collection (Stanford)
providers.what: A free online archive of historical maps hosted at Stanford's David Rumsey Map Center. The site lists about 151,700 maps and images from the 16th to the 21st century, with primary sources from 1500. Search options named are advanced search, browse, text-on-maps search, a location search on a modern map and a random browse. A georeferencing tool overlays old maps on modern ones. The page says over 150,000 items are freely available and prints can be bought. Useful for old boundaries and place layouts; I opened no individual map.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; opened no map.

providers.name: OldMapsOnline
providers.what: A map portal that brings together scanned historical maps from many institutions, searched by place on a map with a timeline, so a researcher finds which library holds a map of an area. The site's project page describes georeferencing and crowdsourcing tools for libraries, and says clicking a map shows the host institution. A paid membership removes ads and adds exports. I loaded the viewer and project page but did not open a map or check which institutions are included.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home and project pages in the browser on 2026-11-08; opened no map.

providers.name: GeoNames
providers.what: A free gazetteer database. The about page states over 32 million names, about 19 million alternate names and 5.2 million populated places, in nine feature classes and 684 feature codes, drawn from sources such as US and UK national mapping data and Canadian GeoBase. Names can be searched in full text and shown as a table or on a map, and the data is downloadable under a Creative Commons attribution licence with free web services.
