It records current names; I did not test historical names.
providers.triageNote: Read the about page on 2026-11-08; ran no search.

providers.name: Meyers Gazetteer online (Meyers Orts- und Verkehrs-Lexikon)
providers.what: An online search of the German Empire's place-name gazetteer, offered with historical maps. The search ignores diacritics and accepts a star wildcard for any run of letters, at the start, end or middle of a name. A help guide and an about page are linked and the site says work on geocoding and a supplement is continuing. The page I read did not state the years covered or say whether use is free, and I ran no search.
providers.triageNote: Read the search page on 2026-11-08; no search run.

providers.name: Wikimedia Commons - Category: Genealogy
providers.what: The genealogy category of Wikimedia Commons, the free media store. Subcategories shown include family trees (about 800 files), parish registers (about 70 files), family registers, genealogy by country, family history and genealogy PDF files, with around 600 files in the category itself. Each file carries its own licence page. I did not find a dedicated passenger-list or church-book category on the part I read; the page was longer than I read.
providers.triageNote: Read the first part of the category page on 2026-11-08; did not read the rest.

providers.name: Digital Public Library of America (DPLA)
providers.what: A national discovery service for US libraries, archives and museums. The about page says it works with a network of partner hubs to make millions of materials from cultural institutions across the country findable in one place, and also runs an e-book marketplace for libraries. I read only the about text in the browser, not a search result, so collection types and years were not checked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the home and about pages in the browser on 2026-11-08; ran no search.

providers.name: Huguenot Society of Great Britain and Ireland
providers.what: A society for the history of the Huguenot refugees, founded 1885. Its home page says the Huguenot Library of printed and archival material for history and family history is housed at The National Archives in Kew and can be used by appointment only. It publishes an annual journal and a Quarto Series of Huguenot records, and links an Irish section, a blog, and corresponding societies in Europe, North America, South Africa and Australia. Membership is open to anyone. Specific genealogy services are not described. I opened no catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08; did not test the library catalogue.

providers.name: Library of the Society of Friends (Quakers in Britain) - Quaker Strongrooms
providers.what: The blog of the Library of the Society of Friends in London, which holds the archives of Quakers in Britain. Posts mention monthly meeting minutes, a burial notebook of 1711-1733, committee minutes from the 1660s to 2022, early letters, diaries, ledgers, deeds, and about 1,400 objects. It points to an online catalogue, an enquiry form and an appointments page, and says some ledgers are on microfilm or PDF and some items are not handled. The pages I read did not specifically describe birth, marriage and burial registers. I did not open the catalogue.
providers.triageNote: Read the blog home page on 2026-11-08 (first 100,000 characters); did not open the catalogue.

providers.name: Mennonite Genealogy Inc.
providers.what: A Mennonite genealogy resource site. The home page shows sections for International, Canada, Latin America, Poland, Prussia, Russia and the USA, a section on emigration from the Soviet Union in the 1920s, church registers, a new-files list, an FAQ and a sitemap. It does not describe a search method or say whether use is free. Updated October 2026 according to the page. I opened none of the sections.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page on 2026-11-08 via page fetch; did not open sections.

providers.name: Dansk Demografisk Database (DDD) - Danish Demographic Database
providers.what: A Danish-language database site whose footer names Rigsarkivet as operator, with English and German versions linked. The front page lists separate searchable databases: censuses (folketællinger, described as collected since 1787), transcribed church books (kirkebøger) arranged by event type, immigrants, emigrants (this one links out to another site), emigrants via Vejle, the 'Nygårds Sedler', First World War fallen, orders and decorations (Dannebrogsmænd, prize recipients, an 'Oeders' database from 1771). Each database has its own search page, and the site says a person must already be in the transcriptions to be found. Volunteers are invited to join as transcribers. I did not run searches or check which parishes and census years are present, and the page states no login requirement.
providers.triageNote: Opened the front page of ddd.dda.dk on 2026-11-08 (WebFetch). Did not open any database search page, so coverage per database and whether images appear are untested.

providers.name: Københavns Stadsarkiv (Copenhagen City Archives) - sources online
providers.what: The city archive of Copenhagen. Its 'Kilder på nettet' page lists digitised sources that can be viewed online, some searchable and some only browsable page by page in a viewer called Kildeviseren. Groups listed include burials 1805-1942, police registers 1890-1923, police household lists (Mandtaller) 1865-1923, poor-relief records 1799-1940, old-age support 1891-1928, house registers 1772-1835, guild and citizenship records, wards and guardians 1805-1903, marriage banns and civil marriages, and school and child-welfare registers. Memoirs written by Copenhageners are also kept. The site is in Danish and asks about cookies; I declined the non-essential ones. I did not test how much is free to view.
providers.triageNote: Opened the Kilder på nettet overview page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08 and read the list. Did not open the viewer or a search result.

providers.name: Politiets registerblade 1890-1923 (Copenhagen police registration cards)
providers.what: A searchable transcription of the Copenhagen police's registration cards, the city's forerunner of a population register, covering residents aged over 10 between 1890 and 1923. The page says there are about 1.4 million cards, typed in by volunteers between 2010 and 2018. A card gives the name, spouse's name, date and place of birth, occupation, addresses, children aged 10 to 14, and police notes such as wanted or punished. Married women are normally on the husband's card, and the military district Nyboder is not included. The cards cover the municipality, including areas added from 1901/02, and many Frederiksberg addresses. A related series of about 38,000 closed registration cards of people who died 1923-32 is also searchable. I did not run a search.
providers.triageNote: Read the full page text in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. Search form not opened; whether it needs an account is untested.

providers.name: Begravelser i København 1805-1942 (Copenhagen burial protocols)
providers.what: The burial section of Copenhagen City Archives' online sources. The page says burial protocols for 1861-1940 were typed in by volunteers (2016-2023) and can be searched by name and address, and that the rest can be browsed as images in Kildeviseren. For 1805-1862 only the protocols of Assistens Cemetery survive. Subpages cover abbreviations, causes of death in the protocols, and the cemetery's sections. Pre-1805 burials are pointed to patronage archives and land-deed protocols from 1575, which are paper and ordered for the reading room. I did not open a search or an image.
providers.triageNote: Read the page text in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. Did not test the search or viewer.

providers.name: Det Danske Udvandrerarkiv (Danish Emigration Archives), Aalborg
providers.what: Denmark's national collection of letters, documents, films, photographs, sound tapes and newspapers about Danish emigration, run from Aalborg City Archives. The page says it was founded in 1932, started with a focus on emigrants to America, and holds material from the 1880s to the present, from well-known people and from thousands of ordinary emigrants. The site links to a 'Søg i Samlingen' collection search and to an 'Udvandrerprotokollen' page, and has an English version. Postal address, reading-room hours and enquiry route are on the page. I did not open the search or the emigrant-protocol page, so I cannot say what that database contains.
providers.triageNote: Read the landing page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08 (udvandrerarkivet.dk and emiarch.dk redirect to it). Did not open Udvandrerprotokollen or the collection search.

providers.name: Slægtsforskernes Bibliotek (Danish genealogists' online library)
providers.what: An online library linked to Danske Slægtsforskere, the Danish genealogy federation. The page says it holds about 64,000 titles covering genealogy, biography, reference works, local history, history and sources, plus digitised archival items such as a 1950 census, probate records, local directories and telephone books, wartime literature, school annual reports, a maritime name index, a membership card index and a coat-of-arms database. It has a catalogue of the online and physical collection, a free-text search with guidance, a person search and a search for books on a family name. The physical collection is at Albertslund by appointment. I did not check fees; the old address bibliotek.dis-danmark.dk showed a bot-check page (Anubis) to scripted access.
providers.triageNote: Read slaegtsbibliotek.dk through WebFetch on 2026-11-08 (the page text names itself Danskernes Historie Online). Did not run a search or open a title.

providers.name: Arkivportalen (Norwegian archive catalogue portal)
providers.what: A Norwegian search portal for archive catalogues, developed and run by Stiftelsen Asta, started in 2010 and relaunched in 2018. The About page says users can search archive material from many institutions, that institutions differ in what services they offer there, and that some have not published all their archives. At the time I read it, it listed 100 depositing institutions and 101,849 published archives, among them county and city archives, labour-movement archives, museums and inter-municipal archives. The site offers a login, help pages on searching and ordering, and an information page on restricted material. I did not run a search or open an archive description.
providers.triageNote: Opened the front page and the Om Arkivportalen page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. No cookie banner accepted; no search tested.

providers.name: Manntalsvefur Þjóðskjalasafns Íslands (Icelandic censuses online)
providers.what: The census site of the National Archives of Iceland (manntal.is forwards here). The search page lists the censuses 1703, 1816, 1835, 1840, 1845, 1850, 1855, 1860, 1870, 1880, 1890, 1901, 1910 and 1920. A person can search all of them at once or tick selected ones, set the number of results per page, and use an advanced search and an option to search all word forms. The interface is in Icelandic with an English switch. I did not run a search, so what fields a result shows, and whether images appear, is not checked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the search page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. No search run.

providers.name: Tímarit.is (Icelandic newspapers and periodicals)
providers.what: A digitised newspaper and periodical service of the National and University Library of Iceland. The front page offers a search box with an inflection list, long snippets and advanced search, plus lists of titles and articles and an About page. Its 'recently added' panel shows titles with year ranges, from 1950s and 1960s periodicals to publications of 2005-2007, so it carries recent as well as old material. It links to sister sites for books, sound and manuscripts, an instruction PDF and a wanted-materials page. English and Icelandic interfaces exist. I did not search, open a page image or read the rules on which years are open.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English front page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. No search or image tested.

providers.name: Digi - Digital Collections of the National Library of Finland
providers.what: The National Library of Finland's digital collections. The English front page counts 33,390,593 pages of material and a search box that can be limited to newspapers, journals, ephemera, books, manuscripts, maps, music notation, pictures, library card indices, archive letters and archive manuscripts. Other sections are serial publications, '100 years ago', clippings and the Tutkain text-mining service, plus open data, a 'Name wizard' and sample collections such as labour newspapers and Priozersk and Lake Ladoga region papers. There is a login link and a cookie choice, and Finnish, Swedish and English. I did not search or read the terms of use, so which years are open to everyone is not checked.
providers.triageNote: Opened the English front page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. No search, no terms page.

providers.name: HisKi - Finnish parish register index, Genealogical Society of Finland
providers.what: A database from the Genealogical Society of Finland holding transcribed lists of christenings, marriages, burials and moves from Finnish parishes. The parish list is long and bilingual (Finnish and Swedish names), and also includes military, hospital, Orthodox, Ingrian and Finnish congregations abroad, with search pages by province. The English information page says not every parish is in the database because entry is unfinished, that the data are unchecked and contain errors, and that name standardisation is incomplete, so hits must be checked against the original books. It offers instructions and examples, and a list of updates. I did not run a search or check years per parish.
providers.triageNote: Opened the parish list and information page in the in-app browser on 2026-11-08. No search done. The Atlas row kansallisarkisto mentions HisKi inside the archive's name, but this database lives at the Society's own address.

providers.name: Suomen Sukututkimusseura (Genealogical Society of Finland)
providers.what: The Helsinki-based genealogical society, founded 1917, with a site in Finnish, Swedish and English. The page lists courses, annual genealogy days, a mentoring service, publications and a webshop, advice and a library. Its digital services include HisKi (parish register search), SukuHaku (a member service opened 2017 as a gateway to Finnish genealogical sources), a gravestone database, Henkikirjahaku (a search tool for Finnish population registers), an open discussion forum, and SukuTopoteekki. The page says some services are reserved for members. I did not open the individual databases.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. Member-only parts untested; no database search opened.

providers.name: Svenska tidningar - Swedish digitised newspapers, Kungliga biblioteket
providers.what: The Swedish National Library's service for digitised newspapers and magazines. The front page says it offers thousands of titles from 1645 to the present, with a search box, an alphabetical title list (0-9, A-Ö), search tips and a practical guide. It states that material younger than 100 years is protected, and that after a temporary restriction it is again possible to search the protected material remotely. The interface is in Swedish and results are shown in a partly new layout. I did not search, open a page image, or read the 'about the content' page, so the exact access rule for newer papers is unconfirmed.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08 (page text was about 115,000 characters; first 100,000 read). No search tested.

providers.name: Regionarkivet Västra Götaland / Göteborgs Stad (regional archive, Gothenburg)
providers.what: The archive of Västra Götaland Region and the City of Gothenburg. Its page says it keeps records useful for family research, such as certificates, patient records, social-service files, maps and drawings, and an association archive (Göteborgs föreningsarkiv) with material from popular movements. There is a section for searching digital collections, an e-service for private persons to order copies (staff review confidentiality first, and social-service records take longer), and pre-ordering of originals for the research room. The page gives no years for holdings. I did not open the digital collections, so what they contain is unchecked.
providers.triageNote: Read the unit page via WebFetch on 2026-11-08 (regionarkivet.se redirects here). Digital collections not opened.

providers.name: Nasjonalbiblioteket (National Library of Norway) - online library
providers.what: The National Library of Norway's site. The English page says everything is free and open to the public in general terms and has a login link, and links a separate page on access to the digital library, which I did not read, so the rules on which items are viewable from outside Norway or by year are unchecked. The search application itself loaded without text in the scripted view.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page (Norwegian and English) with WebFetch on 2026-11-08; the /search page rendered empty in the in-app browser. Access page not read.

providers.name: DIGAR - Digital Archive of the National Library of Estonia
providers.what: The Estonian National Library's digital archive. The English front page offers books, journals (to 2016), graphics and collections, with a detailed search that also covers articles, ephemera, manuscripts, maps, newspapers, photographs, posters, sheet music and sound and video recordings. It says newspapers date from 1821 and that journals from 2017 onward are in a separate DIGAR Estonian Articles portal. Files come in formats such as PDF, EPUB, TIFF and JPG. An 'only available' filter and lock marks suggest part of the material is restricted, and a login for National Library users exists. I did not search or open an item, so the rules on access are not confirmed.
providers.triageNote: Read the English front page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. No search done.

providers.name: Archives nationales de Luxembourg (ANLux) - genealogy and family research
providers.what: The Luxembourg national archives' page for family research lists civil registers from 1795 (births, marriages, deaths and ten-year tables of the two district courts), censuses 1806-1916, notarial minutes from 1588 (five Ancien Régime notaries viewable online), conscription tables 1798-1814, national militia registers 1815-1834, the 1766 Maria Theresa cadastre and hearth counts from 1541. Parish registers are said to be on Matricula Online rather than at ANLux. Anyone can use the collections, with a free reader card at the first visit; an online portal finds shelf marks, microfilms are ordered on site, and copies of acts can be asked for by post. Staff search for vague requests is charged. I did not open the online portal.
providers.triageNote: Read the genealogy page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08 (full text). Portal at archives.services-publics.lu and the digitised-documents page not opened.

providers.name: eluxemburgensia - digital collections of the Bibliothèque nationale du Luxembourg
providers.what: The national library of Luxembourg's digital platform. Its front page lists periodicals, books, manuscripts, posters and portraits, with a search box, a way to explore periodicals by date, staff picks and news. Some images sit on a separate site in three categories: literature, reference documents and other publications, and postcards. Pages on copyright and on works unavailable commercially are linked and probably set the access rules, but I did not read them, and the front page gives no year range. The text I read is in French. I did not search or open a newspaper page.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. No search or access page read.

providers.name: Schweizerisches Bundesarchiv (Swiss Federal Archives)
providers.what: The archive of the Swiss federal government's records, in Bern, with research possible online or on site. The English page describes an online access system to search holdings and order material for the reading room, and online databases: Federal Council minutes 1848-1975, Swiss film newsreels, and digitised official publications such as the Federal Gazette. It has topics and research-tip sections. I did not find a genealogy or family-research page among what I read, so its use for personal ancestry is not established here. Reading-room visits need orders and a workstation reservation in advance.
providers.triageNote: Read the English home page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. Search system and research tips not opened.

providers.name: Staatsarchiv des Kantons Zürich (Zurich cantonal archive)
providers.what: The cantonal archive of Zurich. Courses on family research and reading old handwriting are mentioned, and one was fully booked. The Genealogisch-Heraldische Gesellschaft Zürich is named as partner. The page does not name which series are online or give years, and the archive is closed on Mondays. I did not open the catalogue or a digitised item.
providers.triageNote: Read the archive page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. Catalogue and digitised series untested.

providers.name: Staatsarchiv St.Gallen - digital reading room
providers.what: The cantonal archive of St. Gallen. The reading room itself is open Wednesday to Friday with advance registration, and the page notes a closure in November 2026 for renovation. The page I read does not mention genealogy by name or give year ranges, though sections for private persons and visits are listed. I did not open the digital reading room.
providers.triageNote: Read the archive page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. Digital reading room not opened.

providers.name: Archivportal-D (German archives portal, Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek)
providers.what: The German national archives portal, a sub-portal of the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek. Its front page cites nearly 270 archives, over 170,000 holdings and over 36 million objects, and offers a search of archival objects, an advanced search and a directory of archives, filterable by federal state and archive type (state, municipal, church, business, media). It also hosts four thematic portals (right-wing violence, charters of the Counts Palatine, the Weimar Republic, restitution). Searching appears open; saved lists require a registered 'Meine DDB' account. I did not run a search, so the share of items with images is not checked.

providers.name: LAGIS Hessen - Landesgeschichtliches Informationssystem
providers.what: A regional-history information system run by the Hessisches Institut für Landesgeschichte, grouped into lexica, atlases and maps, views and images, themes, projects and sources. Pages for family research include Hessian biographies, the historical place lexicon, field names, Hessian birth, marriage and death registers and Hessian emigrants. The page says LAGIS is moving to lagis.hessen.de, with some modules still on the old interface during the transition. I did not open the individual databases, so years, parishes and how a search works are unchecked.

providers.name: Archivportal NRW (North Rhine-Westphalia archives portal)
providers.what: A portal for archives across North Rhine-Westphalia, covering the state archive, municipal, university, political, church, business and other archives. The front page cites more than 500 institutions, over 8,800 finding aids, over 5 million researchable items and over 1 million digitised items. It has a map of archives, a keyword search and a holdings-structure search, and help pages with video tutorials. It says most archival items can only be viewed on site in the reading rooms, while some archives offer digitised copies of a small part. The page does not mention civil registers or church books by name, so I cannot say whether such series are online.
providers.triageNote: Read the front page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. No search done.

providers.name: Deutsches Auswandererhaus Bremerhaven - family research stations
providers.what: The emigration museum's page on tracing emigrated ancestors during a visit. It says visitors use two external databases at the museum: Ancestry (historical records only, including passenger lists for ships arriving at US ports, Hamburg lists 1877-1914 and US censuses) and the Bremen Passenger Lists 1920-1939 held by the Bremen Chamber of Commerce archive, about 3,000 lists covering roughly 70 percent of voyages for 1907/08, 1913/14 and 1920-1939. Other Bremen lists were destroyed and post-1945 lists are restricted and held by the Bremen State Archives. Results cannot be emailed, but can be photographed, and the page gives no separate fee. I did not open the databases themselves.
providers.triageNote: Read the family-research page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. A web search suggested the separate Deutsche Auswanderer-Datenbank (Historisches Museum Bremerhaven) is a different project; I did not open its own site.

providers.name: Zeeuws Archief (Zeeland archives), Middelburg - Zeeuwen Gezocht
providers.what: The archive of the province of Zeeland. Its 'research it yourself' section leads to Zeeuwen Gezocht, which the page lists as covering birth, marriage, death, baptism and burial records, population registers, notarial deeds, court judgments, divorce and bankruptcy files, cadastral owners, mortgage and estate-tax records, military service, ship crews, emigrants and refugees, employees, pupils, patients and detainees, and images and coats of arms. Topic pages cover the transatlantic slave trade and Zeeland emigrants. There is an English version. The pages I read give no year ranges, search method or access costs, and I did not open the search.
providers.triageNote: Read the home page and the Zeeuwen Gezocht page with WebFetch on 2026-11-08. The search itself was not opened.

providers.name: Tiroler Landesarchiv - family research and online databases

providers.name: Wiener Stadt- und Landesarchiv (Vienna City and Provincial Archives)
providers.what: The Vienna city archive. Its page lists the WAIS archive information system, a person search (Personensuche), a library catalogue, links to Wien Geschichte Wiki and Wien Kulturgut, and research tips for persons, plans, photographs and films. providers.name: Archivo Histórico Nacional (AHN), Madrid — Spanish National Historical Archive
providers.what: The Ministry of Culture's own page for the national historical archive in Madrid. It names series such as the nobility titles and grandezas, Directorate-General of Security police files and information bulletins, the Cardenal Cisneros institute's student records, the Ensenada cadastre books (a project in progress) and records of the military orders including Calatrava and Santiago visitation books. Several of these are described as published on PARES, the national archives portal, which is the online route; the page itself says remote requests are made by email after registering with an ID copy. The reading room is stated to be free, with ID shown at the door and limited advance booking for out-of-town users. The page does not describe Inquisition records and does not say how much of each series is digitised, and I did not test PARES from here.
providers.triageNote: Opened the AHN home page on cultura.gob.es on 2026-11-08 (read via WebFetch). Did not open PARES (connection to pares.cultura.gob.es timed out/refused from this machine), so which series have images online is not tested.

providers.name: Archivo General de la Administración (AGA), Alcalá de Henares
providers.what: State archive of the Spanish administration at Alcalá de Henares, run by the Ministry of Culture. The page lists purge (depuración) files, censorship files, prison documentation, records of the Consejo Supremo de Justicia Militar, the Junta para Ampliación de Estudios, Madrid provincial finance (cadastre) records and the Servicio Social de la Mujer. It points to a databases section, to PARES (where the purge series for archivists and librarians is described) and to a basic guide to sources. Consultation is in the reading room, free, with ID and an online appointment made between three weeks and 48 hours ahead. The page does not say how much is digitised, so I have not claimed any images online.

providers.name: Archivo General de Indias (AGI), Sevilla
providers.what: The Ministry of Culture's page for the archive of the Spanish empire's Atlantic and Pacific administration, housed in two buildings in Seville (the Lonja and the Cilla). The page lists a holdings section with a classification scheme, a library, and says the Audiencia de Filipinas records (162 legajos) are published with images and descriptions on PARES. It offers consultation in the reading room by appointment, user registration, remote information requests and reprographic services. The page does not itself mention passenger registers and gives no genealogical guide, so what a family historian will find there has to be looked up in PARES. A notice about building works affecting consultation of originals was on the page and may be out of date.

providers.name: Archivo General de Simancas (AGS)
providers.what: The Ministry of Culture's page for the archive of the Crown of Castile's central councils at Simancas, near Valladolid. Series named on the page include the Consejo de Guerra for the reigns of Charles I and Philip II, the Registro General del Sello (1454-1501), the Patronato Real and parts of the Secretaría de Guerra, and the Catastro del Marqués de la Ensenada, which is said to be online through PARES. Some series were withdrawn from in-person consultation in 2016 and have to be consulted on PARES. The researchers' room has stated hours, document requests close at 14:00, and an archive of maps and drawings (Imago Hispaniae) has its own section. I did not open the PARES records or the researcher's guide.

providers.name: Archivo de la Corona de Aragón (ACA), Barcelona
providers.what: State archive in the Palacio de los Virreyes in Barcelona, founded in 1318 and holding the royal chancery registers as its core. The page highlights medieval documents (the Llibre del Repartiment de València, the Liber feudorum maior), a fund of the Servicio de Defensa del Patrimonio Artístico Nacional (1938-1960), and 125 registers of Alfonso V published on PARES. It lists a databases section and a Censo-Guía link, appointments for the reading room, reproduction and self-copying. The page does not mention genealogical series and I did not open its databases, so it is mainly a source for the medieval and early-modern Crown of Aragon, not for parish-level family research.
providers.triageNote: Opened the ACA home page on 2026-11-08. Databases and PARES not opened.

providers.name: Centro Documental de la Memoria Histórica (CDMH), Salamanca
providers.what: Spanish state archive in Salamanca for the Civil War and the Francoist repression, run by the Ministry of Culture. Its page lists person-level online databases: Republican military personnel of sub-officer rank or above and members of the public-order forces and Carabineros, missing Republican army personnel, and Spaniards deported to Nazi camps in 1940-1945 (more than 8,000 records). It also links the ministry's portal of Civil War and Francoist victims. The centre offers in-person consultation, searches and certificates, reproduction and a quick guide to searching. I did not open the databases themselves, so I have not tested the search fields or whether images are attached.
providers.triageNote: Opened the CDMH home page on 2026-11-08; the three database names and the 8,000-record figure come from that page. Did not open the databases.

providers.name: Archivo de la Real Chancillería de Valladolid (ARCV)
providers.what: Ministry of Culture archive of the Real Audiencia y Chancillería de Valladolid (1371-1834), the highest royal court for Castile north of the Tagus, plus its successor the Audiencia Territorial (1834-1988) and other court records still being transferred. I read the home page and the introduction to the holdings only, and did not open the classification table or PARES.

providers.name: Artxibo — Registros sacramentales (Basque Historical Archive, sacramental records) / Sacramental Records of the Basque Country
providers.what: A page of the Basque Government's historical archive describing its online index of Catholic parish books from the dioceses of Bilbao, San Sebastián and Vitoria. providers.name: Archivio Storico Diocesano Reggio Calabria-Bova
providers.what: Archive of the archdiocese of Reggio Calabria-Bova. providers.what: Historical archive of the diocese of Verona, at via del Seminario in Verona.
